title: Challengers Approach: Third Party App Stores Arrive to Google Play
content:
If you are an Android user, you may have noticed it already: Google has begun allowing rival, third-party app stores to be distributed through the Google Play Store. And if you are a developer, you may have noticed new options for billing and distributing your apps. 

For years, Epic Games, maker of games such as Fortnite, has been suing Google, alleging violations of antitrust law. Specifically at issue were Google's restrictions on the distribution of alternate app stores through the Play Store, restrictions on app developers who have little practical choice but to distribute their apps through the Play Store, and Google’s rules governing in-app payments and the fees associated with them. 

Epic’s challenge ultimately resulted in a court order requiring significant changes to Google’s practices. Among other changes, rival, third-party Android app stores are now allowed to access the Play Store’s catalog and to be distributed through the Google Play Store. Developers also have greater freedom to direct users to alternative payment and distribution options.

title: A Long Road to Justice in the Central African Republic
content:
In November 2013, I went to Bangui and met Michel Djotodia, then the Central African Republic’s self-proclaimed interim president. He had taken over the country as the head of a rebel coalition called the Seleka. He received me in a run-down military camp on a hill overlooking the capital, in a darkened office watched over by security cameras and guarded by ragtag soldiers.

I had the uncomfortable task of handing the “president” our latest report. By then, we had documented the killing of civilians and the destruction of more than 1,000 homes by Seleka forces. Djotodia was courteous, engaged, but mostly deflected and sought to distance himself and his forces from many of the crimes we had documented, blaming abuses on criminals.

What struck me then was not simply the denial. It was the chaos of the military camp, the lawlessness in the country, the collapse of the justice system and the complete absence of accountability.

But justice is finally catching up.

title: Why journalism grants can put freelancers at a disadvantage
content:
When Romanian investigative journalist Andrei Petre began researching secrecy surrounding European data centres in 2025, he had documents, a story idea and, eventually, an interested publisher.

What he didn’t have was funding.

Petre applied for a journalism grant but was rejected because his preliminary research was judged insufficient. He continued researching and applied again.

While he waited, another investigative team published a story based on one of the key public documents he had found. His prospective publishing partner was subsequently approached to join that investigation instead. Petre did not get the grant.

His experience illustrated a dilemma at the heart of “The Uneven Split”, a panel debate at IJ4EU’s 2026 UNCOVERED Conference in Budapest: freelancers may need to undertake substantial unpaid reporting to secure funding, but waiting for that funding can mean losing a fast-moving story.

“You cannot really cover stuff that other people are already covering because you have to wait a lot until you get a grant,” Petre said.

title: Hallitus esittää uutta lakia Finnfundista
content:
Hallitus antaa eduskunnalle esityksen vaikuttavuussijoittaja ja kehitysrahoittaja Finnfundin uudesta laista, jonka on määrä korvata lähes 50 vuotta vanhaa sääntelyä. Uudistuksella tehostetaan yrityksille kehitysrahoitusta kanavoivan Finnpartnership-ohjelman hallinnointia ja parannetaan yrityksille tarjottavia palveluja.

Lainsäädännön uudistuksen tavoitteena on vahvistaa suomalaisten yritysten mahdollisuuksia osallistua kansainväliseen kehitysyhteistyöhön, parantaa yrityksille tarjottavia kehitysrahoituksen palveluja sekä selkeyttää julkisten hallintotehtävien hoitamista. Finnfund-konserniin esitetään perustettavaksi tytäryhtiö, jolle siirrettäisiin Finnpartnership-ohjelman hallinnointiin liittyviä julkisia hallintotehtäviä.

title: U.K. Sanctions Four Georgians Over Occupied Ukraine Visit
content:
The U.K. has sanctioned four Georgians—including the brother-in-law of Tbilisi’s mayor—for “legitimising Russia’s occupation of Ukrainian territory” after they met with the head of a Russian-backed separatist republic.

The designations are part of a broader British sanctions package announced in response to intensifying Russian drone strikes against Ukraine in September. According to a press release Thursday, the wider measures target Russia’s “shadow fleet,” Kremlin propagandists, and individuals allegedly involved in human rights abuses against Ukrainian civilians. 

“The U.K. will not flinch in our support for Ukraine,” said Europe Minister Lord Wood of Anfield.

The U.K. sanctions notice states the four men “joined a delegation of Georgian politicians who met with the head of the so-called Donetsk People’s Republic, and subsequently publicised the visit.” All four now face U.K. asset freezes and travel bans.

The sanctioned delegates include political commentator Paata Abuladze, Mamuka Pipia, leader of the minor Solidarity for Peace party, party member Giorgi Iremadze, and Nikoloz Mzhavanadze, founder of a Georgian Russian-language TV channel.

title: LEGO Lets You Build Gaudí’s Sagrada Família in Its Largest Set Ever
content: When work on the Sagrada Família first began in 1882, the original architect could hardly have imagined that, 144 years later, the ambitious undertaking would still be underway. Yet here we are. Famously, the Catalan architect Antoni Gaudí (1852–1926) spent the last four decades of his life designing and building the Gothic-inspired basilica in Barcelona. Then came the Spanish Civil War (1936–1939), which destroyed many of his architectural plans, leaving successive generations of architects to piece together Gaudí’s vision and move the project forward. At long last, earlier this year, builders completed the central Tower of Jesus Christ, which stands 566 feet high, making the Sagrada Família the tallest church in the world.

title: Presidentti Stubb: Tänään alkoi uusi aikakausi Suomen ilmavoimille
content:
Tasavallan presidentti, Puolustusvoimain ylipäällikkö Alexander Stubb osallistui Ilmavoimien F-35-vastaanottotilaisuuteen Rovaniemellä torstaina 1. lokakuuta 2026.

Ensimmäiset kaksi F-35-hävittäjää saapuivat Yhdysvalloista Lapin lennostoon Rovaniemelle 18. syyskuuta. Torstain vastaanottotilaisuudessa Ilmavoimat esitteli uudet F-35-hävittäjänsä seremoniallisin menoin.

Presidentti Stubb kiitti puheessaan Suomen ja Yhdysvaltain erinomaista yhteistyötä F-35-hävittäjähankinnassa. Presidentin mukaan kyseessä on historiallinen hetki, kun vuosien valmistelutyön jälkeen F-35-kalusto otetaan käyttöön Suomessa.

F-35-järjestelmällä on merkittävä vaikutus Suomen puolustuskykyyn ja Ilmavoimien taistelukykyyn. Ne tuovat mukanaan kokonaan uuden sukupolven järjestelmät, jotka tuottavat tietoa koko puolustusjärjestelmän käyttöön.

title: Four Kids in One Faith-Healing Family Died. Authorities Could Do Nothing.
content:
Emma Joyce was sick and vomiting for days until she stopped breathing in her parents’ arms, in a small gray farmhouse in rural Idaho. It was August 2009, and she was 3 years old.

The following summer, Emma Joyce’s little sister got sick. Ava Joan wouldn’t eat or drink anything but a few grapes and some Sprite in a sippy cup. She was breathing hard and fast. And when she vomited, it came out black, the hallmark of internal bleeding. She died in her mother’s arms in July 2010 from a complication of untreated diabetes.

Less than two years later, the girls’ toddler brother died from the same complication of untreated diabetes that killed Ava Joan.

And nine years after that, another sibling died: a 4-year-old boy who’d suffered for weeks with similar symptoms.

The parents told officers that they hadn’t taken the four children who died to the doctor because of their religion, the Followers of Christ, which considers the use of modern medicine a sinful lapse of faith in God. And Idaho exempts parents from faith-healing sects like the Followers from the legal duty to give their children lifesaving medical care.

title: I oktober kan professionella organisationer söka bidrag
content:
Är ni en professionell organisation som verkar på svenska i Finland? Är ert verksamhetsområde civilsamhälle eller professionell konst? Då kan ni lämna in en ansökan i oktober.

Bidraget riktar sig till organisationer med yrkesmässig verksamhet, vilket bland annat innebär att organisationen ska ha minst en person med tillsvidareanställning på minst 50 procent. Dessutom kräver vi att de sökande uppfyller vissa kriterier som vi förklarar noggrannare i vår sökandeinfo.

Lokala föreningar och organisationer som huvudsakligen driver sin verksamhet på frivillig basis kan inte söka det här bidraget. De kan som tidigare söka bidrag i november.

Bidraget är både för allmän verksamhet och för högst två specialprojekt. De organisationer som söker bidrag enbart för specialprojekt ska lämna in en ansökan i november.

Det är möjligt att söka bidraget för ett, två eller tre år.

Ansökningstiden är den 1-15 oktober och alla får besked redan i december. Bidragen kan lyftas från och med början av januari.

Om din organisation i oktober söker bidraget för professionella organisationer ersätter det novemberansökan till Kulturfonden. Din organisation kan alltså inte söka bidrag i både oktober och november.

title: Social media hasn’t killed personal style, it’s killed how we communicate it
content:
This summer, social media was filled with posts declaring that almost anything was “kinda chic”. Repeating outfits was kinda chic. Being overdressed was kinda chic. Doing something unfashionable could, apparently, also be kinda chic.

But can you remember the content of many individual “kinda chic” posts now? Probably not. What is much easier to remember is the format itself: the language, the rhythm, the way an ordinary behaviour or object was reframed as evidence of taste.

That distinction tells us something important about fashion online. We often worry that social media is making everyone dress the same, but perhaps the greater similarity lies in how we communicate being fashionable.

Social media does not only circulate products and trends, it circulates recognisable ways of presenting them. A city street or a zebra crossing becomes the setting for an outfit photograph. Coffee appears alongside carefully placed handbags. Hotels, holidays and fashion events become backdrops. Accessories are photographed in close-up, bodies adopt familiar poses and captions perform effortlessness even when the accompanying image is highly composed.

title: Emeritaprofessori Marjatta Hietala kuvaa muistelmissaan matkaansa tiedemaailman huipulle sekä tutkijanaisena kohtaamaansa vähättelyä
content:
Yleisen historian emeritaprofessori Marjatta Hietalan muistelmateos Karjalaisella sinnikkyydellä kertoo karjalaisten evakkojen tyttären polusta aina historiantutkijoiden maailmanjärjestön presidentiksi. Tietä muille naisille raivannut Hietala kuvaa moninaisten uravaiheidensa lisäksi kohtaamaansa epäoikeudenmukaisuutta miesvaltaisessa tiedemaailmassa.

Miten sukutilansa menettäneiden karjalaisten evakkojen tyttärestä tulee yleisen historian professori ja historiantutkijoiden maailmanjärjestön ensimmäinen naispresidentti? Tarvitaan ainakin ahkeruutta ja periksiantamattomuutta, perheen ja ystävien tukea sekä ripaus onnea.

Sotavuonna 1943 syntynyt Marjatta Hietala kertoo Karjalaisella sinnikkyydellä -muistelmissaan vaiherikkaasta matkastaan Kymenlaaksossa vietetystä lapsuudesta kansainvälisen tutkijayhteisön arvostetuksi jäseneksi. Pitkän uransa aikana hän ehti työskennellä tutkijana ja opettajana Helsingin, Joensuun ja Tampereen yliopistojen lisäksi muun muassa Berliinissä, Lontoossa, Minnesotassa, New Yorkissa ja Prahassa. Moninaisia olivat tutkimusaiheetkin ulottuen nationalismista kaupungistumiseen ja rotuhygieniasta innovaatioihin.

title: War, power games and impunity. I watched the farce that is the UN general assembly: what a tragedy, what a mess | Nesrine Malik
content:
Ukraine, Iran, Palestine and Sudan: it has so many problems to confront and fails to do so. Seen up close, it is a study in stasis and decline

UN general assembly meetings are not usually riveting occasions. But this year’s encapsulated a world in flux and crisis, an international law and organisation structure that is falling apart, and a humanitarian order machine running hot. What unfolded was less a gathering for resolution and resolve than a display of showboating, frustration and fractiousness.

content:
Euroopan komissio jatkaa kansainvälisen sopimuksen tavoittelua tekoälysääntelylle Yhdysvaltain vastustuksesta huolimatta, sanoi EU:n digikomissaari Henna Virkkunen tiistaina Politico-lehden mukaan.

"Yhdysvallat on hyvin julkisesti sanonut, ettei se halua kansainvälistä sääntelyä, koska se voisi haitata innovaatiota", Virkkunen sanoi Brysselissä.

Yhdysvaltain presidentti Donald Trump on sivuuttanut huolet tekoälyn eksistentiaalisista riskeistä "huijauksena" ja julistanut vastustavansa globaalia sääntelyä. Vaatimukset hidastaa teknologista kehitystä ja vahvistaa kansainvälistä hallintoa ovat kasvaneet, kun tekoälyagenttien on raportoitu riistäytyvän käsistä. Tiistaina OpenAI kertoi Wall Street Journalin mukaan, ettei se julkaise uusinta malliaan turvallisuushuolten vuoksi. title: Cops Can Bypass iPhone’s Automatic Reboot to Get Into Locked Phones, Leaked Video Claims
content:
A company that makes phone hacking devices claims to have developed a solution that freezes iPhones in a state that lets cops more easily access sensitive data inside them, according to a video obtained by 404 Media.  

This is the latest salvo in the never-ending battle between Apple and companies that help cops — sometimes those in authoritarian countries — break into iPhones.

In November 2024, 404 Media revealed Apple quietly introduced a new feature in iOS that automatically reboots an iPhone that has not been unlocked for 72 hours. The idea behind this so-called “inactivity reboot” is to revert the phone to a state that makes it harder for police to break into the device, and thus extract sensitive data from it with forensics technology. 

At the time of Apple’s change, law enforcement agents expressed concern about this new feature, given that oftentimes they can’t immediately try to break into iPhones that have been seized. That could be because police are still waiting for a court authorization to do so, or there is simply a backlog of devices to unlock, for example.

title: The Real Existential Risk Is AI CEOs Avoiding Oversight: "Alternative Nobel" Winner Timnit Gebru
content:
We speak to the prominent AI researcher and leading critic of the AI industry, Timnit Gebru, who was recently awarded a 2026 Right Livelihood Award for her work investigating the harms and hype behind the global buildup of artificial intelligence.

“Instead of discussing faulty, unreliable systems,” Gebru says tech leaders like SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk, OpenAI’s Sam Altman and Anthropic’s Dario Amodei are “marketing their systems as all-knowing, superpowerful, superintelligent,” and lobbying for “self-policing and self-regulation” to avoid being held “liable through existing laws.” Gebru expresses skepticism over increasingly widespread claims that AI algorithms pose an existential risk to humanity, warning that such claims are overblown and that “what is actually happening is regulatory capture.”

title: Court Agrees with EFF: Utah’s VPN Law Demands a Technical Impossibility
content:
When state lawmakers attempt to rewrite how the internet works, users rely on courts to recognize that laws can’t make technical impossibilities a reality. That’s why we were happy to see that a court has blocked Utah’s attempt to outlaw the privacy protections of Virtual Private Networks (VPNs). 

In a win for digital rights, a federal judge has issued a preliminary injunction blocking Utah’s SB 73, the state’s draconian anti-VPN age verification law. The decision comes as EFF submitted our comments to the Utah Department of Commerce, detailing how forcing platforms to detect and block privacy-preserving tools undermines user privacy and security worldwide while demanding the impossible.  

Signed into law earlier this year, SB 73 attempted to regulate adult websites by requiring them to block VPN users or to identify the physical location of visitors using them or similar tools that mask their network traffic. It even went so far as to prohibit websites from offering instructions on how to use a VPN to bypass these checks. This made Utah, to EFF’s knowledge, the first state in the nation to target the use of VPNs to avoid legally mandated age-verification gates.

title: Monthly Report – September 2026: Human Rights Situation in Iran
content:
Executions

During September, at least 59 prisoners, including four women, one juvenile offender, and four Afghan nationals, were executed by hanging in prisons across Iran.

Of those executed, 29 had been sentenced to death on murder charges, 26 on drug-related charges, and one on a charge of rape.

In addition, three individuals were executed on political and security-related charges: Ali Hemmati and Majid Nikandish were executed in Mashhad in connection with the nationwide protests of January 2026, while Hossein Pedaran was executed on charges of espionage and intelligence cooperation with Israel.

During the same month, Iran’s judicial authorities also issued 23 death sentences. Three of those sentenced to death are women, including Mahboubeh Shabani, who was sentenced to death in connection with the January 2026 protests.

Also during the month, Iran’s Supreme Court upheld ten death sentences.

title: Mauritius Rights Body Calls for Marriage Equality
content:
The National Human Rights Commission in Mauritius earlier this year urged the government to legally recognize same-sex marriages, stating that the refusal to recognize such unions is discriminatory and lacks justification under domestic law.

The Commission’s recommendation comes after two same-sex couples filed complaints alleging that the country’s civil status office’s refusal to register their marriage is prejudicial to them. In their complaints and in public testimony before the Commission, same-sex couples and lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender (LGBT) individuals testified about the burdens they face with regard to taxation, inheritance, immigration, medical decision-making, family formation, and social acceptance in the absence of partnership recognition.

The Commission agreed that any exclusion of same-sex couples from marriage could amount to discrimination and recommended the formation of a government committee to eliminate discrimination in partnership recognition and marriage.

title: Lohjan Pyhän Laurin kirkon kukkiva kastepuu siunataan käyttöön
content:
Lohjan seurakunta saa pääkirkkoonsa kastepuun Mikkelinpäivänä eli ensi sunnuntaina 4. lokakuuta. Kanta-Lohjan alueneuvosto tilasi vuoden vaihteessa kastepuun suunnittelun lohjalaiselta taiteilijalta Annastiina Mäkitalolta, joka on suunnitellut useita julkisia taideteoksia niin Lohjalle kuin muualle Suomeen.

Kastepuu on valmistettu metallista ja sen on valmistanut metalliseppä Mika Vuori. Puu puhkeaa kukkaan jokaisen kastetun myötä, kun jokaiselle kiinnitetään oma kukka. Kynttilänpäivänä helmikuussa perheet voivat noutaa oman lapsensa kukan itselleen kotiin kasteen muistoksi.

Annastiina Mäkitalo toivoo, että Kastepuu otetaan hyvin vastaan ja se palvelee lohjalaisia perheitä vuosisatojen ajan.

- Tavoitteeni oli luoda teos, joka on kaunis ja luonteva osa kulttuurihistoriallisesti erittäin arvokasta ja hyvin säilynyttä kirkkoympäristöä. Kastepuun värimaailma ja muotokieli nousee kirkon interiööristä, Mäkitalo kertoo.

Mäkitalo toivoo, että Kastepuusta tulisi lohjalaisille rakas symboli uuden elämän ihmeelle.

title: Uusi kumppanuussopimus vahvistamaan EU:n yhteistyötä Afrikan, Karibian ja Tyynenmeren maiden kanssa
content:
Valtioneuvosto esittää, että eduskunta hyväksyisi Euroopan unionin ja sen jäsenvaltioiden sekä Afrikan, Karibian ja Tyynenmeren valtioiden järjestön jäsenten välisen kumppanuussopimuksen eli niin kutsutun Samoan sopimuksen.

Kyseessä on aiemman, samoja alueita koskeneen sopimuksen tapaan laaja yhteistyösopimus, joka sisältää kaikkia osapuolia koskevan yleisosan sekä kolme alueellista pöytäkirjaa. Sopimus kattaa laajan kirjon yhteistyöalueita, kuten demokratian ja ihmisoikeudet, kestävän talouskasvun ja -kehityksen, ilmastokysymykset, inhimillisen ja sosiaalisen kehityksen, rauhan ja turvallisuuden sekä muuttoliikkeen ja liikkuvuuden.

Sopimuksella luodaan puitteet EU:n ja AKT-maiden vuoropuhelulle sekä oikeudelliset puitteet muun muassa Euroopan investointipankin (EIP) toiminnalle kaikissa AKT-maissa.

Sopimus on jatkoa Cotonoun sopimukselle, joka päättyi vuonna 2020. Uusi sopimus allekirjoitettiin Samoalla marraskuussa 2023, minkä vuoksi siitä käytetään usein nimitystä Samoan sopimus. Valtioneuvoston tuore esitys koskee Samoan sopimuksen kansallista voimaansaattamista.

title: Ex-Hungarian Minister Detained in $53 Million Graft Probe
content:
Black-masked law enforcement officers escorted Balázs Hankó, a former Hungarian culture minister, into a district court on Thursday, where a judge ordered him held in pretrial detention over allegations that he masterminded the widespread misappropriation of state funds to benefit the party of former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán.

Hankó was taken into custody after Hungary's Parliament voted 139 to 0 on Monday to strip his legislative immunity. Before surrendering to prosecutors later that evening, he spent the day inside the Parliament building surrounded by his family, framing his pending arrest as political persecution.

"My conscience is clear; this is a political show trial," Hankó said in a video broadcast live on Orbán’s Facebook page before walking out alongside relatives and lawmakers from Fidesz, Orbán's right-wing party, which is now in opposition.

title: Euroopan turvallisuus esillä presidentti Stubbin valtiovierailulla Luxemburgissa
content:
Tasavallan presidentti Alexander Stubb ja hänen puolisonsa Suzanne Innes-Stubb tekivät valtiovierailun Luxemburgiin 29.–30. syyskuuta 2026 suurherttua Guillaumen ja suurherttuatar Stéphanien kutsusta.

Vierailulla olivat esillä Suomen ja Luxemburgin kahdenväliset suhteet ja kaupallistaloudellinen yhteistyö, globaalihaasteet, kokonaisturvallisuus ja Euroopan vahvistaminen sekä Venäjän laiton hyökkäyssota Ukrainassa. 

Presidentti Stubb tapasi edustajainhuoneen puhemies Claude Wiselerin, pääministeri Luc Friedenin sekä varapääministeri ja ulkoministeri Xavier Bettelin.

Iltapäivällä presidenttipari ja suurherttuapari tapasivat Luxemburgin pormestari Lydie Polferin kaupungintalolla. 

Presidentti Stubb vieraili Euroopan investointipankissa ja Euroopan unionin tuomioistuimessa Kirchbergissä.

Päivän päätti suurherttuaparin isännöimä illallinen valtiovierailun kunniaksi.

title: Gears of War: E-Day review – an alien invasion shouldn’t be this boring
content:
Xbox, PC (version tested); The Coalition/Xbox Game Studios
E-Day boasts the best combat in 20 years of Gears games – but everything surrounding it is disappointing

Every Gears of War game released in the last 20 years has made reverent reference to Emergence Day, when alien creatures emerged from the earth, single-minded in their savagery. In E-Day, you’re there to witness it: the police lights, flipped cars, ground tremors, civilians running, aliens pouring out of fissures in the earth and ripping faces off. You’re at ground zero in a squad of four soldiers called Gears – Marcus Fenix, the leader; Dom, who wants to retire; Lucas, a green cadet with a buzzcut; and the dishonourably discharged Mags. Only this dysfunctional quartet can turn the tide. With guns. Lots of ’em.

Instead of answering questions raised by the ending of 2019’s Gears 5, we’re back to the start to find out why Marcus has a scar on his lip and why these soldiers started strapping chainsaws on to their assault rifles. Anything that was left to the imagination is here, for you to point at and say: “I understood that reference. This is a thing that I have seen.”

title: One in three Ukrainian civilians estimated to meet the criteria for PTSD or complex PTSD – new study
content:
Resilience is a word frequently used to describe the way Ukrainian society has responded to the war with Russia. It’s a term that can inspire sympathy and mobilise support. But it also risks overshadowing effects of war that require both domestic and international attention to enable Ukraine to withstand Russia’s invasion and manage long-term recovery.

The protracted conflict that started with Russia’s annexation of Crimea in 2014, continued with the war in Donbas and escalated into Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022 has recently reached a new level of intensity through concerted Russian attacks on civilian targets. As a result, the effects of war at the level of individuals, communities and society at large are becoming ever more apparent.

Trauma is an unavoidable effect of war. Measuring the psychological effects of trauma in countries following war and conflict can be difficult. Obtaining a reliable picture of the situation in Ukraine – where, after four and a half years, there is no end to the conflict in sight – has proved even more challenging.

title: Jo lähes 10 000 oirearviota tehty Pohjois-Savossa, joka viides saa avun itsehoito-ohjeista
content:
Pohjoissavolaiset ovat tehneet Omaolo-palvelussa jo lähes 10 000 digitaalista oirearviota. Noin joka viides käyttäjä saa oirearvion perusteella itsehoito-ohjeet, ja yli 1 100 asiakasta on ohjautunut suoraan terveydenhuollon ammattilaiselle.

Pohjoissavolaisille on avattu nyt seitsemän uutta digitaalista oirearviota. Oirearvion voi tehdä esimerkiksi silmätulehduksesta, yskästä tai kurkkukivusta.

Pohjois-Savon hyvinvointialue otti käyttöön ensimmäiset oirearviot kesäkuussa 2024. Uusia oirearvioita on avattu vaiheittain ja samalla palvelun suosio on kasvanut. Tänä vuonna oirearvioita on tehty jo noin 4 700.

Suosituimpia oirearvioita ovat tänä vuonna olleet virtsatietulehdus, seksitauti ja hengitystietulehdus.

- Asukas voi tehdä oirearvion Omaolo-palvelussa milloin tahansa. Vastausten perusteella hän saa lääketieteelliseen tietoon perustuvan arvion hoidon tarpeesta sekä ohjeet siihen, miten tilanteessa kannattaa toimia, kehittämisasiantuntija Merja Jumpponen kertoo.

Oirearvio auttaa tunnistamaan, voiko oiretta hoitaa itse vai tarvitaanko ammattilaisen arviota.

title: Viivästyneet diagnoosit heikentävät naisten elämänlaatua
content:
Naisten terveyteen liittyvät ongelmat jäävät Suomen Gynekologiset Syöpäpotilaat -yhdistyksen mukaan liian usein vähälle huomiolle. Gynekologisissa syövissä oireiden tunnistamatta jääminen tai niiden vähättely voi viivästyttää diagnoosia ja hoidon aloittamista.

"Kyselystä toiseen potilaiden kokemuksissa korostuu se, että heidän oireisiinsa ei ole suhtauduttu riittävällä vakavuudella. Näin ei saisi olla, sillä virheelliset ja viivästyneet diagnoosit voivat johtaa pahimmillaan ennenaikaiseen kuolemaan", yhdistyksen puheenjohtaja Taru Salovaara sanoo yhdistyksen tiedotteessa.

Hallitus valmistelee parhaillaan naisten terveyden strategiaa. Sen tavoitteena on koota yhteen tietoa naisten terveydestä sekä löytää keinoja terveyden, työkyvyn ja hyvinvoinnin edistämiseen. Strategian on määrä valmistua tämän hallituskauden aikana.

"Olisi todella tärkeää, että naisten terveyden strategiassa huomioitaisiin myös gynekologiset syövät. Gynekologiset syövät voivat heikentää työkykyä, sillä syöpähoidoista aiheutuu monenlaisia haittoja, jotka voivat jäädä jopa pysyviksi", yhdistyksen varapuheenjohtaja Eva-Maria Strömsholm painottaa.

title: Happy Opt Out October! Let’s Find Real Alternatives to the Tech Giants
content:
Over the years, the major tech companies have found all sorts of ways to embed themselves into our lives. We often use their software, their AI tools, their social media, and their operating systems by default without even thinking about potential alternatives. It’s time to rethink that relationship. 

Last year, we created Opt Out October to help remind ourselves of the variety of ways we can take back control of our data through small steps inside apps, operating systems, and other various forms. This year, we highlight the idea that sometimes the best way to control your data is to leave a platform, app, or operating system altogether. 

To do so, we’ve created a hub of resources sharing ways to find new software that isn’t made by the tech giants, take advantage of the growing universe of new social media options, install a whole new operating system, and better control how various popular tools and software use your data for AI training.

content:

title: US: Nebraskans Losing Coverage as Medicaid Changes
content:
(Washington, DC) – Nebraska’s efforts to implement new, federally mandated work requirements for Medicaid underscore fears that millions of people will experience avoidable barriers to healthcare coverage, Human Rights Watch, Oxfam America, and Nebraska Appleseed said today.

On May 1, 2026, Nebraska became the first state to implement work requirements for Medicaid, the public health insurance program for people with low- or no-income, as part of public spending cuts mandated by the Trump administration’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA), which also extended and deepened tax cuts that overwhelmingly benefit high-income households and corporations. These new rules will require most adults without dependents to document at least 80 hours per month of work, education, or other approved activities to maintain Medicaid coverage. States must implement the requirements by January 1, 2027, though they may do so sooner, as Nebraska has.

title: Hallitus esittää lakia kehityspoliittisista sijoituksista
content:
Valtioneuvosto on antanut eduskunnalle hallituksen esityksen laiksi kehityspoliittisista sijoituksista. Esitys loisi selkeän säädösperustan Suomen kehityspoliittiselle sijoitustoiminnalle ja määrittelisi toiminnan tavoitteet, periaatteet ja menettelytavat.

Esitys toteuttaa hallitusohjelman tavoitetta vahvistaa yksityisen sektorin roolia kehityspolitiikassa ja lisätä yksityisen pääoman kohdistumista kestävää kehitystä edistäviin investointeihin kehittyvissä maissa. Esitys on yksi Kansainvälisten taloussuhteiden ja kehitysyhteistyön selonteon (2024) toimenpiteistä näiden tavoitteiden edistämiseksi.

"Kestävän kehityksen rahoitustarpeet ovat huomattavasti suuremmat kuin julkisesti käytettävissä olevat varat. Siksi tarvitsemme monipuolisesti keinoja saada yksityistä pääomaa mukaan rahoittamaan investointeja, yritystoimintaa ja työpaikkojen syntymistä kehittyvissä maissa", sanoo ulkomaankauppa- ja kehitysministeri Ville Tavio.

title: Raids Across Europe Target Far-Right Network Accused of Producing Neo-Nazi Music
content:
Authorities in five European countries carried out coordinated searches on Wednesday as part of an investigation into a suspected far-right criminal organization accused of producing and selling sound recordings containing music that incited hatred and spread National Socialist, antisemitic, racist and dehumanizing ideology.

The Rostock Public Prosecutor’s Office and the Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania State Office of Criminal Investigation said four suspects, aged 55, 52, 48 and 43, are being investigated for alleged membership in a criminal organization. One of them is also suspected of acting as its ringleader. The searches were carried out under warrants issued by an investigating judge at the Rostock Local Court.

Investigators suspect the four formed a permanent association no later than 2020 and worked together in an organized division of labor to produce and sell recordings containing hate-inciting music.

title: Could a former IDF chief break Benjamin Netanyahu’s grip on power in Israel?
content:
Israel is heading to the polls on October 27 and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is facing perhaps the toughest political battle of his career.

He’s facing fresh allegations that he was warned of a major Hamas plot ahead of the October 7 attacks.

Professor of Israel Studies Dov Waxman tells The Conversation Weekly although Netanyahu denies it, many hold him personally responsible for the attacks because he didn’t take those warnings seriously.

Netanyahu has consistently deflected any kind of blame and has basically pointed the finger at the Israeli army, at the Israeli military. This is something that I think many Israelis are really appalled by: his refusal to take any sort of personal responsibility.

title: Puolen miljoonan asukkaan Pohjois-Norja ottaa oululaisen Medanets-mobiiliratkaisun käyttöön alueellisella sopimuksella
content:
Oululainen terveysteknologiayhtiö Medanets on solminut alueellisen sopimuksen Pohjois-Norjan erikoissairaanhoidosta vastaavan terveysviranomaisen Helse Nordin kanssa. Sopimus mahdollistaa Medanetsin mobiiliratkaisujen käytön koko Pohjois-Norjan alueella aina Huippuvuorille saakka. Alue kattaa noin 45 prosenttia Norjan pinta-alasta ja palvelee lähes puolta miljoonaa asukasta.

Medanetsin ratkaisu integroituu alueella käytössä oleviin järjestelmiin ja täydentää niitä mobiileilla työnkuluilla. Ratkaisun avulla terveydenhuollon ammattilaiset voivat tarkastella ajantasaista potilastietoa ja kirjata tietoja mobiilisti siellä, missä hoitotyö tapahtuu: potilaan vierellä.

Helse Nord vastaa erikoissairaanhoidosta Nordlandin, Tromssan ja Finnmarkin alueilla sekä Huippuvuorilla. Kyseessä on yksi Euroopan maantieteellisesti vaativimmista terveydenhuollon toimintaympäristöistä, jossa pitkät välimatkat, hajautettu sairaalaverkko ja arktiset olosuhteet asettavat erityisiä vaatimuksia tiedonkululle ja hoitotyön sujuvuudelle. Yksi alueen keskeisistä sairaaloista on Tromssassa sijaitseva Universitetssykehuset Nord-Norge (UNN), maailman pohjoisin yliopistollinen sairaala.

title: Report on the Execution of Seven Death Sentences
content:
According to HRANA, citing Javan Online, at dawn yesterday, Wednesday, September 30, five prisoners at Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj, who had been sentenced to death in separate cases on murder charges, were executed by hanging.

According to the report, one of the prisoners went to his wife’s workplace in August-September 2020 due to a dispute with her and physically assaulted her. Later, when his wife’s parents went to the couple’s home to follow up on their marital problems, he killed both of them.

Another prisoner killed a young woman in August-September 2019 and subsequently, with the assistance of another individual, transported her body to the deserts near Robat Karim and set it on fire.

The report states that two other prisoners entered the home of an elderly man in Khordad 2020 with the intention of committing robbery and killed him during the robbery.

Another prisoner had been sentenced to death for the fatal shooting of a young man on March 14, 2024. During the investigation, he claimed that the victim had been harassing his sister.

title: UK Trial Challenges Gold Industry’s ‘Responsible Gold’ Certification
content:
An unusual trial will begin next week in London’s High Court: the families of two 23-year-old Tanzanian men who were fatally shot in 2019 at a Canadian-owned gold mine in northern Tanzania are bringing a case against the London Bullion Market Association (LBMA), an industry body that oversees the London gold market.

Another 30 Tanzanians recently joined the case, while a Canadian court dismissed another lawsuit over the killings, saying it did not have jurisdiction. The families are seeking redress for the LBMA’s decision to certify gold from the mine as “responsible gold.”

Human rights groups have reported for years that police have killed and injured people accused of trespassing and mining at the North Mara mine. Barrick Gold, the mine owner, has acknowledged deaths occurred, but says that the police were not under its control.

title: Suomi tukee Ukrainaa 50 miljoonan euron lainalla Maailmanpankkiryhmän kautta
content:
Ulkoministeriö myöntää 50 miljoonan euron kehityspoliittisen lainan Maailmanpankkiryhmään kuuluvalle Kansainväliselle kehitysjärjestölle IDAlle. Laina kohdistetaan IDAn uuteen erityisrahoitusohjelmaan SPUR 2.0 (Special Program for Ukraine Recovery 2.0), jonka tavoitteena on vastata Ukrainan mittaviin jälleenrakennus- ja elpymistarpeisiin.

Maailmanpankkiryhmän IDA myöntää maailman köyhimmille maille avustuksia ja pehmeäehtoisia lainoja köyhyyden vähentämiseksi ja kestävän kehityksen edistämiseksi. Ukrainan tukemiseksi perustettu SPUR 2.0 on osa IDAn uutta kriisirahoitusvälinettä. Se mahdollistaa lisärahoituksen mobilisoinnin Ukrainan jälleenrakennuksen ja taloudellisen elpymisen tueksi IDAn kautta.

Maailmanpankin uusimman arvion mukaan Ukrainan jälleenrakennuksen ja elpymisen kustannukset ovat lähes 588 miljardia Yhdysvaltain dollaria seuraavan vuosikymmenen aikana. SPUR 2.0 -ohjelman rahoituksella vahvistetaan Ukrainan taloudellista vakautta, yhteiskunnan toimintakykyä ja jälleenrakentamista Venäjän hyökkäyssodan jatkuessa.

title: Leaked Warrant List Reveals How Turkmenistan Targets Critics Abroad
content:
Even as he bounced between Poland, Sweden and the Netherlands seeking political asylum, Nurmuhammet Annayev kept pressure on the authoritarian regime in his home country of Turkmenistan.

Annayev runs a YouTube channel that has brought him popularity among fellow critics of the Turkmenistan government. But his activism has also kept him firmly in the regime’s sights.

“Turns out they can even take people from abroad,” he said. “These guys are ready to eliminate — to disappear — the person standing in front of them to achieve their goals.”

Annayev, whose exact location OCCRP is not disclosing due to security reasons, is right to believe he is a target of Turkmenistan’s sprawling security and legal apparatus. 

OCCRP’s member center, Turkmen.news, has obtained an arrest warrant list from the Ministry of Internal Affairs showing that Annayev was wanted in his home country for political reasons. He was accused of “calls for an armed seizure of power or change of the constitutional order,” as well as “open calls for extremist activities.”

title: AI chatbots remove hijabs from images of Muslim women when prompted
content:
Guardian tested chatbots after French far-right politician stripped a Muslim woman of her hijab in a photo

When prompted, AI chatbots will edit images to remove the hijabs from Muslim women, a violation of one of the world’s most common and visible expressions of faith.

The Guardian asked ChatGPT, Grok, Gemini and Claude to take the veil off an AI-generated image of a woman wearing a hijab. Both OpenAI’s ChatGPT and xAI’s Grok bots complied with the prompt. Anthropic’s Claude responded that it does not have an image-editing or -generating feature but that it would not alter a photo to remove someone’s hijab.

title: Rising CO₂ is making African savanna grasses grow more – what this means for grazing, fire and carbon storage
content:
Plants use carbon dioxide (CO₂) in photosynthesis to make the carbohydrates they need to grow. As the CO₂ in the atmosphere rises, mainly because humans are burning fossil fuels, many plants can photosynthesise more or use water more efficiently. This is known as “CO₂ fertilisation”.

Scientists have carried out numerous studies into CO₂ fertilisation in forests, crops and temperate ecosystems. What has been much less researched is how wild grasses in tropical savannas respond.

For decades, the grasses that dominate the ground layer of these savannas were expected to respond less strongly to rising CO₂ than many trees and other plants. Most use a type of photosynthesis called C4 photosynthesis. They include common African savanna species such as red grass (Themeda triandra) and bushveld signal grass (Urochloa mosambicensis).

title: Haiti: Attack in Artibonite underscores the urgent need to turn international commitments into effective protection
content:
In response to the attack reportedly carried out on 28 September by members of the armed gang Kokorat San Ras in Gros-Morne, Artibonite department, in which at least 11 people were killed and several others injured according to available information, Ana Piquer, Amnesty International’s Americas Director, said:

“Once again, a Haitian community is mourning after a brutal attack by armed gangs. The killings in Gros-Morne reveal an unbearable reality: as violence continues to spread beyond Port-au-Prince, people are paying with their lives for a deepening crisis.

title: A new publication examines the cumulative impacts of the green transition on traditional Sámi livelihoods
content:
30.09.2026

  • Share on FaceBook
  • Share on LinkedIn

    • Researcher | Arctic Centre, the University of Lapland

    In Nordic cooperation made report “Towards understanding and managing cumulative impacts in Sápmi: approaches & collaboration – Workshop Report with focus on spatial data, reindeer and reindeer herding” explores the use of spatial data and methods in assessing cumulative impacts on traditional Sámi livelihoods.

    The impacts of the green transition on Sápmi and reindeer herding areas have been increasing due to factors such as forestry, rare-earth mineral mining, and the production of hydroelectric and wind power. The planning processes for these past, ongoing, and future projects are highly fragmented; consequently, the cumulative impacts of the projects and the perspectives of local people have not been adequately considered during the planning stages. Assessing the impacts of both historical and new activities in Sápmi requires concepts, frameworks, and tools capable of addressing cumulative impacts across space, time, sectors, and borders, as well as a stronger knowledge base to support just decision-making.

title: Analysis: Wind and solar save UK from gas imports worth £5.9bn during Hormuz crisis
content:
The UK has avoided the need for gas imports worth £5.9bn since the start of the Hormuz crisis as a result of record generation from wind and solar, reveals Carbon Brief analysis.

While gas prices are surging to levels not seen since the 2022 energy crisis, the UK has been generating record amounts of power from wind and solar, up 14% year-on-year.

This unprecedented clean-power generation is directly cutting the need for gas-fired electricity, which is down by nearly 10% year-on-year in 2026 to date.

In total, wind and solar have generated a record 41% share of the UK’s electricity needs in 2026 to date, compared with 25% from gas, according to Carbon Brief’s analysis.

The figure below shows that wind and solar has avoided the need for UK gas imports worth £5.9bn, since the outbreak of war between the US and Iran in February 2026.

These avoided gas imports would have required the UK to secure the equivalent of more than 100 additional tanker deliveries of liquefied natural gas (LNG).

The £1.3bn import saving in September 2026 to date is the result of record wind and solar output, at nearly 10 terawatt hours (TWh), combined with surging gas prices.

title: Russia’s Rage Fixes on the British
content:
British statecraft has “lived free in Russia’s head” for hundreds of years, in the words of a former UK defense attaché in Moscow. The historian Mark Galeotti noted that, over the last century, “Perfidious Albion” was, in Russia’s eyes, its “most cunning and devious foe”.

From this soil, fed by £25 bn ($33 bn) of UK aid to Ukraine since 2022, has emerged an eruption of suspicion and hostility. It may yet produce something more menacing than the current torrent of Kremlin-inspired verbal barrages.

Russia is run in part by a siloviki of former Soviet security officials who were spoon-fed distrust of the British as part of their training. It is part of their lore that London did terrible harm to the Bolsheviks and then the Soviet era, and that British intelligence chalked up significant triumphs at their expense. In this worldview, British attempts to undermine Russian power and greatness are part of an old game.

The flip side is the strange magnetism of Britain for the Russian elite; there have been massive Russian investments in British real estate, academia, and legal and financial sectors which have led to the sobriquet ‘Londongrad’ for the second home of many oligarchs.

title: Youth perspectives on polarisation: When does difference become division?
content:
From Finland to Armenia and Palestine, young people encounter polarisation in different forms. Yet across these contexts, similar questions emerge about trust, belonging, participation and the spaces available for dialogue. These themes were at the heart of CMI’s webinar that brought together young voices to reflect on how divisions shape their societies and what role young people can play in addressing them.

The webinar, organised as part of the annual Youth Peace Week Finland’s programme, explored how polarisation affects young people in everyday life and how they navigate increasingly divided social and political environments. The discussion featured youth worker and peacebuilder Liana Vahanyan from Armenia, communications professional and researcher Atta Khaled from Palestine, and Finnish youth activist Heta Uhtio. The conversation was moderated by CMI’s Project Officer Shekeba Ahmadi and can be watched through a recording.

title: Openness & Digital Sovereignty: Who Sustains the Commons?
content:
We are in a critical moment for the open web, and must raise the issues of openness and the commons to the level of public dialogue as we try to steer AI development to serve the public interest. We are also in a moment when open is being hailed as a panacea for digital sovereignty. This warrants interrogation.

On September 21st, Creative Commons convened leading experts, practitioners, and builders for a day of conversation about the collaborative underpinnings of openness, investigating all the layers of the stack for a better, shared understanding of what openness can—and cannot—do to help communities and nations drive towards digital sovereignty.

This event was made possible through the generous support of the Siegel Family Endowment. We are grateful to our co-hosts at the NYU Engelberg Center for making the space for a conversation like this.

Clear throughlines from the convening were:

  • Openness creates choices
  • Sovereignty depends on our ability to exercise and sustain those choices
  • Sustaining the people, institutions, and shared resources that make openness possible must be part of any sensible sovereignty strategy

title: 80 Years After Nuremberg Trials, U.S. Leads Assault on ICC & International Law: Wolfgang Kaleck
content:
Eight decades after the Nuremberg trials against Nazi war criminals, the Trump administration has launched an all-out assault on the International Criminal Court, primarily over the tribunal’s pursuit of Israeli leaders for war crimes committed in Gaza. In his recent address to the United Nations, President Donald Trump called the ICC a “rogue institution” and urged other states to abandon it, and his administration has vowed to dismantle it through sanctions and other pressure tactics.

“It’s so sad to remember that the core group behind the Nuremberg trials were Robert Jackson, Telford Taylor and Benjamin Ferencz, the U.S. prosecutors,” says Wolfgang Kaleck, lawyer and founder of the European Center for Constitutional and Human Rights. His new book is The Power of Law: Reconciling Legality and International Justice.

title: 72 Hours or Two Weeks? Europe Takes Different Approaches to How Prepared People Should Be for a Crisis
content:
This raises the same practical question across Europe: how long should an individual household be able to cope on its own?

Some countries already have a clear answer – at least 72 hours. Others recommend being prepared for three to seven days, or even two weeks in certain scenarios. In some countries, there is no general preparedness timeframe at all.

The differences are not limited to the number of days. Countries also have different ideas about what preparedness actually means: in some, it means having water, food and medicines at home; elsewhere, it also includes alternative heating, cooking, electricity and communication, as well as access to civil protection infrastructure.

Three days have become something of a symbol of civil preparedness in Europe in recent years.

title: Victory! California Appeals Court Refuses to Revive Surveillance Tech CEO’s Meritless Lawsuit Against Journalist
content:
When the rich and powerful try to use the court to silence negative reporting about themselves, it’s worth calling out that behavior for what it is: an attack on free speech. This is why EFF is happy to stand up for reporters who find themselves in that situation.

The California Court of Appeals upheld a lower court’s decision to strike a former Premise Data CEO’s meritless lawsuit against a journalist who exposed the CEO’s secret arrest for felony domestic violence. Jack Poulson, the writer and publisher of All Source Intelligence, reported details from the San Francisco Police Department’s report of the arrest and posted a copy of the report after receiving the document from a confidential source. Poulson later learned the arrest record had been sealed. The CEO, Maury Blackman, sued Poulson, Substack, AWS, and another organization for damages to try and force the removal of Poulson’s reporting from the internet.

title: Montenegro celebrates its first European Heritage Award, presented to the Pacijenca Project – Safeguarding the Dobrota Lace Tradition
content:
On 25 September, the Pacijenca Project – Safeguarding the Dobrota Lace Tradition, a 2026 European Heritage Award / Europa Nostra Award winner, was celebrated with a moving event at St. Tryphon Cathedral in Kotor, Montenegro. “Pacijenca” is the first Montenegrin project to receive Europe’s top heritage award in 25 years. The ceremony, held as part of the European Heritage Days, brought together national and municipal officials, representatives of cultural institutions, the lace-making community led by Nada Radović, and the wider public.

Led by Museums of Kotor, the Pacijenca Project was awarded in the Education, Training and Skills category for reviving the endangered skill of Dobrota needle lace-making through sustained teaching, public demonstrations and contemporary heritage interpretation. Its name comes from the Italian word for patience, “pazienza”.

The ceremony opened with the reading of a congratulatory message from the President of Montenegro, Mr. Jakov Milatović.

title: Living better while living longer
content:
Europeans are living longer. This is one of the achievements of our social model. The question is whether we are living those additional years in good physical and mental health and whether this progress is shared equally across society.

The pursuit of longevity cannot simply mean adding years to life. It just as well means adding life to those years. In other words, extending the time in which we can take a full part in society, keep our relationships, feel accomplished and live with dignity. Importantly, though, healthy longevity must not become another privilege that correlates with income or social status. The right to healthy longevity needs to become an imperative of the progressive agenda for Europe.

title: How do you know when AI is wrong? Lessons from our AI x Investigative Journalism Forum
content:
Your story's data came from a scraper a reporter vibe-coded. The spot checks came back clean. Do you publish?

We opened the AI x Investigative Journalism Forum at The New York Times on Sept. 25 with that question, and 81% of attendees said they'd hold the story until someone reviewed the code. On the live polling app I built for the kickoff, attendees dragged a dot toward their answer, and 70% of the "hold" voters pushed theirs nearly all the way to the edge.

It was a snap judgment, made on phones in seconds. Reading the code is part of checking such a tool, but it won't tell you how often the output is wrong. For that, several speakers argued, you have to test the results.

That afternoon, Avery Schmitz of CNN taught attendees to vibe-code their own flight-tracking analysis and closed the workshop with his own stricter rule: "Never vibe code to a finding," and a checklist to go with it: check every finding against the raw source, reproduce the key claim and read the lines of code that produce it.

title: United Arab Emirates: A Year On, Critic Remains in Detention
content:
(Beirut) – A South Sudanese political commentator remains in prison in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) without charge a year after his arrest, Human Rights Watch said today. Emirati authorities have not disclosed the legal basis for the arrest of the commentator, Samuel Peter Oyay, to his family.

Oyay fled South Sudan in 2014, fearing for his safety. He moved to the UAE and had been running a private business there. While in the UAE, Oyay had written regularly for independent South Sudan-focused platforms, accusing its government of corruption that benefits the elite. The UAE and South Sudan have strengthened their bilateral relations in recent years. In 2025, President Salva Kiir visited the UAE at least three times.

“The UAE government’s zero-tolerance policy toward peaceful criticism is increasingly targeting critics of Abu Dhabi’s foreign allies who live in the UAE,” said Joey Shea, senior United Arab Emirates researcher at Human Rights Watch. “Emirati authorities should immediately release Samuel Oyay, who has been held for a year without charge.”

title: America, the Threatened?
content:
By Jonathan Power

LUND, Sweden | 30 September 2026 (IDN) — The French ambassador to the US from 1902 to 1924, Jean-Jules Jusserand, observed that distant powers could not easily threaten the US because “On the north, she has a weak neighbour; on the south, another weak neighbour; on the east, fish and on the west, fish”.

The coming of the submarine-based nuclear missile has not changed that. Apart from the fact that no enemy would dare use them for fear of retaliation, and that there is no country in the world that feels that hostile to America (except North Korea), the fact is America is too big and too far away to be invaded and dominated. A foreign army could not launch a blitzkrieg across the Midwest or create a Vichy America.

The real tragedy of 9/11 is that, just as a majority of the US electorate had settled into a post-Cold War comfort zone, with the new president, George W. Bush, not being overly pushy or confrontational in foreign affairs, America was jolted so badly that a large proportion of its electorate has been paranoid ever since.

title: How to sustain journalism that rarely pays for itself
content:
Investigative journalism is expensive to produce and rarely pays for itself. A single story can require months of reporting, cross-border collaboration, specialist expertise and legal support, with no guarantee that the revenue it generates will cover those costs. For newsrooms doing this work, financial sustainability means finding ways to sustain reporting whose public value far exceeds its commercial return.

That makes decisions about revenue especially consequential. Time spent developing a new income stream is time a small team cannot spend investigating. Yet dependence on a narrow funding base can leave a newsroom vulnerable to shifting donor priorities or pressure from advertisers. The challenge is to identify sources of income that fit an organisation’s editorial mission, make sensible use of its limited resources and protect its independence.

title: Metrons & Logons: Morgane Billuart in Conversation with Matthew Johnstone
content:
Metrons and Logons brings together Matthew’s recent series of photographic works with display structures made by eva duerden. The images move between recognisable objects and architecturally processed surfaces, reminding us of objects we used to consider technical, while acknowledging their obsolescence. The longer one looks, the less clear that designation of time becomes. The result is a set of images that seem familiar but increasingly difficult to place, inviting the viewer to stare at pictures with an intrigued, yet suspicious eye. In this conversation, Matthew Johnstone and Morgane Billuart discuss what happens to an image when it unknowingly appears to be a testimony of a world that breaks down, and yet, perhaps, with another life force, an odd gaze, is starting anew.

Matthew Johnstone,  Repose_8176, 2025. Archival C-type print, PVC, Metrons & Logons, Turning Space, Berlin, 2026. Courtesy of the artist and Turning Space

title: Poison Pills
content:
Copyright reform is again on the horizon in Europe. Not only is the 2019 Directive on Copyright in the Digital Single Market under evaluation, but the European Commission has also called for evidence about a series of potential reforms and, just yesterday, 29 September, launched a targeted consultation.

One idea on the table is a possible reform of the Union’s copyright exception for research, to facilitate researchers’ work when engaging with copyrighted materials. There will be plenty of discussion about the precise wording of this in the months and years to come.

In this context, we will see the contours of a broader question: what are the aspects of copyright law that need to be avoided if we want to uphold the interests of users, the institutions they rely on, and society more broadly?

These legislative ‘poison pills’ sharply reduce the scope and beneficial impact of otherwise potentially beneficial legislative provisions. When engaging in copyright reform discussions, it is therefore valuable to look out for these and highlight the threat they pose early on.

title: Why Museums Matter for Young People: Lessons from Amsterdam to Singapore
content:
Teenagers are swapping phone numbers at the end of a museum workshop. A young person who barely left home for three years is pitching their own exhibition to journalists. High school students in Los Angeles are teaching their younger siblings breathing exercises they first learned in front of a Van Gogh. Here is why museums matter for young people, and why they matter now more than ever.

Ask most people who museums are for, and young people tend to appear in only two roles: the primary school group on a trip, or the child in a buggy on a family day out. Somewhere between those early visits and adulthood, many of them drift away. The teenage and young adult years are often the point when museums lose them.

Yet these are exactly the years when young people most need what museums quietly offer. Anxiety, loneliness and uncertainty about the future are shaping a generation, and the places that traditionally support young people, from schools to youth services, are under strain. Many young people spend their days being measured, graded and compared, online and off.

title: Human knowledge at stake: Wikimedia Foundation makes its case at the United Nations General Assembly
content:
New York, 30 September 2026 – During the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), the Wikimedia Foundation’s CEO, Bernadette Meehan, and Global Advocacy team traveled to New York City to speak with policymakers, philanthropists, and high-level executives about the importance of protecting human knowledge in the age of AI. 

Throughout the week, the team undertook a range of external engagements, including a fireside chat at the UN headquarters with Melissa Fleming, UN Under-Secretary-General for Global Communications; joining Heather Gerken, President of the Ford Foundation and Nobel Laureates Maria Ressa and Muhammad Yunus on the main stage of the Clinton Global Initiative; and speaking with Dr. Rumman Chowdhury at the Devex Impact House. A number of bilateral meetings were also held with a wide range of UN representatives, technology leaders, and academics from around the world. During the week, our message was the same across every conversation: in the age of AI, we must keep humans at the heart of knowledge online.

title: The US Blacklists Alleged Venezuelan Cyber Crime Mastermind
content:
The U.S. Department of the Treasury on Wednesday announced it had placed on a special blacklist Aníbal Alexander Canelón Aguirre— a Venezuelan who appears on the FBI’s "Ten Most Wanted" list—identifying him as a key link in a financial network for the notorious crime group Tren de Aragua. 

Canelón Aguirre is wanted by the Justice Department for allegedly leading a multi-million dollar ATM fraud scheme. Authorities accuse him of masterminding a jackpotting operation involving malware that when installed allows thieves to direct the bank machine to spew out money.

The alleged Venezuelan hacker topped a list of six Venezuelans and three Mexicans whose names were announced Wednesday as having been added to a group of specially designated nationals. It effectively locks them out of the global financial system. Six of the named are co-defendants of Canelón Aguirre in a U.S. prosecution.

The accused hacker has been on the run, lending his tech skills to the likes of a Romanian mafia operating along Mexico's white-sand beaches and became the cyber "engineer" of the infamous Venezuelan Tren de Aragua gang.

title: The Cable that Changed the World: How Instant Global Communication Began in 1858
content:
The word wireless is going the way of computerized and portable, and for much the same reasons. We no longer regard wireless devices that require no physical connections to anything else as marvels, but as something close to necessities. But our age, with its increasingly common assumptions that information just travels through the air, owes its existence to wires — and, in a historical sense, to one set of wires in particular, whose story is told in the Primal Space video above. Woven into a mighty 2,000-mile-long cable, it was laid across the Atlantic Ocean 168 years ago, enabling the first direct communication link between North America and Europe. Not that intercontinental video sharing was just around the corner.

No, the height of communication technology at the time was the telegraph: the Victorian Internet, if you like, to borrow the title of the book by Economist editor Tom Standage that inspired the video. As a technology, telegraphy itself is quite a bit older than the aforementioned transatlantic cable. One possible starting point is 1746, when scientist Jean-Antoine Nollet managed to send a jolt of static electricity all the way down a line of 200 monks.

title: Julkiset palvelut ja etäisyyden politiikka
content:
Suomessa julkisten palvelujen ja päätösvallan keskittäminen kasvattaa etäisyyttä valtion ja kansalaisen välillä. Mitä etäisyys merkitsee hyvinvointivaltion ja demokratian kannalta?

Suomessa on ollut jo pitkään käynnissä kehitys, jossa julkisia palveluita kouluista poliisilaitoksiin ja terveysasemiin keskitetään suurempiin kaupunkeihin. Myös päätösvaltaa on keskitetty alueellisesti laajemmille yksiköille eli hyvinvointialueille. Tämä on johtanut kuntien päätösvallan kaventumiseen.

Samaan aikaan Suomessa käydään vilkasta keskustelua hyvinvointivaltion tulevaisuudesta. Monet poliitikot ja viranhaltijat ovat ehdottaneet hyvinvointivaltiosopimuksen uudelleenajattelua tilanteessa, jossa väestö vanhenee ja talouskasvu sakkaa.

title: A Girl Nearly Died After Drinking Raw Milk. The State Did Little to Punish the Unlicensed Farmer Who Sold It.
content:
Sitting in a pediatric intensive care unit last year, watching a ventilator keep her 17-month-old daughter alive, Emily Marris scoured the contents of her phone for evidence to give to California health and food safety investigators. 

She had bought raw goat milk from a farm recommended to her in a Facebook group run by her chiropractor. Marris had hoped the milk, unprocessed and natural, would help with her daughter Brooklyn’s constipation. But doctors now suspected the unpasteurized milk, which hadn’t been heated to kill off pathogens, was the source of the toddler’s severe E. coli infection. 

To the regulators who’d reached out to Marris, the case was a top priority. The farm appeared to be defying state law to sell unregulated raw milk to unsuspecting families; soon, another child, a 6-year-old girl who’d drunk milk from the same farm, would wind up in the same San Diego hospital, with the same potentially fatal illness, needing blood transfusions.

    Voiko tulevaisuustiedosta tehdä muutakin kuin raportin, esityksen tai skenaarion? Kokemuksellinen ennakointi auttaa muuttamaan abstraktit tulevaisuuskuvat koettaviksi tilanteiksi, jotka herättävät ajatuksia, tunteita ja toimintaa. Tässä 5+1 vinkkiä, joilla pääset alkuun.

    Tulevaisuudesta puhutaan usein kaavioina, raportteina ja skenaarioina. Ne ovat tarpeellisia, mutta eivät aina riitä. Mitä monimutkaisemmista muutoksista on kyse, sitä vaikeampaa voi olla hahmottaa, miltä niiden vaikutukset tuntuvat arjessa, työssä, päätöksenteossa tai yhteiskunnassa. Miten esimeriksi siirtymä kiertotalouteen tai neuroteknologian kuluttajakäyttö muuttaisi ihmisten arkea?

Sen tavoitteena ei ole ennustaa tulevaisuutta, vaan tehdä mahdollisia tulevaisuuksia koettaviksi: esineinä, tarinoina, peleinä, simulaatioina, tiloina, rooleina, kehollisina harjoituksina tai muina kokemuksina. Kun tulevaisuus tulee lähemmäs, se voi avata uusia kysymyksiä: mitä tämä tarkoittaisi minulle, meille tai niille, joita päätöksemme koskevat?

title: Kouvolan kirjastoleikkaukset osuisivat lapsiin, senioreihin ja vähävaraisiin
content:
Kouvolassa esitetään Haanojan ja Korian lähikirjastojen lakkauttamista. Jos kirjastot suljetaan, matka kirjastoon pitenee kohtuuttomasti.

Muutos vaikeuttaisi erityisesti lasten, senioreiden ja sellaisten ihmisten asiointia, jotka eivät voi kulkea kauemmas omin avuin tai joilla ei ole käytössään autoa.

Haanojan kirjaston lainaus on kasvanut viisi vuotta peräkkäin. Korialla kirjaston käyttö on jatkunut entisellään. Kirjastot ovat siis ahkerassa käytössä samaan aikaan, kun niiden tulevaisuus on vaakalaudalla.

Kirjastojen toimipisteiden lakkautus tai henkilöstön vähentäminen osuisivat suoraan kirjavinkkaukseen, kouluyhteistyöhön, satutuokioihin eli erityisesti lasten ja nuorten lukemista tukevaan toimintaan.

Myös aikuisten lukutaito heikkenee, sillä kirjasto on yksi harvoista tahoista, joka huolehtii myös aikuisten lukemisesta. Kirjastoissa tehtävä työ palvelee ihmisten juurtumista kotiseutuunsa ja tunnetta kuulumisesta yhteisöön.

Lukutaitoon satsaaminen on ensiarvoisen tärkeää niin Kouvolan kuin koko Suomen kannalta.

title: Inside Zuckerberg, Huang’s push for White House AI pact
content:
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg was the chief architect of the “morally binding” AI accords that emerged from Tuesday’s White House lunch with President Donald Trump, Speaker Mike Johnson and more than a dozen tech executives, according to five people familiar with the private meeting.

Zuckerberg, with the help of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, pitched the so-called AI accords to senior White House officials and some of the biggest names in tech during the luncheon, three of the people said. Both Huang as well as Trump administration officials helped shape the pact ahead of the meeting, according to two of the people.

All five people were granted anonymity because they were not authorized to share details of the discussions.

As part of the voluntary agreement, signatories would commit to the importance of enacting safeguards to mitigate potential risks from advanced AI models, but without a clear enforcement mechanism, it is unclear what if any consequences they may face for failing to do so.

title: Almost everyone naturally turns left when walking – and we still have no idea why
content:
This story began, like so many in the history of science, with something we were not looking for.

In 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic, we were studying a practical question: how do people move around in an enclosed space when you ask them to keep apart from one another? Watching the footage time after time, we noticed something odd: almost every participant walked in loops that turned in the same direction, always anticlockwise. Stranger still, none of them seemed to have noticed they were doing it.

That observation sent us on a five-year quest to work out why humans behave in this way.

The effect itself is easy to describe. Let a crowd roam within a closed space with no particular destination, and it slowly begins to rotate, almost always to the left. Nobody directs that motion. Nobody decides it.

To a physicist, this looks like a textbook instance of “emergent behavior”: a collective pattern that grows out of countless small interactions, either between individuals or between individuals and their surroundings. These were our two prime hypotheses, which we tried to validate in isolation.
snippet: This story began, like so many in the history of science, with something we were not looking for.

title: Nigeria’s school kidnapping threat is changing: 4 lessons from the 56-day Oyo attack
content:
Following the mass abduction of 46 pupils and teachers in Oyo State, south-west Nigeria in 2026, the authorities attributed the attack to the Ansaru terrorist group. Key suspects were prosecuted and handed prison terms. But this was not the first time terrorist groups had engaged in mass abduction of school pupils in Nigeria. Peace and security researcher Saheed Babajide Owonikoko explains what factors could have motivated the Ansaru terror group to stage that attack and what lessons Nigeria should take away from the incident, which lasted 56 days.

The lessons can be deduced from the differences between the incident and others that have taken place in Nigeria.

The first striking difference is that northern Nigeria was previously the centre of kidnapping incidents in Nigeria. As of 1 June 2026, there had been 31 mass school kidnapping incidents involving over 2,530 people in Nigeria since the 2014 Chibok incidents.

title: Report: Climate risks could multiply disruptions to Finland’s security of supply
content:
Climate change threatens Finland’s security of supply by increasing the likelihood of simultaneous crises and disruptions. Finland must prepare for climate risks as part of geopolitical crises and security policy, states a new report by the Finnish Institute of International Affairs (FIIA) and the National Emergency Supply Agency (NESA).

“Climate risks cannot be treated as something that we can circle back to once military crises are over,” says Leading Researcher Emma Hakala from FIIA, who headed the research project.

For example, extreme weather events can disrupt production, transport and the supply of critical raw materials, all of which are essential for security of supply, while the very same supply chains are being hindered by wars and trade disputes.

“This year, heatwaves caused significant problems across Europe, and the impacts of such phenomena are also quickly felt in Finland,” Hakala points out.

title: Guest Post — Medical and Health Data Sharing Policies Need Specific Guidance: New STM Recommendations Aim to Help

title: Web Archive Collections in Online Reference Resources
content: It’s officially fall, and in the U.S. that means the new school year is in full swing with bus stops, backpacks, books, and best friends. As primary source literacy and digital literacy become more critical than ever for elementary through higher education students, initiatives like the Library’s By the People and the National Archives and Records Administration’s Citizen Archivist Program bring historical documents right to desktops for transcription projects. Thanks to projects like these, teaching with primary sources and learning directly from them have never been easier. But have you ever thought about web archives in the context of these back-to-school materials? If not, let’s change that! Archived websites are born-digital primary sources of our current age that offer a plethora of information literacy opportunities for educators and students alike.

title: Sámedikki dutkanehtalaš ráđđi álggahii doaimmas / Sämitige tutkâmeettisâš rääđi algâttij tooimâs
content:
Davvisámegiella | Anarâškielâ

Sámedikki ođđa dutkanehtalaš ráđđi nanosmahttá sámiid vejolašvuođaid oassálastit sámiid guoski dutkama ehtalaš árvvoštallamii. Ráđi bargun lea ovddidit dutkanehtalaš rávvagiid ollašuvvama, mearridit sámiid searvvušlaš ovdamiehtamiin ja ovddidit ovdamiehtanmeannudeami.

Sámedikki dutkanehtalaš ráđi doaibma vuođđuduvvá dan meannudanvuohkái, man Sámediggi válddii atnui 2016, mainna diđoštuvvo friija dihtui vuođđuduvvi ovdamiehtan. Meannudanvuogi mihttomearrin lea dorvvastit sámiid álgoálbmotvuoigatvuođaid ollašuvvama dutkamis ja prošeavttain, mat gusket dahje sáhttet guoskat sámiid kulturárbái ja árbedihtui. Seammás meannudanvuohki ovddida sámiid kulturárbbi seailuma ja nanne sámiid iešmearridanvuoigatvuođa iežaset kulturárbái ja árbedihtui. Kandidáhta- ja pro gradu -bargguin eai gáibiduvvo ovdamiehtanmeannudeapmi.

Dutkanehtalaš ráđđi čoahkkanii vuosttas háve 29.9.2026. Čoahkkimis álggahuvvui ráđi bargu, gieđahallojedje sámiid guoski dutkan- ja ovddidanprošeavttaid ovdamiehtanbivdagat ja válmmaštallojuvvui bealiváldin sámiid duohtavuohta- ja soabadankomišuvnna doaibmabidjoevttohussii sámi dutkama doaibmagottis.

title: Valokuituyhtiö Valoo Oulun Kirjamessujen ja pohjoisen kirjallisuuden tukijaksi
content:
Oulun Kirjamessujen projektipäällikkö Eija Honkonen iloitsee uudesta yhteistyökumppanista, joka edustaa perinteisen kirjamaailman ulkopuolista toimialaa.

”On hienoa saada myös teknologiayritys mukaan tukemaan pohjoista kirjallisuutta ja tätä hienoa tapahtumaa. Sähköiset formaatit ovat yleistyneet vahvasti myös kirjamaailmassa, ja luotettavia, hyviä nettiyhteyksiä tarvitsevat nykypäivänä kaikki”, Honkonen toteaa.

Valoon myyntijohtaja Antti Ruotsalainen näkee teknologiayrityksen ja kulttuuritapahtuman arvoissa paljon samaa. ”Kirjallisuus, lukeminen ja jatkuva oppiminen ovat sivistyneen yhteiskunnan peruspilareita. Valokuituverkkojen tarkoitus on yhdistää ihmisiä ja mahdollistaa tiedon sekä tarinoiden sujuva siirtyminen. Haluamme ehdottomasti olla mukana tukemassa pohjoista kulttuuria. Hyvä nettiyhteys mahdollistaa osaltaan kirjallisuuden ja oppimateriaalien tasa-arvoisen saavutettavuuden asuinpaikasta riippumatta”, Ruotsalainen sanoo.

Valoon lisäksi pohjoisen kirjallisuuden tukijoihin kuuluvat sanomalehti Kaleva, LähiTapiola Pohjoinen, Pohjolan OP, Oulun kulttuurisäätiö sekä Oulun kaupunki.

title: “East of Eden” Is at the Library; Now It Comes to TV
content:
Florence Pugh and Zoe Kazan, the star and screenwriter (respectively) of Netflix’s “East of Eden,” a fresh take on John Steinbeck’s classic 1952 California novel, recently came to the Library to get a look at some original Steinbeck material.

Among other items on display, there were signed first editions of “Eden,” manuscript pages from “The Grapes of Wrath” and a dozen or so books from the 19th and early 20th centuries that documented the land and the people of the Salinas Valley, the primary setting of “Eden,” “Of Mice and Men” and other Steinbeck works.

The seven-episode series, which debuts tomorrow,  will stretch, like the book, from the end of the Civil War to World War I. It will also be a tale of good and evil, like the book, but is more centered around the lightning rod character of Cathy Ames, played by Pugh.

“I believe there are monsters born in the world to human parents,” Steinbeck writes in introducing Cathy in the novel, a famous sentence that also begins the series’ trailer, already viewed more than 5 million times on YouTube alone.

title: Tutkimus: Ilmastoriskit voivat moninkertaistaa Suomen huoltovarmuushäiriöt
content:
Ilmastonmuutos uhkaa Suomen huoltovarmuutta lisäämällä samanaikaisten kriisien ja häiriötilanteiden todennäköisyyttä. Ilmastoriskeihin on varauduttava osana geopoliittisia kriisejä ja turvallisuuspolitiikkaa, todetaan Ulkopoliittisen instituutin (UPI) ja Huoltovarmuuskeskuksen (HVK) raportissa.

”Ilmastoriskeihin ei voida suhtautua jonakin, johon voidaan palata sitten, kun sotilaalliset kriisit ovat ohi”, sanoo tutkimushanketta vetänyt UPIn johtava tutkija Emma Hakala.

Esimerkiksi äärisäät voivat häiritä huoltovarmuuden kannalta olennaista tuotantoa, kuljetuksia ja kriittisten raaka-aineiden saatavuutta samalla, kun sodat ja kauppakiistat vaikeuttavat samojen toimitusketjujen toimintaa.

”Tänä vuonna helle aiheutti Euroopassa merkittäviä ongelmia, ja vaikutukset heijastuvat nopeasti myös Suomeen”, Hakala huomauttaa.

Samat ongelmat toistuvat eri aloilla

Tutkimuksessa tarkasteltiin ilmastonmuutoksen vaikutuksia lääkehuoltoon, kriittisiin raaka-aineisiin, lannoitteisiin ja sähköistyvään energiajärjestelmään. Kaikilla aloilla toistuivat samat ongelmat. Tuotanto on keskittynyt harvoihin maihin, ja se on riippuvaista yksittäisistä toimittajista.

title: Malaysia begins Myanmar repatriations despite warnings from UN and rights groups
content:
Kuala Lumpur plans to send a total of 5,000 Myanmar nationals back to the war-torn country despite persecution concerns

Malaysia began sending back about 1,500 Myanmar nationals on Tuesday, the government confirmed, as it launched a scheme that rights groups say may endanger migrants and asylum seekers by returning them to the war-torn country.

The group is the first of 5,000 Myanmar citizens that Kuala Lumpur says agreed to “voluntary” repatriation from detention centres amid a huge uptick in anti-migrant sentiment in Malaysia.

Riitta ja Ilkka -kirjassa kulkevat rinnakkain Suomisen vanhempien sekä Riikka Suomisen oma rakkaustarina. Kirja ei ole romanttista huttua vaan ihan todellista tilanteiden, prosessien ja tunne-elän kuvausta. Ihmisten pohtimista vaikeiden ratkaisujen äärellä.

Tiedot vanhempien Suomisten tarinasta perustuvat heidän kirjeenvaihtoonsa sekä keskusteluihin pariskunnan tuttavien kanssa, toki mielikuvitusta unohtamatta.

title: WikiCon: Wie es der Wikipedia-Community in einer sich verändernden Welt geht
content:
Seit 2011 ist die WikiCon der wichtigste Treffpunkt für Menschen, die sich in der deutschsprachigen Wikipedia und ihren Schwesterprojekten engagieren. Mitte September kamen insgesamt 413 Ehrenamtliche in Regensburg und online zusammen, um gemeinsam über aktuelle Themen und Herausforderungen zu diskutieren.

Mehr als 70 Programmpunkte gab es auf der diesjährigen WikiCon. Den Auftakt machte eine Podiumsdiskussion, in der es gleich um die ganz großen Fragen ging: Welche Rolle spielen freie Wissensprojekte für eine offene und resiliente Demokratie? Und welche Chancen und Herausforderungen ergeben sich für freiwilliges Engagement im digitalen Raum?
