title: How the bad science of AI doomerism is good for big business
content:
There is no clear path showing that today’s AI systems will lead to superintelligence, much less a basis for calculating the probability of doom.

The power attributed to superintelligence has led some in these communities to describe advanced AI in God-like terms. […] “They believe in the advent of an almighty powerful AI god, which will either lead to destruction of humanity or help us achieve utopia,” says Boyan Milanov, Senior Research Scientist at AI Now Institute.

“What we have to keep in mind is that all this doomerism isn’t based on any scientific work,” says Milanov. “It really is science fiction. None of the claims are scientifically verifiable or falsifiable.”

title: Kokoomuksen leikkausohjelma tarkoittaisi kehitysyhteistyön totaalista romuttamista – Fingo: ”Kannustamme tarkistamaan numerot”
content:
Suomalaisten kehitysjärjestöjen kattojärjestö Fingon laskelmien mukaan kokoomuksen ehdotus tarkoittaisi kehitysyhteistyön totaalista romuttamista ja suunnanmuutosta Suomen ulkopolitiikkaan.

Jaa

Kokoomus ehdottaa velkajarruohjelmassaan kehitysyhteistyöhön ensi vaalikaudelle 300 miljoonan euron leikkausta.

Varsinaisen kehitysyhteistyön määrärahat ovat ensi vuonna noin 483 miljoonaa euroa. Fingon vaikuttamistyön johtaja Ilmari Nalbantoglu kuvailee, että leikkaus olisi mahdollista kohdistaa lähinnä tähän osaan kehitysyhteistyön rahoitusta. Muu kehitysyhteistyörahoitus pitää sisällään esimerkiksi Suomen osuuden EU:n kehitysyhteistyöstä. Tästä kehitysyhteistyön rahoituksen osasta ei ole juurikaan mahdollisuuksia leikata.

Kokoomus on lisäksi tavoiteohjelmassaan kirjannut, että se haluaa turvata humanitaarisen avun rahoituksen. Puolue toteaa velkajarruohjelmassaan, ettei se myöskään lakkauttaisi Ukrainan maaohjelmaa.

Näin ollen kokoomuksen ehdotuksen täytyisi tarkoittaa monenkeskisen (esimerkiksi YK-järjestöjen, kuten UNICEFin ja UN Womenin kautta kanavoitu rahoitus), kahdenvälisen ja järjestöjen kehitysyhteistyön ajamista kokonaan tai lähestulkoon kokonaan alas.

title: Webinar: Making the case: how libraries justify support for open access. Oct 22, 10 am (GMT) | Open Book Collective
content: Most librarians who champion open access have, at some point, had to justify or defend the spend. Who is this money for? Why this model and not another? What do we stop funding to make room for this? These questions rarely have easy or tidy answers, and the case that persuades finance committees or senior management is not always the one that best reflects our values. In this Open Access Week session, we hear from two institutions that have made that case in practice. Hannah Crago, previously from the University of Essex, now at the University of Cambridge, will discuss her experiences in helping the library to build institutional support for OA. Louise Otting from TU Delft will talk about the university's dedicated fund and how it came to exist. Caroline from the Open Book Collective will bring both together in the wider landscape of collective, community-governed funding for Diamond OA books.

title: Hub publishes policy paper and launches campaign to put cultural heritage at the heart of Public AI in Europe
content:
The EU-funded European Heritage Hub has published its policy paper “Beyond adopter and supplier: putting cultural heritage at the heart of Europe’s Public AI ecosystem”, released on 29 September on the occasion of the Hub’s Policy Talk  “INNOVATE. PROTECT. EMPOWER: How cultural heritage can make Public AI a reality” and is launching its dedicated advocacy campaign. Developed with the Europeana Foundation and with input from Hub partners across Europe, the paper highlights the role of the cultural heritage sector in the European Commission’s forthcoming AI strategy for the Cultural and Creative Sectors, expected in 2027. The campaign turns its key messages into a call for action: organisations and networks across Europe are invited to endorse it.

Read the policy paper · Read the executive summary

The AI strategy for the Cultural and Creative Sectors was announced in the Culture Compass for Europe published in November 2025. The Hub’s paper builds on “The case for Public AI: making it happen with cultural heritage”, published in June 2026, and on the responses that the Hub and the Europeana Foundation submitted to the Commission’s Call for evidence.

title: Lawyer Cites ChatGPT-Invented Fake Witnesses in Murder Appeal
content:
A lawyer used ChatGPT to generate briefs that included completely made-up witnesses and testimony while representing a man accused of shooting his wife. When he was caught by the judges, the lawyer blamed it on his own “stupidity.” 

“It's little comfort to know that my stupidity is what brings us together this afternoon,” New Mexico attorney Stephen D. Aarons said in a hearing last month before five judges. He “assumed” ChatGPT would generate a “bulletproof summary of proceedings.” Instead, ChatGPT generated false testimony from “wholly fabricated witnesses,” according to an order of direct contempt from the New Mexico Supreme Court. Aarons was representing a man who was found guilty of killing his wife earlier this year; Aarons said he hadn’t told his client directly that he was caught using ChatGPT on the case because he’s currently serving life in prison.

title: German innovation award recognises CMI’s pioneering digital approach to peacemaking
content:
The Round Table for Mediation and Conflict Management of the German Economy (RTMKM) has named CMI the winner of its 2026 Innovation Prize for Mediation and Conflict Management at an award ceremony in Frankfurt am Main on 22 September.

CMI – Martti Ahtisaari Peace Foundation has won a prize for innovation in mediation and conflict management for its AI-supported consultation that increased young people’s participation in its work with Yemeni political parties.

Felix Kufus (fourth left) at the prize ceremony. He led CMI’s development and implementation of the approach.

The prize by the Round Table for Mediation and Conflict Management of the German Economy recognises innovative approaches that promote alternative dispute resolution or conflict prevention.

Eligible innovations could be procedural, substantive, technical or non-technical, but had to be theoretically grounded, already applied in practice and respond to a recognisable demand.

“Digital innovation is most valuable when it helps us hear voices that might otherwise go unheard,” said Johanna Poutanen, Head of CMI’s Inclusion and Digital Innovation team.

title: Scenario Planning: Civil Society Responses to Far Right Authoritarianism
content:
This is a scenario planning tool for civil society organisations concerned about whether they have the right strategies in place given the rise of the authoritarian far right and the influence it is already having.

The tool was developed by Jim Coe, UK social movement researcher and consultant. Jim Coe and Natasha Adams have convened gatherings; undertaken research; and produced reports investigating the impact of the far right on civil society organisations, and the range of potential responses.

In their report, Towards Meaningful Action: NGOs’ responses to threats from far-right authoritarianism, Coe and Adams emphasise the need to take substantive steps across a range of areas: Building a collective response; Organisations’ capabilities and preparedness; and Organisational strategy.

The problem we are facing is that a far-right, authoritarian political party is increasingly gaining access to power and could potentially form a future government, but also that the influence of the far-right is already permeating government and other policy, discourse, and spaces for influence. – Towards Meaningful Action, 2026

title: "No Land to Stand On": Mahmoud Khalil on His Memoir, Palestine, Fighting Deportation & Suing Columbia
content:
We speak with Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil about his new memoir, No Land to Stand On: Notes from Detention. It details his 104 days of detention inside a Louisiana ICE jail after he was targeted for arrest and deportation by the Trump administration over his pro-Palestine campus advocacy at Columbia University. Khalil missed the birth of his first child, Deen, while he was separated from his wife, Noor Abdalla, who is a U.S. citizen. The administration is still trying to deport Khalil, who has launched civil rights lawsuits against the government and Columbia University over his treatment.

“Eighteen months after my arrest, this administration has never charged me with any crime or even presented any evidence that I committed any crimes, yet they are able to get away with this because I’m Palestinian,” Mahmoud tells Democracy Now!

title: Has Russia deployed 80,000 troops near the Latvian and Estonian borders?
content:
Talk of possible mobilisation in Russia, together with reports that the aggressor state is preparing up to 20,000 beds in civilian hospitals near the Baltic Sea, has added to public concern. But public anxiety also creates fertile ground for false information.

In early September, a social media post claimed that Russia had deployed a “new army” of up to 80,000 troops near its borders with Latvia and Estonia, citing purported information from Lithuanian intelligence. The claim is false.

On 1 September this year, an anonymous account called “Кассандра” (Kassandra) published a post on Threads with an alarming introduction: “Don’t make any plans for autumn. We’re taking the Baltics. Lithuanian intelligence reports that the Baltic people are soon going to be ***.” The post claimed that Russian armed forces had moved hundreds of military trucks to the borders with Latvia and Estonia, that new offensive divisions had been formed from brigades stationed there, and that the total strength of this “new army” was between 50,000 and 80,000 troops.

The post also claimed that “fresh satellite images confirm the troop buildup. The concentration of equipment is alarming NATO and the Baltic people.”

title: Who can speak on behalf of the people? The new frontiers of protest in the Sahel
content:
Can a democracy exist without the right to disagree?

Originally published on Global Voices

Demonstrations in the Sahel: (left) Mali, (center) Niger, and (right) Burkina Faso. Screenshots via YouTube.

This post is part of Global Voices’ September 2026 Spotlight series, “Protest in Democracy.” With this Spotlight, we seek to explore the many forms of protest, the tactics states use to delegitimize and suppress them, and the complex relationship between protest and democracy. You can support this coverage by donating here.

In the countries of the central Sahel, Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger, military juntas present themselves as the voices of restored popular sovereignty. At the same time, political parties have been dissolved in all three countries, more than a thousand civil society organizations have been suspended in Burkina Faso, and labor unions are under attack in Niger. What becomes of the right to protest when those in power claim to embody the very people on whose behalf the protests are being held?

title: Tigray’s Renewed Conflict: How Drone Warfare is Reshaping the Battlefield
content:
By Daniel Tesfa, Shim Masha and Filmon Gebremikael

Addis Ababa | Ethiopia | 30 September 2026 (IDN) — Drone warfare reshapes Ethiopia–Tigray’s battlefield, while civilians relive the devastation of past wars.

From Pretoria to Renewed War

The Pretoria Agreement of November 2022, formally known as the Cessation of Hostilities Agreement (CoHA), was intended to end Ethiopia’s devastating Tigray war. Yet implementation faltered almost immediately. Internally displaced persons (IDPs) never returned to Western Tigray, which remained under the control of Amhara Fano militias, ENDF‑affiliated Tekeze Zeb units, and Eritrean forces. Large swathes of Eastern, Central, and Northwestern Tigray continued to be occupied by the Eritrean Army, undermining the credibility of the peace deal.

title: From Tagging to Togetherness: How Art UK Turned a Digital Tool into Real-World Connection
content:
A simple artwork-tagging tool has become the starting point for friendships, wellbeing and a renewed pride in place. At the Digital Collections Summit, Art UK’s Katey Goodwin and Natalie Willatt explained how.

Digital collections work is often measured in records, clicks and page views. But what happens when a national online platform is deliberately turned into something local, social and face-to-face?

That was the question behind a talk at the Digital Collections Summit by Katey Goodwin, Deputy Chief Executive and Director of Community Engagement at Art UK, and Natalie Willatt, the organisation’s Community Volunteer Manager. Using Art UK’s community volunteering programme in Stoke-on-Trent as a case study, they showed how a crowdsourcing tool called Tagger has sparked genuine human connection, reduced isolation and strengthened people’s relationship with art and place.

As Goodwin put it, Art UK’s mission is simple: to connect people with art. This programme set out to test whether art could also become a catalyst for connecting people with one another.

Čitna Báffa är ett tvärvetenskapligt verk av den samiska bildkonstnären Máret Ánne Sara och koreografen Alexandra Wingate, som förenar bildkonst, koreografi, rörelse och ljud. Verket utforskar en existentiell spänning mellan ett yttre liv som präglas av det västerländska industrisamhället och kapitalismen, och en inre värld som grundar sig på samisk filosofi och urfolkskunskap.

Projektet, som har sina rötter i samiska och arktiska sammanhang, samlar konstnärer från hela Norden, lyfter fram samiska perspektiv och skapar möten mellan publik, konstnärer och kulturaktörer. title: Fiji Overhauls Evidence Security After 52 Kilos of Cocaine Vanish from Court
content:
Fiji’s police chief has ordered the immediate transfer of all illicit drugs and cash to highly secure police vaults after officials confirmed Wednesday that 52.4 kilograms of cocaine tied to two major criminal cases were stolen from a High Court evidence room, in the capital, Suva, with much of the contraband replaced by flour.

The incident is seen as a significant blow to a police force already struggling with corruption allegations amid a surge in international drug trafficking. However, Police Commissioner Rusiate Tudravu maintained that police are not responsible for guarding evidence once it is transferred to the judiciary, comparing the nation’s High Court to a private residence.

“It’s just like your home,” he told an OCCRP reporter. “You’re the boss of your home. I cannot come and tell you I’ll guard your home. Simple.”

Fiji, a nation of fewer than a million people, is facing an escalating drug crisis. It has become a transit hub for cocaine smuggled from South America to Australia and New Zealand, and is now seeing a spike in domestic use driving soaring HIV rates linked to intravenous methamphetamine use.

title: The Oldest Book Printed with Movable Type is Not The Gutenberg Bible: Jikji, a Collection of Korean Buddhist Teachings, Predated It By 78 Years and It’s Now Digitized Online
content:
The history of the printed word is full of bibliographic twists and turns, major historical moments, and the significant printing of books now so obscure no one has read them since their publication. Most of us have only the sketchiest notion of how mass-produced printed books came into being—a few scattered dates and names. But every schoolchild can tell you the first book ever printed, and everyone knows the first words of that book: “In the beginning….”

The first Gutenberg Bible, printed in 1454 by Johannes Gutenberg, introduced the world to movable type, history tells us. It is “universally acknowledged as the most important of all printed books,” writes Margaret Leslie Davis, author of the 2019 book, The Lost Gutenberg: The Astounding Story of One Book’s Five-Hundred-Year Odyssey. In 1900, Mark Twain expressed the sentiment in a letter “commenting on the opening of the Gutenberg Museum,” writes M. Sophia Newman at Lithub. “What the world is to-day,” he declared, “good and bad, it owes to Gutenberg. Everything can be traced to this source.”

title: Ansök om trycknings- och översättningsstöd i oktober
content:
I oktober kan bokutgivare söka om stöd för att trycka fack- och skönlitteratur på svenska, samt stöd för att översätta böcker från finska till svenska.

Delegationen för den svenska litteraturens främjande handlägger statligt stöd för tryckning av svenskspråkig skön- och facklitterära verk som ges ut i Finland, samt stöd för översättning av finskspråkig skön- och facklitteratur till svenska. Delegationen handlägger även tryckningsstöd ur följande fonder inom SLS: Christian och Constance Westermarcks fond och Ingrid, Margit och Henrik Höijers donationsfond I.

Verket ska ges ut i Finland. Stöd kan sökas av förlag, föreningar och organisationer som ger ut litteratur i Finland. Det går också att söka stöd för böcker utgivna av privatpersoner på eget förlag förutsatt att utlåtanden av två oberoende lektörer bifogas ansökan. Stöd kan inte sökas av bokens författare utan endast av utgivaren.

Stödet utbetalas när avtal har undertecknats och fyra (4) exemplar av den färdiga boken har sänts till SLS.

Aktuell ansökningstid är 1–31.10.2026.

OBS! Frågor gällande ansökan besvaras fram till kl. 16 på fredag 30.10. Frågor kan skickas till adressen delegationen@sls.fi.
snippet: I oktober kan bokutgivare söka om stöd för att trycka fack- och skönlitteratur på svenska, samt stöd för att översätta böcker från finska till svenska.

title: ‘Absolute s–t’: EU’s Microsoft Teams alternative draws bad reviews from officials
content:
BRUSSELS — The European Commission has rolled out an alternative to Microsoft Teams — but officials using it aren’t impressed, with one describing the tool as “absolute shit.”

The Commission introduced Element Pro over the summer as a “sovereign back-up to Teams,” according to an internal staff memo seen by POLITICO. The platform is intended to provide a fallback for Commission communications if U.S.-based Teams becomes unavailable.

While Teams remains the Commission’s main communications tool, Element Pro is an “internal back-up … that helps ensure our business continuity” in the event of a “disruption,” the memo says.

But three officials have questioned why the Commission needs the new system — and whether it works well enough to serve as a genuine backup.

“I don’t understand the added value here,” one official wrote on an internal staff message board, seen by POLITICO. Another described the tool as “absolute shit.”

A third official said that, judging matters on how well Element Pro works compared to Teams, the U.S. would “instantly win the war” if it ever decided to switch off its technology. All the officials were granted anonymity to speak freely.

title: Cities across the world are sinking because of groundwater depletion. But the process can be reversed
content:
Many cities around the world are sinking because too much water is extracted from the groundwater reservoirs beneath them.

This sinking makes these coastal cities more exposed to rising seas as the climate warms.

But as our new research shows, this process can work in reverse; when groundwater is replenished, cities can rise.

Our findings also reveal an unexpected clue: faultlines play a key role in shaping where the fastest groundwater recovery and land uplift occur.

Land subsidence, the gradual sinking of the ground surface, affects many of the world’s major cities.

Parts of Jakarta, the capital of Indonesia, are sinking more than ten centimetres each year, prompting the government to plan a relocation of the city.

The coastal city of Tianjin, China, is home to 15 million people. It, too, is a subsidence hotspot. If sinking there continues unabated, 15% of the city’s population will be underwater by 2120.

Similar stories are playing out from San Diego to Iran’s major cities, wherever groundwater has been pumped faster than it can refill.

title: Immo Salonen appointed CEO of Profinder
content:
Immo Salonen has been appointed the new CEO of Profinder, taking up his position at the beginning of November 2026. In his new role, Salonen will also lead Liana, both part of the Ilkka Group.

Salonen joins Profinder from his role as CEO of Auntie Solutions. He has previously held leadership positions at companies including LINK Mobility, TietoEVRY and Giosg.

Salonen’s appointment marks the next phase in Profinder’s development, with a continued focus on growth, data-driven sales and marketing, and expanding the company’s international opportunities.

“Profinder has built a strong position through its expertise in data-driven sales and marketing. I see significant potential to build on this foundation and accelerate growth. Together with Liana, there are also opportunities to combine complementary data, technology and commercial expertise to create new value for customers,” says Immo Salonen.

Profinder and Liana will continue to operate as separate businesses, with their own brands, teams and services. Existing customer agreements and contact persons remain unchanged, and the appointment will not affect customers’ day-to-day business.

title: Maahanmuuttajataustaiset lapset: Rasismia on kaikkialla – aikuisten pitäisi puuttua enemmän
content:
Maahanmuuttajataustaiset lapset toivovat päättäjiltä ja aikuisilta nykyistä voimakkaampaa puuttumista rasismiin, syrjintään ja kiusaamiseen.

Lapsiasiavaltuutetun toimisto kokosi keväällä 5.–6.-luokkalaisista maahanmuuttajataustaisista lapsista Nuoret neuvonantajat -tiimin. Yhdentoista lapsen ryhmä kokoontui neljä kertaa keskustelemaan siitä, miten maahanmuuttajataustaisten lasten oikeudet voisivat toteutua Suomessa nykyistä paremmin.

Lasten mukaan hyvän arjen perusta on varsin tavallinen: kaverit, läheiset ihmiset, koulu ja harrastukset. Olennaista on tunne siitä, että kuuluu joukkoon ja että tulee kohdelluksi samalla tavalla kuin muut.

Yksi ryhmään osallistuneista lapsista kuvasi hyvää tilannetta näin:

"Sitä ei nolota oma kansallisuus ja ei kohtaa rasismia, ei koe kiusaamista, ei katsota eri tavalla, häntä kohdellaan samalla tavalla, häntä ei syrjitä, saa kavereita, tuntuu turvalliselta, saa tukea muilta, ja häntä kunnioitetaan."

Lasten mukaan tavallista ja turvallista arkea vaikeuttavat erityisesti kiusaaminen, syrjintä ja rasismi.

Rasismi koettiin laajaksi ja konkreettiseksi ongelmaksi. Se liittyi lasten kokemuksissa usein ihmisen taustaan, kieleen tai ulkonäköön.

title: USPS To Put Cameras in Trucks That Scan Roads for ‘Community Safety’
content:
The United States Postal Service is running a pilot program to put cameras in its mail carrier trucks that continuously scan roads and signs, map roadways and sidewalks, and improve “community safety,” according to a letter posted by a labor union and a statement from the agency to 404 Media. The idea is that, since the trucks are constantly traveling anyway, they can be used as a way to collect data, eventually potentially across the nation.

“The purpose of this pilot is to leverage the Postal Service’s unique ability to collect this valuable data due to the scale and frequency with which our fleet of postal vehicles travel the streets of every community across the country,” the letter, posted by NALC Branch 238 to Facebook, reads.

The letter, written by the United States Postal Service (USPS) Labor Relations to Brian Renfroe, the president of the National Association of Letter Carriers, says the USPS will partner with Next Base, a dashcam company, for the pilot. At the moment, the cameras will be used in the Washington, DC area, and will be installed on a hundred vehicles, the letter says.

title: NATO Drones: Swarm or Be Swarmed
content:
Picture a Ukrainian command center: screens show drones moving into a contested battlespace. Their pictures are relayed back to military operators, but they are also acting in concert through linked communications. Software helps determine which drone is best positioned to continue the mission based on its location, payload, and chances of survival.

The operator assesses the information collected by the drone flight, confirms the target, and makes the final decision on whether to engage. Artificial intelligence accelerates the process, but the human remains in control of the critical decision.

This is what coordinated autonomy means in practice. It does not remove people from warfare. It allows one operator to supervise multiple systems that can navigate, exchange information, and divide tasks even when satellite systems like GPS are jammed, or communications are disrupted. Without this, every drone must be managed separately, decisions take longer, and military units cannot operate at the speed and scale that modern warfare requires.

title: The Bank of Latvia has not “printed” new money since 2014. Was Prime Minister Kulbergs wrong?
content:
In the discussion, it was pointed out that “price increases are the direct responsibility of The Bank of Latvia (Latvijas Banka, LB)”. When it was suggested that it “continually “prints” new money”, Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs (United List) replied that the central bank “has not printed money since we joined the eurozone in 2014”. The discussion was joined not only by other users but also by LB, which pointed out that it both “issues euro banknotes and coins and participates in their printing”.

LB’s post on X about money issuance and its involvement in “printing”, as well as the charts it provided, sparked a new thread, with the bank being accused of lying. “Here, the Bank of Latvia is lying. title: Russia Challenges South Africa’s Exclusion From G20 Summit
content:
By Kester Kenn Klomegah*

MOSCOW | NEW YORK | 30 September 2026 (IDN) — At the 81st UN General Assembly in New York, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov reiterated Russia’s objection to South Africa’s exclusion from the forthcoming G20 summit in the United States, while emphasising the importance of multilateral institutions and the place of Africa in the emerging international order.

Lavrov described in some detail Russia’s assessment of the current state of relations with the United States. His remarks also touched on broader questions confronting Africa and other countries of the Global South and East as they seek to strengthen the multilateral foundations of the international system and counter what they regard as neocolonial practices.

The 2026 G20 Leaders’ Summit is scheduled for Miami, Florida, on 14–15 December. The United States has invited Russian President Vladimir Putin to attend, an invitation US Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed after talks with Lavrov on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.

title: What Will the Future Remember? Why Museums Must Start Collecting Social Media Now
content:
Try to imagine studying the Renaissance without its art. Now imagine a historian in 2126 trying to understand our era without hashtags, viral videos or online activism. At the Digital Collections Summit, Craig Middleton (State Library of South Australia) and Caroline Wilson-Barnao (University of Queensland) argued that museums can no longer afford to leave social media out of their collections, and offered a practical roadmap for getting started.

Here’s a thought experiment worth sitting with. A historian 100 years from now wants to understand what it was like to be alive in 2026. What should they be able to see?

Our buildings, newspapers, government records and photographs, certainly. But what about the TikToks, Instagram posts, Facebook groups, memes, WhatsApp conversations and YouTube videos through which so much of contemporary life is actually lived?

For Middleton and Wilson-Barnao, co-authors of Collecting Social Media in Museums (Routledge, 2025), the answer is an obvious yes. The more interesting question is why so many museums are still hesitant to act on it.

title: Egyptian Security Services Arrest Entire Newsroom within 24 Hours
content:
Egyptian security services have arrested six journalists between Monday and Tuesday, all working for local independent investigative journalism platform Matsadaash. According to a statement published by the news platform on Wednesday, the crackdown began with raids on the homes of two of the journalists on Monday evening and early Tuesday morning. Over the following hours, authorities raided the homes of the other journalists working for the platform, without providing “any clear explanation for this escalation or its legal basis,” the statement said.

“With these latest arrests, the entire editorial team in the Matsadaash newsroom is now in detention.”  

In a separate statement, the journalists’ legal representative, the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, said that all six journalists' whereabouts remain unknown, adding that they have not been allowed to contact their families or legal team.

title: EU and Canada to announce sweeping new partnership pact
content:
BRUSSELS — The EU and Canada will use a landmark summit next month to announce an expansive new partnership, ranging from breaking down digital trade barriers to joint support for Ukraine and investing in fighting wildfires.

“The world is rapidly changing with unprecedented geopolitical challenges as well as challenges across trade, energy, technology, climate, and resources,” reads a draft joint statement to be issued by the two sides, circulated to EU ambassadors in preparation for the planned summit that begins on Oct. 29, and obtained by POLITICO.

The EU and Canada have been seeking to shore up their strategic ties as they grapple with the fallout from U.S. President Donald Trump’s trade war. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen this month proposed inviting Canada to become an associate member of the EU, triggering an immediate threat by Trump to impose tariffs.

“Canada and the EU, with our unparalleled trade access, shared values, and complementary economic strengths, can build a deeper and more integrated relationship,” the draft paper says.

title: After a decade, the UN’s Antonio Guterres is stepping down. His legacy will be mixed, at best
content:
In his farewell address to the United Nations General Assembly last week, António Guterres reminisced about his time as secretary general.

In his words, it was a decade during which wars:

dragged on with despicable cruelty. Civilians were targeted. Human rights trampled. Hunger weaponised. Humanitarians killed. International law cast aside.

dragged on with despicable cruelty. Civilians were targeted. Human rights trampled. Hunger weaponised. Humanitarians killed. International law cast aside.

It’s true Guterres and the UN faced increasingly difficult challenges during his decade-long period in office, but as he prepares to depart office at the end of the year, how should his tenure be judged?

There are currently 65 active armed conflicts in the world, the most since 1946.

Two permanent members of the UN Security Council, Russia and the United States, have started wars in violation of the UN Charter.

Meanwhile, tech experts are now warning that AI might wipe out humanity. Accelerating climate change also poses an existential threat.

No UN secretary general could solve all these crises. But historical comparisons are not in Guterres’ favour.

title: Mitä lumi merkitsee elolliselle luonnolle? – Biologi Arto Marjakankaan tietoteos talvesta ilmestyy
content:
Mitä eläinten jäljet hangella kertovat talvisesta elämästä? Millä keinoin kasvit selviävät talvesta? Miten linnut kätkevät ravintonsa talvea varten? Nämä ja monta muuta kysymystä lumesta selviävät biologi Arto Marjakankaan uudesta tietoteoksesta Elämää lumessa – Miten luonto talvehtii.

”Halusin koota Suomen oloissa ensimmäisen kokonaisesityksen lumen merkityksestä elolliselle luonnolle. Lumipeite ylläpitää luonnon monimuotoisuutta, mutta nyt lumeen sopeutuneita eliöitä uhkaa talvien lämpeneminen”, Arto Marjakangas kertoo.

Lumipeite ylläpitää luonnon monimuotoisuutta. Lumesta onkin enemmän hyötyä kuin haittaa pohjoisille eliöille, jotka ovat sopeutuneet vuodenaikojen vaihteluun. Elämää lumessa – Miten luonto talvehtii on tietokirja lumen merkityksestä elolliselle luonnolle. Marjakangas kertoo, kuinka elämä kietoutuu lumen ympärille talvella ja millä keinoin se muovaa luontoa.

Kirja on kokonaisesitys luonnon talvisesta elämästä Suomen lumisissa ympäristöissä. Se myös kuvaa talvien muuttumista ja sitä, miten talvien lämpeneminen ja lumiolojen muutokset vaikuttavat eliöihin.

”Teos on kirjoitettu yleistajuisesti kaikille talvisesta luonnosta kiinnostuneille”, Arto Marjakangas kertoo.

title: Immo Salonen appointed CEO of Liana
content:
Immo Salonen has been appointed the new CEO of Liana, taking up his position at the beginning of November 2026. In his new role, Salonen will also lead Profinder, both part of the Ilkka Group.

Salonen joins Liana from his role as CEO of Auntie Solutions. He has previously held leadership positions at companies including LINK Mobility, TietoEVRY and Giosg.

With Salonen’s appointment, Liana enters its next phase of growth with a continued focus on developing its marketing and communications technology offering, strengthening its international business and creating greater value for customers.

“Liana has a strong position in the market, with established customer relationships, talented people and a strong technology offering. I see significant potential to build on these strengths and accelerate international growth. At the same time, closer cooperation with Profinder creates opportunities to combine complementary expertise in technology, data and marketing,” says Immo Salonen.

title: Internet Infrastructure Services Empower Deepfake Abuse, New Study Finds
content:
Abusive, sexually explicit deepfakes have only become easier to make and more widespread in the last nine years. Since we first covered deepfakes when they appeared in 2017, they’ve never been the stuff of dark web sites or shadowy networks. They're found on social media networks, through basic web searches, and on easily downloadable apps and accessible forums. 

The most prominent hosts of non-consensual, AI-generated imagery are supported by some of the biggest web infrastructure providers in the world, getting their hosting, email, advertising, and content management systems from these companies. A new study examines how providers like Cloudflare, Google, Proton, Namecheap, and WordPress help non-consensual imagery sites thrive. Despite years of knowledge about these wildly popular sites, big tech companies continue providing infrastructure services that prop up abuse imagery, even though their own terms of service often prohibit illegal and harmful content, the study claims.

title: Kyiv: When Night Phantoms Arrive in Daytime
content:
It’s truly terrifying to come under ballistic missile attack, but such strikes have a certain familiar logic in a city that’s been at war all these years. The alerts told you that something would happen, mostly at night. It would eventually end with the all-clear.

No longer. The rhythm has changed.

Great flocks of whining drones, their numbers swelled by new, jet-powered versions, arrive hour after hour, day and night. One swarm ends and another begins, with a gap that may be as short as 15 minutes. The old habits of wartime Kyiv, when we organized our day around a mostly predictable pattern of attacks, have been replaced. It is everywhere, all around and all at once.

This creates new pressures. Last week, I woke up with my son and waited for an air raid to end so I could take him to school. I drove him there and dropped him off. Almost immediately, the attack resumed.

A friend bringing her child to the same school wrote that a Shahed drone had fallen nearby. Then there were more. I knew something was being hit close to the school. So I drove back.

title: Will Canada become part of Europe? What von der Leyen’s initiative means for security
content:
Although Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney praised von der Leyen’s move when addressing the European Parliament the following day, diplomats speaking behind the scenes say they had not been warned and do not really understand what the status of an “associated member state” would actually mean. Closer ties with Canada are particularly important for Latvia, as Canada has been a leading NATO country deploying troops here to deter Russian aggression since 2014.

Foreign policy researcher Mārtiņš Vargulis says the new “association” could most easily be put into practice in the areas of security and defence production. Meanwhile, Latvia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs told Delfi that it supports deeper ties with Canada, particularly in the field of security, but that in order to formulate a specific Latvian position on the “association”, it is necessary to wait until the terms of such an arrangement are defined in greater detail.

title: Dutch Police Arrest Alleged Member of Hacking Group that Targeted FBI
content:
Dutch Police have announced the arrest of a 24-year-old alleged member of the cybercrime group ShinyHunters that has been responsible for a string of major data breaches, including the hacking of an FBI website last week.

In a statement Tuesday, police said that following the suspect's arrest last week that they found information on his laptop revealing that he was arranging two murders abroad. Police added that this alleged plot “is not related to the investigation into ShinyHunters.” The statement did not disclose the suspect's name. 

Addressing the ShinyHunters group directly in a video statement, , FBI's Cyber Division Assistant Director Brett Leatherman urged the hacking group to surrender to authorities. “To the remaining members of ShinyHunters: You’ve heard about the arrest of your colleague,” Leatherman said.

title: EU accused of hiding environmental impact of data centers
content:
The European Union has shielded data centers from public scrutiny about how much energy they use, according to a formal complaint filed Monday against the European Commission.

The complaint lodged this week by Lighthouse Reports, and first reported by POLITICO, accuses the EU executive of setting up rules keeping the public from seeing how much energy and water are used by individual data centers.

This comes as public opposition to power-hungry AI data centers grows across Europe, while energy prices rise.

Lighthouse Reports, a Netherlands-based non-profit conducting cross-border investigations of alleged government and corporate wrongdoing, accuses the Commission of building a “wall of silence” about energy consumption.

EU policymakers are determined “to deny or deter access to, and obfuscate understanding of, how data centers are performing,” reads the complaint filed under the Aarhus Convention, a legally binding international treaty that gives the public rights to information and participation in environmental decision-making.

title: The EU considers ChatGPT a search engine. But strict rules may miss its most important part
content:
ChatGPT has now been placed in the same regulatory category as Google and Bing in the European Union. At the end of August, the European Commission designated it as a so-called Very Large Online Search Engine (VLOSE). For OpenAI, this means an additional layer of obligations under the Digital Services Act (DSA).

The decision is primarily linked to ChatGPT’s web-search capabilities. The Commission considers ChatGPT a “hybrid” service: the chatbot answers users’ questions and can search the internet for information while doing so. Under the DSA, its search function therefore falls under the definition of an online search engine.

OpenAI reported an average of 159.1 million monthly active users in the EU over the six months to March 2026. That is more than three times the 45-million-user threshold above which the Commission can designate a service as a VLOSE.

Following the designation, OpenAI has four months to comply with the new rules. The additional obligations for VLOSEs should therefore apply to ChatGPT by January 2027 at the latest.

Among other things, OpenAI will have to monitor its algorithms more closely and better document and account for how sources are selected.

title: EPPO Indicts Two Polish Nationals in €100 Million Electronics VAT Fraud Scheme
content:
The European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) in Katowice has indicted two Polish nationals alleging that they were part of a cross-border VAT fraud and money laundering scheme involving more than 100 million euros ($113.58 million) in fraudulent invoices. The indictment is the first to stem from "Operation Escape Room," a broader investigation targeting an electronic device trading ring operating across Austria, Belgium, Germany, Latvia, the Netherlands, and Poland.

According to prosecutors, the network used hundreds of shell companies and fake invoices to conceal transactions, evade VAT, and claim illegal tax reimbursements. In addition to the fraudulent invoices in Poland, the scheme caused an estimated 47 million euros ($53.39 million) in unpaid VAT damage in Belgium and 22 million euros ($24.99 million) in the Netherlands. If convicted, the defendants face between seven and a half and 25 years in prison.

title: Two New Birds Louder Than Jackhammers Just Dropped
content:
Scientists have identified two new contenders for the world’s loudest bird—the bare-throated bellbird and the red-legged seriema—both of which can exceed 120 decibels, which is louder than a jackhammer, according to a study published on Tuesday in Evolution. 

These two bird species are now in the same league as the white bellbird, which shattered the record for loudest bird in 2019 after its bizarre call was first measured and reported by Jeff Podos, a professor in the department of biology at the University of Massachusetts Amherst. It’s worth taking a moment to listen to the bellbird’s otherworldly call, which the males unleash over their remote habitat in the northern Amazon rainforest.

In the new study, Podos and former UMass Amherst graduate student João C.T. Menezes report that the bare-throated bellbird and the red-legged seriema occupy the same decibel range as the white bellbird. It's tough to declare a clear winner among the three birds due to differences in measurement techniques and individual variations within each species.

title: Mali: Damning evidence of war crimes by state armed forces and Wagner Group personnel – new report
content:
• Killings of civilians during military joint operations
  • Civilians tortured to death in detention, others subjected to simulated drowning, beatings and electric shocks
  • Fulani, Arabs and Tuaregs targeted  

    • Members of Mali’s armed forces working together with personnel from the Wagner Group committed war crimes, including the murder and torture of civilians, during joint operations between 2023 and 2025, Amnesty International said in a new report.

    ‘No one is spared’: War crimes committed by the Malian army and foreign allied forces along the Mauritanian border documents the killings of at least 34 civilians in seven localities in Mali between June 2023 and December 2025, committed by the Malian armed forces (Forces armées maliennes – FAMa) and the Wagner Group (a Russian private military company active in Mali between late 2021 and June 2025).

    The report also documents other serious violations of international humanitarian law and international human rights law, such as torture, enforced disappearance, and the pillaging and destruction of civilian property.

title: The AI Financial Fault Line — Does China Enjoy an Edge?
content:
The US depends on private financing. Chipmakers and other tech leaders are leveraging their booming profits to invest in, guarantee, and otherwise finance customers. The Economist has even labeled NVIDIA the “central bank of AI.”

China uses a different model: state-led funds, state-run bank financing, local government investment vehicles, subsidized compute, and state coordination. 

Although the US private financing approach works well at the start of a capital-intensive build-out, it may come under stress during a downturn. If AI demand disappoints, chip prices fall faster than expected, or AI applications take longer to produce paying customers, the pain could spread fast and wide, hitting equipment sales, data center revenues, customer creditworthiness, and the value of the supplier’s equity stake.

China suffers its own debt and overcapacity risks. State-directed funds can create duplication and poor allocation; local governments already carry high debt burdens; and state banks may roll over weak projects rather than force rapid restructuring.

title: Philippines: Government must implement its human rights obligations on civic space
content:
CIVICUS, a global civil society alliance, urges President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to stop his assault on civic freedoms and to implement the government’s human rights obligations and commitments. More than four years since he came to power, the environment for civil society and activists continues to deteriorate as highlighted in a CIVICUS brief published today.

The civic space in the Philippines is rated as ‘repressed’ by the CIVICUS Monitor due to government’s continued failure to fulfil its human rights obligations under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR), which it ratified in 2007. The ICCPR imposes obligations to respect and protect civic freedoms, including freedoms of association, expression and peaceful assembly. These rights are also enshrined in the Philippines constitution

title: Afghans "Have Been the Victims" of U.S. Military, Taliban, Cartels & More for Decades: Nagieb Khaja
content:
Award-winning Danish Afghan journalist and filmmaker Nagieb Khaja’s most recent documentary, Winning Heart and Minds, is an investigation into what went wrong in the U.S.-led war in Afghanistan. In the film, Khaja travels to Musa Qala, the capital of the southern Helmand province. Danish and British troops had been deployed to Musa Qala in 2006 to defend their allies, the local police, against Taliban insurgents.

While urban areas benefited from U.S. occupation during the war, “Western forces allied themselves with forces that in rural Afghanistan were considered worse than the Taliban,” says Khaja. “The police forces and the warlords that were fighting side by side with American, Danish and British forces, they were drug cartels, they were ruthless criminals, they were rapists.”

title: Yhteisöveron alennus halutaan perua uusista havainnoista huolimatta
content:
Useat julkisuudessa kantansa ilmaisseet taloustutkijat näyttävät olevan sitä mieltä, että yhteisöveron lasku on väärää politiikka. Etlan mielestä alennus on tarpeellinen osa suurempaa kasvupakettia. Suosituksen suunta näyttää riippuvan siitä, kuinka laaja-alaisesti muutoksen vaikutukset otetaan huomioon, kirjoittaa Etla-kolumnissaan Aki Kangasharju.

Etla taitaa olla talouspolitiikan arviointineuvoston (2026) kanssa ainoa taho, joka on ilmaissut yhteisöveron alennuksen Suomeen sopivaksi politiikaksi.[1]

Kriitikot vetoavat tutkimuksiin[2], joiden mukaan yhteisöveron lasku ei nosta tarpeeksi yhteisöveron pohjaa. Toisin sanoen yhteisöveron alentaminen ei kannusta yrityksiä kasvamaan – ja sitä kautta lisäämään voittojaan riittävästi, jotta alemman yhteisöveroprosentin vaikutus verotuloihin kompensoituisi. Vaikutus kompensoituisi, jos voitot kasvaisivat niin paljon, että alemmasta prosentista huolimatta voitoista perittävän yhteisöveron tuottoa kertyisi valtiolle entiseen malliin.

title: Selvitys kartoittaa pohjoismaisten taideorganisaatioiden kriisinkestävyyttä
content:
Tuore selvitys Innovative models: A report on resilience in Nordic spaces for contemporary art kartoittaa erilaisten nykytaideorganisaatioiden toimintastrategioita Ruotsissa, Suomessa ja Tanskassa.

Pohjoismaissa toimivien nykytaideorganisaatioiden toimintaa ovat leimanneet viime vuosina kasvava taloudellinen epävarmuus, poliittiset muutokset ja muuttuvat rahoitusrakenteet. Frame Contemporary Art Finlandin, Bildkonst Sverigen ja Danish Association of Art Centresin yhteistyössä käynnistämä selvitys tutkii, miten alan toimijat kehittävät ja ylläpitävät kriisinkestävyyttään muutosten keskellä.

Tuore selvitys kokoaa yhteen kokemuksia ja esimerkkejä Ruotsista, Suomesta ja Tanskasta, jotka ilmentävät, miten taideinstituutiot sopeutuvat muuttuviin olosuhteisiin ja pohtivat uudelleen yhteiskunnallista rooliaan. Hanke on syntynyt myös tarpeesta vahvistaa vapaan, osallistavan ja demokraattisen kulttuuritoiminnan pohjoismaista perinnettä.

Raportti on suunnattu ensisijaisesti nykytaiteen organisaatioille ja instituutioille, mutta se tarjoaa tietoa ja näkökulmia myös sekä poliittisilla tasoilla että yksityisissä säätiöissä päätöksiä tekeville.

title: Vieraana Ida Yli-Mäenpää: ”Tulokset näkyvät, kun tekee tarpeeksi töitä”
content:
Kun Ida Yli-Mäenpää asteli kahdeksan vuotta sitten ulos Voice of Finlandin lavalta, hän uskoi läpimurron olevan lähellä. Pian ovia aukeaisi, yhteydenottoja satelisi ja ura lähtisi vauhdilla lentoon.

Hän odotti ja odotti – mutta lopulta oikein mitään ei tapahtunutkaan.

Pettymys jätti jälkensä, ja parikymppinen artistinalku alkoi epäillä itseään. Vaikka musiikki oli kulkenut mukana koko elämän ajan, yhtäkkiä jokin pidätteli Idaa.

”Jotenkin jäädyin. Ajattelin, että ehkä musta ei olekaan tähän. Pelkäsin epäonnistumista, ja se esti mua tavoittelemasta unelmiani.”

Ida kyllä jatkoi musiikin tekemistä satunnaisesti, mutta moni asia tuntui takkuavan.   

”En vaan yksinkertaisesti tehnyt tarpeeksi töitä, että asiat olisivat edenneet. Odotin, että joku tulee hakemaan mut kotoa.”

Vuonna 2023 Ida tunsi olevansa hukassa. Hän päätti, ettei halunnut enää jäädä odottamaan omaa vuoroaan.

Syntyi suunnitelma.

Ida alkoi ahkeroida videoita TikTokiin. Niiden avulla hän kasvattaisi sosiaalisen median kanavansa niin suuriksi, että joku musiikkialalta väistämättä huomaisi hänet.

”Halusin, että mulla on valmis yleisö siinä vaiheessa, kun alan julkaista musiikkia. Päätin, että näin myös tulee tapahtumaan.”

title: Censorship Regarding Genocide
content:
By Jan Servaes

BRUSSELS | 29 September 2026 (IDN) — During his speech to the UN General Assembly in New York on 24 September, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu used a visual aid. He displayed a pager resembling the devices used in the deadly pager attacks that Israel carried out in Lebanon in 2024.

An arrest warrant for ‘war crimes’ was issued against Netanyahu in 2024 by the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague; however, he has not yet been arrested.

In contrast, Palestinian leader Mahmoud Abbas had to address the General Assembly via video link that same day, as the United States had—for the second consecutive year—denied him a visa to attend the UN summit in person, violating obligations the US undertook under the host country agreement.

Abbas highlighted Israeli attacks on the operations of the UN agency for Palestinian refugees (UNRWA) in Jerusalem and the West Bank, stating that the undermining of the agency’s work has led to a severely deteriorated humanitarian situation in those areas. “What is the international community waiting for to protect the Palestinian people?” he asked.

title: Every Night Is Different: Ryley Walker on Preserving Live Music
content:
Ryley Walker says he’s flattered when people tape his live performances and post them on the Internet Archive. If he knows ahead of time, the 37-year-old singer-songwriter often puts their name on the guest list and invites them early for a sound check.

“I love when people come — either as a hobbyist or a professional — to record the show and make it available for everybody else to hear,” says Walker of his experimental/folk music. “My live shows have always been a bit dynamic with a lot of improvising. So, there’s different approaches every night to the music, and it’s cool that’s documented.”

Walker has 95 shows preserved on the Internet Archive dating back to 2017. The recordings are part of the Live Music Archive, a collection built over the past 20 years by volunteers and Internet Archive staff that now tops 300,000 recordings from more than 9,000 artists.

[See Walker’s online collection and his personal website]

“I don’t think taping the show and putting it on the internet for someone to listen to for free is like a lost sale or anything,” Walker said. “It’s been a net positive.” Indeed, the Los-Angeles based musician said the online exposure has attracted new fans.

title: Seela Sella oli lukioikäisenä kesätöissä kirjastossa
content:
Näyttelijä Seela Sella tasoittaa yhä lähikirjastossaan hyllyrivejä.

Luettiinko sinulle, kun olit lapsi?
”Luettiin paljon – mutta ei niinkään satuja, vaan runoja. Lausunta oli siihen aikaan muotia, ja jokaisessa juhlassa kuultiin aina joku lausuntanumero. Äitini oli loistava esiintyjä, ja hän lausui paljon. Minäkin olin usein mukana esiintymässä. Lausuin niitä runoja, joita äiti oli lukenut minulle. En tietenkään ymmärtänyt kaikkea, mutta äiti selitti aina, mistä runoissa oli kyse. Koetin lapsen eläytymiskyvyllä päästä mukaan tunnelmaan. Runoja oli silloin jo päässäni niin kuin nytkin.”

Millaisia ovat varhaiset kirjastomuistosi?
”Meidän kirjastossamme oli kirjastonhoitajana Annikki-niminen vanhempi rouva. Häneltä sai käydä kysymässä, mitä voisi lukea. Hän tiesi aina kaiken. Hän oli aivan ihana. Tuohon aikaan myytiin koottujen teosten kokonaisuuksia. Kirjaston palvelu oli puolestaan yksilöllistä. Siellä et ollut osa massaa, jolle myydään jotain pötkössä. Siellä mietittiin, mikä juuri sinua voisi kiinnostaa.”

title: BIOS-tutkimusyksikön Ville Lähde vastaa kiperiin kysymyksiin ilmastokriisistä
content:
1. Kritisoitte kirjassa yhden ­totuuden ympäristö­ajattelua, kuten sitä, että ongelmiin olisi olemassa vain yksi juurisyy. Miksi yksinkertaistaminen on vahingollista?

Yksinkertaistaminen on välttämätöntä, mutta se ei saa olla tyhmistävää ja paikoilleen jumittavaa. Ajattelu on toki helpompaa, jos katsoo maailmaa vain yhden teorian läpi. Ympäristökriisissä täytyy kuitenkin pitää mielessä monta totuutta yhtä aikaa ja suhteuttaa niitä toisiinsa.

2. Miten ympäristökriisi poikkeaa muista yhteiskunnallisista kriiseistä, jotka maailma on yrittänyt ratkaista?

Poliittinen mielikuvituksemme on tottunut tarkastelemaan oikeuksien, vapauksien ja tasa-arvon kaltaisia kysymyksiä, ja aineellisella maailmalla on ollut siinä vain sivurooli. Ympäristökriisi on ensimmäinen iso poliittinen kysymys, jossa aineellinen maailma vaikuttaa omalla painollaan koko ajan. Orjuuden vastaista kamppailua voitiin käydä satoja vuosia, ympäristökriisissä kamppailu muuttaa joka vuosi ­muotoaan.

3. Miten tulevaisuutta voi hahmottaa, kun historiastakaan ei voi ottaa oppia?

title: Oletko julkishallinnon asiantuntija? Luo kansainvälisiä kontakteja ja jaa osaamistasi EU:n TAIEX-yhteistyöllä
content:
Oletko kiinnostunut kansainvälisestä yhteistyöstä? Haluatko jakaa oman alasi parhaita käytäntöjä ja suomalaista osaamista maailmalla? Liity TAIEX-asiantuntijarekisteriin!

Euroopan komission lyhytkestoisen teknisen tuen ohjelma TAIEX tarjoaa suomalaisille julkisen hallinnon asiantuntijoille mahdollisuuden jakaa osaamista, oppia uutta ja luoda arvokkaita kansainvälisiä kontakteja.

Lyhytkestoiset asiantuntijatehtävät edistävät hyvää hallintoa EU:n kumppanimaissa, vahvistavat Suomen roolia kansainvälisenä toimijana ja tukevat virkahenkilöiden ammatillista kehitystä.

TAIEX-toiminnasta 60 prosenttia toteutetaan EU:n laajentumis- ja naapuruuspolitiikan alueilla, mutta yhteistyötä tehdään miltei kaikkialla maailmassa.

TAIEXin kautta rahoitettavien tapahtumien kesto on yleensä 2–5 päivää, ja niiden sisältö suunnitellaan yhteistyössä edunsaajamaan ja komission kanssa. Komissio rahoittaa esimerkiksi työpajoja, räätälöityjä koulutuksia edunsaajamaassa sekä kumppanimaiden asiantuntijoiden opintomatkoja EU-maihin.

title: New Norwegian online newspaper has strong ties to party with link to Russia
content:
The online media describes itself as independent, but the man behind it is a member of the FOR party, NORDIS partner Faktisk.no reports. 

Towards the end of May, a Facebook post published by Fred og Rettferdighet (FOR) leader Marielle Leraand appeared. In it, she said that a new online newspaper called “Perspektiv” had been launched in Norway and that she was impressed by the articles she had read.

Vladimir Fedorov is behind the website, and confirms that he considers himself a member of the FOR party. According to Fedorov, it is coincidental that several people on the website’s editorial team are party members.

“They are simply people who share the same views, but it has nothing to do with the party. It just means that we are moving in the same direction as them,” says Fedorov.

FOR became known to the Norwegian public ahead of the 2025 parliamentary election, when it ran an advertising campaign against Norway providing financial support for Ukraine’s defence against Russia. Norwegian billionaire Atle Berge, who has business interests in Russia, confirmed that he supported the party financially.

title: Trafigura Bought Venezuelan Gold in ‘Historic’ US Deal in March. It’s Still in Storage.
content:
Six months after the U.S. government announced it would begin gold imports from Venezuela following years of sanctions prevented the trade, the first major tranche of gold from the deal is still in storage, OCCRP has learned.

The gold is being held by commodities-trading giant Trafigura, which became the first international firm to take advantage of relaxed U.S. restrictions on purchasing Venezuelan gold in March, in what the White House touted as a “historic” deal.

"All gold Trafigura has purchased from Venezuela to-date is currently in storage, under Trafigura's control,” a Trafigura spokesperson told OCCRP in early September.

The firm declined to comment on why the gold had not been sold yet in the U.S., but experts said the hold-up could be related to supply-chain issues. Venezuelan gold is extracted from a lawless and violent region, and it may be difficult to meet U.S. requirements to show it has been produced ethically.

title: How to Explain Complicated Things
content:
You may remember a time when it was difficult to make it through the day without hearing someone cite a TED Talk. A major technological reason for that was streaming video’s new accessibility on practically everyone’s computer (especially those of people bored at work). A major cultural reason was there was a considerable demographic overlap between those who knew their way around the new video-sharing realms of the internet and those likely to want to hear a “thought leader” speak for eighteen minutes or less. Whether schools kill creativity, the mechanics of procrastination, what happens when you reply to spam e‑mail: these are just a few of the subjects that most aggressively captivated the minds of the suddenly large and chatty TED Talk audience of the late two-thousands and early twenty-tens.

Since those days, some of the most popular TED Talks ever given have undergone reputational re-evaluation. The robustness of the science undergirding Amy Cuddy’s “Your Body Language May Shape Who You Are” has been called into question, while Bill Gates’ “The Next Outbreak? We’re Not Ready,” from 2015, started to look a whole lot more prescient four or five years after it was uploaded.

title: Pedaalin matkassa Bolognaan ja Venetsiaan
content:
Torstaina pedaalilaiset aloittivat päivän tutustumalla 1560-luvulla rakennettuun Bolognan yliopiston vanhaan rakennukseen, jossa sijaitsee myös Anatominen teatteri. Osallistuimme yleiselle opastukselle, jolle olimme varanneet pääsyliput. Asiantunteva opas kuljetti meitä rakennuksen molemmissa kerroksissa, ja pääsimme kurkistamaan myös suljettujen ovien taakse. Rakennuksessa on toiminut kirjasto vuodesta 1838 lähtien.

Bolognan yliopisto on Euroopan vanhin yliopisto, ja sen historia ulottuu vuoteen 1088 saakka. Bologna on nykyäänkin vilkas yliopistokaupunki. Osa vanhasta yliopistorakennuksesta ja sen taideteoksista tuhoutui toisen maailmansodan pommituksissa. Osa taideaarteista onnistuttiin kuitenkin pelastamaan, ja erään huoneen tuhoutuneisiin freskoihin tutustuimme ennen pommituksia otettujen valokuvien avulla.

Kierrokseen kuulunut 1600-luvulla rakennettu Anatominen teatteri tuhoutui osittain pommituksissa, mutta se rakennettiin myöhemmin uudelleen. Pommituksilta säästyi esimerkiksi puisia veistoksia ja muita arvokkaita yksityiskohtia. Anatominen teatteri restauroitiin alkuperäistä ulkoasua kunnioittaen.

Osoite ja sijainti kartalla: Piazza Luigi Galvani, 1, 40124 Bologna

title: Tasavallan presidentti Alexander Stubbin puhe Luxemburgin valtiovierailun juhlapäivällisellä Suurherttuan palatsissa 29. syyskuuta 2026
content:
Puheen alkuperäinen kieli on englanti.

Muutosvarauksin

Teidän kuninkaalliset korkeutenne,
arvoisat ministerit,
arvoisat suurlähettiläät,
hyvät naiset ja herrat,
hyvät ystävät.

Tänne on aina yhtä hyvä palata. Aivan kuin tulisi kotiin.

Haluan aloittaa yksinkertaisella havainnolla: Suomi ja Luxemburg ovat ehkä pieniä maita, mutta emme ole koskaan ajatelleet pienesti. Historiamme, taloutemme ja asemamme Euroopassa osoittavat, että kun maailma muuttuu, me mukaudumme nopeasti ja tartumme avautuviin mahdollisuuksiin.

Tänään haluaisin puhua kolmesta meitä yhdistävästä asiasta: ensinnäkin kyvystämme muuntautua; toiseksi, siitä miten olemme sitoutuneet Eurooppaan ja monenkeskiseen yhteistyöhön; ja kolmanneksi, ihmisten välisistä siteistä, jotka yhdistävät maitamme.

Aloitetaan muuntautumiskyvystämme.

Suomella ja Luxemburgilla on epätavallinen historiallinen yhteys: Luxemburg on suurherttuakunta ja Suomi oli aikoinaan suuriruhtinaskunta. Luxemburg on säilyttänyt valtiomuotonsa, kun taas Suomi valitsi eri tien, ja meistä tuli tasavalta.

title: “A Massive Power Grab”: White House Proposal Threatens Funding That Helps Disabled Americans Vote
content:
Without Amy Miller, some elderly and disabled people wouldn’t be able to vote.

The attorney for Disability Rights Nebraska travels the state, investigating the quality of nursing homes and assisted living facilities. As she reminds the residents how they can report abuse or neglect, she also offers voter registration forms. Last month, she helped a veteran with a traumatic brain injury fill out change-of-address paperwork so he could vote in the upcoming midterm elections. “He 100% knew who he wanted to vote for,” Miller said, but he struggled to write with a pen.

Learn more about this story on ProPublica’s podcast “Paper Trail.”

Congress funds her organization’s efforts to ensure that even people who might not have access to the internet or transportation have the opportunity to participate in elections.

Now a White House proposal threatens that work.

title: Suomen Kulttuurirahaston apurahahaku lokakuussa
content:
Suomen Kulttuurirahaston apurahojen hakuaika lähestyy. Uudistetussa hakumenettelyssä sekä maakuntarahastojen että keskusrahaston apurahoja haetaan yhdessä valtakunnallisessa haussa. Erillistä maakuntarahastojen Tammikuun hakua ei enää jatkossa ole.

Kulttuurirahaston haussa myönnetään yhteensä 44,2 miljoonaa euroa apurahoina tieteelle, taiteelle ja kulttuurille. Summa vastaa viime vuoden hauissa yhteensä myönnettyä euromäärää. Apurahoja voi hakea valtakunnallisessa haussa 15.–30.10.2026. Hakuaika päättyy viimeisenä hakupäivänä klo 16 Suomen aikaa.

Lähikulttuuri-apurahoilla tuetaan kotiseutujen paikalliskulttuuri- ja kulttuuriperintöhankkeita. Apuraha kulki aiemmin nimellä Kotiseututyö, ja se oli haettavana maakuntarahastojen Tammikuun haussa.

Apurahaa voi hakea tieteelliseen tai taiteelliseen työskentelyyn sekä hankkeisiin ja hankintoihin. Hakea voivat suomalaiset tai Suomessa asuvat tai toimivat henkilöt ja yhteisöt. Hakea voi myös, jos hakemuksella on selkeä, vahva yhteys Suomeen tai suomalaiseen kulttuuriin.

title: Ny bok: Historiska och litteraturhistoriska studier 101
content:
SLS årsbok Historiska och litteraturhistoriska studier (HLS) 101 har temat rörelse.

HLS 101 öppnar ett brett perspektiv på rörelser med texter av åtta skribenter. I ett par av bidragen behandlas arbetarrörelsen och den finlandssvenska samlingsrörelsen, medan transnationella perspektiv på rörelse öppnas i texter om Larin-Kyösti som svensk och finsk poet och den provensalska rörelsen. Andra artiklar handlar om rörelse i det konstnärliga arbetet: om taktpinnens svepande rörelser i körledarens hand och om rörelsen genom Tove Janssons manuskript. Vi får också läsa om hur ett brev av lantmätare Theodor Mollin inspirerade J.L. Runebergs skildring av Saarijärvi. I numret ingår även Kristina Malmios festtal från SLS årshögtid, om den finlandssvenska romanens kraft, och ett minnesord till Ann-Marie Ivars.

Medverkande: Robin Chouleur, Pia Forssell, Matias Kaihovirta, Christa Lundström, Juhani Niemi, Kristina Malmio, Christoffer Sundman och Sakari Ylivuori. Medverkande i minnesordet: Mona Forsskåhl, Charlotta af Hällström-Reijonen, Pirkko Nuolijärvi, Caroline Sandström, Marika Tandefelt, Camilla Wide & Jan-Ola Östman.

title: Andy Burnham keeps his options open on Brexit
content:
LIVERPOOL, England — Andy Burnham pledged to undertake the most ambitious review of Brexit since Britain left the EU.

But for now at least, he’s keeping all his options open.

Speaking at his party’s annual conference in Liverpool on Tuesday, the U.K. prime minister said the current plans to improve the Brexit settlement struck by the last Conservative government were “not enough” and that leaving the bloc had done “more harm than good.”

But Burnham didn’t pledge an immediate fix.

Instead, the newly-installed British PM said he would lay out “what I believe the different options are for Britain’s long-term relationship with our European partners” at a U.K.-EU summit later this year.

“And there are different options,” he said. “I will see if we can find consensus around one, which will give us clarity about our position and the future of the continent that we live in.”

title: How American political campaigns are using AI – and what they’re spending on the tools
content:
Though politicians are quiet about how they use AI, the book Rewiring Democracy examines how AI is starting to influence American politics

New campaign finance disclosure data shines a light on which US political campaigns are using AI tools and how much they are spending on them.

Candidates’, parties’ and committees’ spending reveals that AI is fast becoming an essential tool of politics. The candidates themselves are quiet about how they are using the technology in their own campaigns. It’s a sensitive issue that we have been tracking closely since we started writing our book, Rewiring Democracy, which examined how AI is beginning to influence politics. A September 2025 Pew survey of Americans found that more than 70% would think less of a candidate if they used AI to help write a speech.

title: How World Trade Organization reform could help address the EU-China trade imbalance
content:
The world was closely watching the high-stakes US-China summit in Washington from September 23 – 25, which resulted in the US and China agreeing, among other things, to extend their trade truce by two months. Now, the spotlight has shifted to Beijing, as the EU and China enter the final stretch ahead of a decisive round of trade talks seeking to remedy export/import imbalances. On October 8 and 9, trade negotiators from both sides will gather in Beijing for the second meeting of the newly established EU-China Trade and Investment Consultations Mechanism (TIC).

The TIC was launched in June this year, marking a significant step for both sides in restoring an institutional channel for dialogue on trade and investment after a period of relatively limited engagement. The forthcoming meeting is therefore more than a routine round of talks. It will be the first real test facing the new TIC: whether it is useful in stabilising EU-China relations and pulling the two back from the brink of a looming trade war. It is far too early to tell. What is already clear, however, is that some of the most difficult and pressing issues are on the negotiating table.

title: The ‘WarGames’ problem: Computer science has long understood what it takes to keep AI under control
content:
AI agents don’t go rogue. That’s something only humans do.

Nevertheless, a New York Times article – representative of much news coverage of AI – described an OpenAI hacking as “A.I. bots going rogue and independently spearheading a cyberattack.”

Name-brand artificial intelligence agents have been on a hacking spree in 2026. OpenAI’s software agents hacked software company Hugging Face and government sites, Anthropic’s Claude hacked four companies’ systems, and in cybersecurity experiments Google’s Gemini hacked three companies.

The AI companies are investigating tens of thousands of incidents involving their agents, according to a report in Axios. These episodes have heightened fears about AI agents taking actions without human prompting.

The problem with headlines proclaiming that AI agents have gone rogue goes beyond anthropomorphizing the technology. It creates the impression that the agents were beyond the control of the AI companies that made them and there was little the companies could do about it.
snippet: AI agents don’t go rogue. That’s something only humans do.

title: Are Libraries Prepared for the Second Digital Transformation of Distinctive Collections?
content:
Academic and research libraries, as well as public libraries, historical societies, and other organizations, hold extensive collections of rare and unique materials, such as archival and manuscript collections. These materials form an essential part of humanity’s cultural and historical record, and they are the vital source material for many humanistic fields. I believe that a second digital transformation is at hand for distinctive collections. How can library leaders establish a strategy for their distinctive collections that is fit for purpose today?

The world faces a “narrowing window” to restore forests essential for food security and resistance to the climate emergency, a United Nations report has warned.

title: Ouluun tuleva tieteidenvälinen instituutti ratkoo monimutkaisia yhteiskunnallisia ongelmia
content:
Oulun yliopisto perustaa uuden tieteidenvälisen instituutin, jonka tarkoituksena on vahvistaa eri tieteenalojen sekä tutkimuksen ja muun yhteiskunnan välistä yhteistyötä.

Integra-niminen instituutti kokoaa yhteen tutkijoita, opiskelijoita ja yhteiskunnan eri toimijoita kehittämään uusia tapoja tarkastella ja ratkaista monimutkaisia yhteiskunnallisia haasteita.

"Aikamme merkittävimmät haasteet eivät noudata tieteenalojen rajoja. Siksi myöskään ratkaisut eivät synny yksittäisen tieteenalan sisältä. Tieteidenvälinen yhteistyö on välttämättömyys, jos haluamme löytää uusia ja vaikuttavia ratkaisuja yhteiskunnan suuriin kysymyksiin", tutkimuksesta vastaava vararehtori Matti Latva-aho sanoo Oulun yliopiston tiedotteessa.

Instituutin tavoitteena on tuoda yhteen eri tieteenalojen osaamista sekä yliopiston ulkopuolisia toimijoita. Tarkoituksena on kehittää ja testata uusia ideoita, menetelmiä ja ratkaisuja sekä edistää niiden käyttöönottoa.

Samalla yliopisto pyrkii synnyttämään tutkimushankkeita, jotka ylittävät perinteisiä tieteenala- ja organisaatiorajoja. Tutkimuksella halutaan tuottaa tietoa muun muassa kestävän hyvinvoinnin, kilpailukyvyn ja yhteiskunnan uudistumiskyvyn tueksi.

title: Uusi Eettisen kehityssanaston opas suosittelee välttämään kehitysapu-termiä
content:
Fingon ja sen jäsenjärjestöjen laatima Eettisen kehityssanaston opas muistuttaa, että sanat ovat valtaa – ne muovaavat ihmisten käsityksiä maailmasta ja rakentavat todellisuutta. Opas kehottaa luopumaan muun muassa kehitysapu-termistä.

Jaa

Suomalaisten kehitysjärjestöjen kattojärjestö Fingo on julkaissut Eettisen kehityssanaston oppaan, joka tarkastelee kansainvälisen kehityksen parissa käytettäviä termejä kriittisellä silmällä.

Oppaassa pohditaan esimerkiksi seuraavia kysymyksiä: Millaista todellisuutta sanat luovat? Minkälaisia valta-asetelmia niihin liittyy? Onko termien kuvailema tarina rehellinen ja reilu? Kenen näkökulmaa ne peilaavat?

Oppaassa käydään läpi yhteensä yli 50 ilmausta. Ne luokitellaan kolmeen kategoriaan: 1) Lakkaamme käyttämästä (9 kpl), 2) Herättävät kysymyksiä (10 kpl) ja 3) Vaihtoehtoinen ilmaisutapa (36 kpl).

Eettisen kehityssanaston opas kehottaa esimerkiksi välttämään käsitettä kehitysapu.

”Kehitysapu-termi ei kuvasta todellisuutta rehellisesti. Termi rakentaa tarinaa aktiivisesta auttajasta ja passiivisemmasta avunsaajasta. Todellisuudessa kehitysyhteistyötä tehdään sananmukaisesti nimenomaan yhteistyössä”, oppaassa perustellaan.

title: Surveillance Finds a Way
content:
A thing I’ve been saying over and over is that surveillance companies can’t be trusted to regulate themselves or to make privacy decisions themselves, because one company’s red line is another company’s business opportunity. Today we’re investigating a company that saw Flock was not offering facial recognition and saw a challenge.

Also: Some dudes are letting ChatGPT drive a car in a parking lot in San Francisco, a data center company promises to cut people big checks if their data center gets approved, and the Muse backlash has begun. Welcome back to our new experiment with daily newsletters. If you like this, subscribe here. -Jason

As Flock continues to be the center of a nationwide conversation about automatic license plate reading cameras, the company has said that it doesn’t, and won’t, do facial recognition: “We will not add facial recognition to our devices,” Flock CEO Garrett Langley said in a recent video. But other, third-party companies are telling cops that they are willing to add facial recognition to data gathered by Flock cameras in order to “close that gap.”

title: "Buying More Time for the Genocide": Muhammad Shehada on Trump's Gaza Plan 1 Year Later
content:
The Palestinian death toll from Israel’s war on Gaza has surpassed 74,000, according to the Ministry of Health in Gaza. While this figure represents the official death toll as confirmed by local authorities, the true number could be much higher when missing people and indirect deaths are taken into account, such as from disease, exposure, denial of medical treatment and the destruction of civic infrastructure. And since the so-called ceasefire brokered by Trump last October, nearly 1,400 Palestinians have been killed in Israeli attacks.

“The [ceasefire] plan ended up just buying more time for the genocide,” says Muhammad Shehada, a writer and analyst from Gaza speaking to Democracy Now! in Copenhagen. “Instead of suspending attacks on Gaza, Israel has been bombing Gaza every day.”

“The idea of the plan was to divide the reconstruction, rehabilitation, Israeli withdrawal, decommissioning of Hamas and Palestinian statehood into three phases,” says Shehada. “So far, only one item of the 20 items on the Trump plan has been fulfilled, and that is the release of every single Israeli hostage in Gaza.”

title: When the right to protest remains, but demonstrating comes at a price
content:
Climate activists are particularly vulnerable to arrest and persecution

Originally published on Global Voices

A climate protest in Copenhagen. Image from Flickr. CC BY-NC-ND 2.0.

This post is part of Global Voices’ September 2026 Spotlight series, “Protest in Democracy.” With this Spotlight, we seek to explore the many forms of protest, the tactics states use to delegitimize and suppress them, and the complex relationship between protest and democracy. You can support this coverage by donating here.

Across Europe, governments are using criminal laws against climate and environmental protesters — a phenomenon that shows few signs of retreating. A comparative study published in late 2025, examining 14 countries across the Global North and South, found that criminalization forms part of a wider pattern of repression. Researchers identified not only arrests, but new anti-protest laws, the strategic use of existing laws and legal processes, surveillance, harassment, and the public vilification of activists.

title: Iraqi Lawmaker Sentenced to 7 Years, Fined $21 Million for Illicit Enrichment
content:
An Iraqi court has sentenced sitting lawmaker Mohammed Farman Shaher to seven years in prison for illicit enrichment, ordering him to pay the equivalent of over $21.4 million in restitution and fines, according to legal authorities.

Shaher was ordered to repay 11.8 billion Iraqi dinars ($9.01 million) and $1.73 million in illicit gains, alongside an equivalent fine.

Shaher, who was arrested on June 28, serves on parliament’s Oil and Gas Committee. He is a member of the Sunni Taqaddum Party, led by former parliament speaker Mohammed al-Halbousi and home to current speaker Haibat al-Halbousi.

title: Mick Jagger Tells the Story Behind ‘Gimme Shelter’ and Merry Clayton’s Haunting Background Vocals
content: In the fall of 1969 the Rolling Stones were in a Los Angeles recording studio, putting the final touches on their album Let It Bleed. It was a tumultuous time for the Stones. They had been struggling with the album for the better part of a year as they dealt with the personal disintegration of their founder and multi-instrumentalist Brian Jones, whose drug addiction and personality problems had reached a critical stage. Jones was fired from the band in June of that year. He died less than a month later. And although the Stones couldn’t have known it at the time, the year would end on another catastrophic note, as violence broke out at the notorious Altamont Free Concert just a day after Let It Bleed was released.

title: EU to Trump: We will keep pushing for global AI safety rules
content:
The European Commission will continue to seek an international agreement on AI security, despite U.S. resistance, EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen said Tuesday.

“The U.S. has been very public saying they don’t want to have international regulation … because they have concerns that it’s hindering innovation,” Virkkunen said on the stage of the RAID Conference in Brussels in response to questions by POLITICO.

U.S. President Donald Trump has brushed away concerns about AI existential risks as a “hoax,” and declared his opposition to global regulations. The EU takes a different view, having offered its support for last week’s initiative for an international safety body to monitor AI led by Finland and Norway, and signed by 20 other countries.

“We have a different approach because we think that, if you are regulating in a pro-innovation manner, it’s also a good basis for innovation that people have trust in those technologies,” said Virkkunen, the EU Commissioner responsible for technology.

She praised the EU’s landmark 2024 AI Act as a strong regulatory basis for tackling challenges posed by AI bots.
snippet: The European Commission will continue to seek an international agreement on AI security, despite U.S. resistance, EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen said Tuesday.
