title: Mac mini M6 review: truly mighty but now more pricey
content:
Apple’s cheapest desktop computer is no longer a bargain but its newest, fastest chip makes it a pocket powerhouse

Apple’s latest Mac mini brings real speed and power for far more than everyday tasks in a practically pocketable form you can fit almost anywhere.

The impressive new desktop machine is the first to receive an update to Apple’s latest M6 chip while remaining smaller than a headphones box. It is the cheapest computer Apple sells with an M-series chip, but like every other memory-containing piece of electronics, it has been hit by RAMageddon, driving up the starting price to £899 (€1,049/$899/A$1,449) from the £599 or equivalent of its M4 predecessor.

title: How do Denmark and the UK compare when it comes to alcohol and drinking habits?
content:
For decades, Denmark and the UK have been known as countries where alcohol plays a big role in people’s social lives. In this way, the two countries make an interesting comparison when it comes to alcohol consumption because they both have a strong drinking culture.

For years, Denmark has appeared near the top of European rankings for teenage alcohol use, with Danish teenagers consistently reporting higher levels of drinking than their peers in much of Europe — including the UK.

Binge drinking has historically been a particular concern in the UK, especially among young adults. But drinking habits have changed substantially since the 2000s, with the proportion of UK adults who reported binge drinking in the previous week falling from around 18% in 2005 to 15% in 2013.

In England, around 21% of adults drank more than 14 units of alcohol per week in 2024. This is equivalent to roughly six pints of average-strength beer or seven standard (175ml) glasses of wine. Denmark shows similar drinking rates.

title: How sugar from outer space became one of the backbones of life on Earth
content:
Is there life elsewhere, or is Earth unique in the universe? This is one of humanity’s great unanswered questions.

One way to approach this mystery is to investigate how life began here on Earth. Our research explores the conditions where a mixture of molecules somehow transformed from chemistry into biology.

In a new study published in Scientific Reports, we shed new light on one possible step in this process: how a fragile sugar from outer space may have helped create the conditions for its own survival on Earth, where it eventually became the backbone of one of life’s most important molecules.

Scientists think life arose from a complex mixture of water, minerals and carbon-containing molecules: the proverbial primordial soup. These mixtures may have been in oceans, lakes or hot springs. They would have been shaped by changing temperatures, flowing water, mineral surfaces and evaporation, creating conditions in which increasingly complex chemistry could develop.

title: Vihreät nuoret esittää Suomeen päihdehoitotuomioistuinta
content:
Vihreät nuoret esittää Suomeen päihdehoitotuomioistuinta ihmisille, joiden rikoskierteen taustalla on päihderiippuvuus.

Ehdotusta perustellaan päihdeongelmien ja rikosten uusimisen vahvalla yhteydellä. Järjestön tiedotteen mukaan 87 prosentilla Suomen vangeista on todettu elinaikainen päihteiden käyttöhäiriö. Useamman kerran vankilassa olleista päihdehäiriö on todettu 91 prosentilla. Lisäksi noin puolet käräjäoikeudessa tuomituista henkilöistä on rikoksenuusijoita.

"Olisi aika kysyä, puutummeko uusintarikollisuudessa syyhyn vai vain sen oireisiin. Päihderiippuvuus ratkaistaan hoidolla ja avulla, ei vankilalla", Vihreiden nuorten puheenjohtaja Maria Saita kommentoi tiedotteessa.

"Mitä jos rikoskierteen taustalla oleva riippuvuus hoidettaisiin ennen rankaisemista?" Saita kysyy.

Esitetty päihdehoitotuomioistuin perustuisi kansainväliseen Alcohol and Other Drug Treatment Court -malliin. Rikoksesta syylliseksi todettu henkilö voisi ennen rangaistuksen määräämistä hakeutua vapaaehtoisesti intensiiviseen hoito- ja kuntoutusohjelmaan. Ohjelman onnistunut suorittaminen voisi johtaa lievempään rangaistukseen.

title: Greenland Deal: Trump Drops Threat to Annex Denmark Territory in Favor of Greater U.S. Military Role
content:
After months of threatening to take over Greenland by force, President Trump last week signed a 10-page agreement with Greenland and Denmark that bolsters the U.S. military presence on the mineral-rich and strategically located island but falls short of his earlier demands to make it American territory. Under the 1951 Defense of Greenland Treaty, the United States already has wide latitude to station forces and build military bases in Greenland. The U.S. currently has one active military base and around 160 troops on the ground. Under the new agreement, signed shortly after President Trump’s speech to the United Nations General Assembly last week, the U.S. can build two new bases. The deal keeps Greenland as part of Denmark and would still apply if Greenland chooses independence.

“In many ways, the deal is good, because the right for self-determination is approved,” says Julie Rademacher, chair of Uagut, the national organization for Greenlanders in Denmark. At the same time, “after threats [for] one-and-a-half years to annex Greenland, we don’t have the same faith or the same trust in Americans and the U.S. president.”

title: Seven Arrested in Massive EU Fraud Scheme Selling Used Phones as New
content:
An international law enforcement operation led by the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) resulted in the arrests of seven people, including two alleged ringleaders, to dismantle a criminal network suspected of selling more than one million used mobile phones as new, the EPPO announced Tuesday. The cross-border crackdown, code-named "Troja," involved more than 1,700 officers conducting over 160 searches across 19 countries. Authorities estimate the scheme defrauded European Union consumers of at least 300 million euros ($340 million) and caused 30 million euros ($34 million) in value-added tax (VAT) losses.

According to prosecutors, the syndicate assembled phones from used components in Hong Kong and the United Arab Emirates. The devices were then shipped through the Netherlands to warehouses in Germany, where they were cleaned, packaged, and sold on online marketplaces to unsuspecting customers across the EU as brand-new products.

title: ‘Do better for Australia’: OpenAI apologizes for unauthorized access
content:
CANBERRA — OpenAI has apologized to Australia for unauthorized access to Medicare statistical data by its agents and its handling of the incident, promising to do better and rebuild trust with the Australian public.

OpenAI broke its silence about the June incident, which it described as artificial intelligence models accessing Australian government websites “in ways they were not authorized to do” during internal training and evaluation.

“We are sorry and working to do better in the future,” OpenAI said in a statement.

“This is a new kind of cyber incident which represents an emerging global challenge. One of the ways we intend to take accountability for the situation is to be intentional in working with Australia to help develop practical approaches to how AI developers and governments identify, disclose, and respond to AI cyber behavior, whether malicious or unintentional.”

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese responded to the apology Tuesday, saying he had a “direct but constructive discussion” with OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman. “OpenAI have been very constructive and open … and I welcome that.”

title: Why Europe wants to boost its Arctic presence
content:
EU leaders gathered in northern Finland recently for a summit focused on reaffirming the importance of the Arctic region to European security. The meeting, which took place in the city of Rovaniemi, came a month before the EU is expected to release its updated Arctic policy.

This will be the first update since 2021, during which time the geopolitical climate has undergone considerable change. After Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, for example, the work of the Arctic Council was put on hold.

The seven other Arctic states had previously used this forum to engage with Moscow directly, using it to exchange information and promote cooperation on issues such as environmental protection and development in the region.

Russia has stepped up its military, economic and strategic activities in the region over the intervening years.

On September 10, it was reported that a joint operation between the UK, US and Norway earlier in 2026 successfully disrupted Russian vessels simulating the deployment of a weapon designed to disable undersea cables near the remote Norwegian archipelago of Svalbard.

title: Ethiopia is sliding back toward war – a look at what is driving the fighting and why it matters
content:
Four years after a fragile ceasefire ended widespread conflict in Ethiopia, the region is again slipping back into full-out war.

On Sept. 23, 2026, advancing soldiers of the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) seized government positions in northern Ethiopia.

It followed the announcement of a new alliance of seven armed movements in opposition to the Ethiopian government and deteriorating relations between the country and neighboring Eritrea, which it accuses of supporting the new alliance.

As an expert on conflict in the Horn of Africa and Ethiopian national security, I know the spiraling conditions now have been long in the making. The November 2022 Pretoria Cessation of Hostilities Agreement ended immediate fighting between Ethiopia and Tigrayan rebels, but it did not constitute a comprehensive peace settlement. Crucially, it was never followed by wider political negotiations to address the root causes of the war. The concern now is that the conflicts will intersect with the civil war in neighboring Sudan, causing a complicated, regionwide conflagration.
snippet: Four years after a fragile ceasefire ended widespread conflict in Ethiopia, the region is again slipping back into full-out war.

title: Lithuanian Mayor Found Guilty in Expense Fraud Case
content:
A Lithuanian court has found Prienai district Mayor Alvydas Vaicekauskas guilty of abuse of office, fraud, and document forgery over false expense claims he submitted while serving as a municipal councilor. The Alytus District Court fined him 7,500 euros ($8,800) and barred him for three years from holding elected or appointed public office once the judgment becomes final.

Investigators found that between 2019 and 2023 Vaicekauskas submitted 17 expense reports containing false information about fuel purchases purportedly related to his council work, in some cases using bank cards belonging to other people. Prosecutors said he improperly obtained about 1,113 euros from the municipality.

The ruling can be appealed within 20 days. His lawyer, Audrius Pėstininkas, told OCCRP the defense would appeal the verdict. “We did not find in the judgment answers to the questions raised by the defense, and naturally we still do not understand which legal act or procedure A. Vaicekauskas violated, or where the court saw document forgery or deception in his actions,” he said.

title: How can the same El Niño cause drought in one part of the world and floods in another?
content:
The Pacific Ocean is warming unusually quickly, and this year’s El Niño has already surpassed previous records. Forecasters expect it to strengthen even further before approaching its usual peak around December.

El Niño, the warm phase of a natural fluctuation in the Earth’s climate system, can reshape weather thousands of miles away, bringing drought to some regions while increasing the risk of heavy rain and flooding in others. To understand why, you need to follow what happens to the Pacific’s warm water – and the air above it.

Usually, winds over the tropical Pacific blow from east to west, pushing warm surface water towards the western Pacific, where it piles up around Indonesia and nearby regions. These are the trade winds. As warm water moves westward, colder water from deeper in the ocean rises to replace it in the east — a process called upwelling. This is why the western Pacific is usually much warmer than the eastern Pacific.

title: OCCRP Partner Siraj Wins 2026 Samir Kassir Award
content:
The Samir Kassir Award for Freedom of the Press has named Ali Al-Ibrahim, co-director of OCCRP member center Siraj, and Syrian investigative journalist Mais Katt as joint winners in its investigative reporting category. The award recognizes  their September 2025 cross-border investigative project, “Syria’s Stolen Children: How the Assad Regime Turned Detainees’ Children into Hostages Between Intelligence Agencies and Orphanages.” 

Published a year ago following the fall of Bashar al-Assad in late 2024, the investigation documents how officials from al-Assad’s security services abducted hundreds of Syrian children of political detainees and hid them inside children’s charities in order to coerce and intimidate their families. The investigation exposed the complicity of several care institutions, including facilities run by the major European charity SOS Children’s Villages, whose leadership knew about the abuses for years and remained silent.

The Samir Kassir Award, which has been presented by the E.U. since 2006, selected the investigation from 194 submissions across 11 countries in North Africa, the Middle East and the Gulf.

title: US tech leaders are urgently calling for rules on AI – China already has them
content:
Recent warnings from American AI leaders have created the impression that the world is only beginning to confront the dangers of advanced artificial intelligence.

Dario Amodei, chief executive of tech company Anthropic, has called for governments to intervene to slow the development of increasingly powerful AI models.

His proposal begins with independent evaluators embedded inside AI companies, moves on to regulation and progresses to government-backed coordination among democratic states.

Ultimately, it seeks global agreements with China on testing of AI systems, dangerous applications of the technology and the pace of AI development.

Yet there is a China-shaped hole in this narrative. The Asian superpower is portrayed as the difficult final participant in a governance system that the US and its allies must first create.

In fact, China has already established an extensive system of AI rules, assessment, filing, technical standards and government oversight. Here’s how China’s AI governance system has developed in stages alongside the technology itself.
snippet: Recent warnings from American AI leaders have created the impression that the world is only beginning to confront the dangers of advanced artificial intelligence.

Die Aktuatoren des Roboters sind auf Klemmen montiert und ermöglichen den Benutzer*innen die Befestigung an unterschiedlichsten Oberflächen, Objekten und Instrumenten. Sie werden über MIDI oder Software wie Ableton Live gesteuert.

title: Analysis: Lula presidency saved at least 20,000km2 of Brazilian Amazon since 2022
content:
• ‘Brazil is back’
  • New Jersey-sized forest
  • Election significance
  • ‘Greenest’ policies 
  • Soy moratorium and Brazilian congress

    • An area of Amazon forest roughly the size of the US state of New Jersey has remained standing due to Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s leadership of Brazil, according to Carbon Brief analysis. 

    Lula beat Jair Bolsonaro in the 2022 election to become president of the nation that is home to nearly 60% of the Amazon rainforest. 

    Forest loss surged during Bolsonaro’s far-right presidency and dropped sharply under the left-wing Lula, with Amazon deforestation likely to hit its lowest level on record this year. 

    Now, as another presidential election approaches, Lula is facing off against Bolsonaro’s son, Flávio Bolsonaro, whose “anti-environmental” policies are similar to his father’s.

    Carbon Brief’s analysis suggests that at least 20,000 square kilometres (km2) of deforestation has been avoided since Lula took office and prioritised Amazon protection.

    The analysis is based on modelling by an international research team of an alternative scenario in which Brazil’s flagship forest code legislation was not enforced – a proxy for Jair Bolsonaro’s leadership.

title: Europe’s Gigafactory Miracle — or Mirage?
content:
The European Commission wants to spend up to €10 billion in public funds on seven gigafactories, data centers full of cutting-edge AI chips designed to help European researchers, startups, public services, and industrial firms catch up in the AI race.

It’s a good idea to accelerate access to AI compute. But the gigafactory agenda risks reviving a damaging European instinct: equating sovereignty with self-sufficiency and treating imported technology as evidence of strategic failure.

Gigafactories will be consumers of chips, not manufacturers of them. European gigafactories will use imported GPUs, not create a European GPU, foundry, packaging ecosystem, or AI software stack. The “gigafactories” label blurs compute infrastructure with semiconductor production and creates false expectations.

title: COST Action Blog: What is prayer?
content:
What is prayer?

This blog was written by the COST Action PRAYTICIPATE.

For centuries, prayer has played a central role in shaping worldviews, education and formation, religious experience, community life, and the organisation of everyday life across Europe. Yet, despite the “religious turn” in the humanities, prayer is still often treated as an ordinary or self-evident practice. This has limited our understanding of its complex and varied histories in the late medieval and early modern worlds. At the same time, the remarkable plurality of prayer practices is reflected in fragmented scholarship across disciplines and regions.

By approaching prayer as a participatory practice, social, communal, embodied, and mediated through material objects and media, the COST Action PRAYTICIPATE together with its strong international research network, seeks to develop a more comprehensive understanding of this widespread and multifaceted practice.

Reconsidering its vocabulary through objects

What is prayer?

title: Europe grows its network of experts in cultural heritage risk preparedness
content:
24 heritage professionals began their training in cultural heritage risk preparedness in June 2026 as part of a second group of specialists coming from 19 countries participating in the Creative Europe programme.

The training provided by the READY project involved two weeks of online learning followed by ten days of in-person training in Bucharest this September.

The new cohort joins the 24 professionals trained during the project's first year, forming a growing network dedicated to heritage risk management. In doing so, they have also built the knowledge and partnerships needed to protect heritage sites and associated living traditions from complex and cascading risks.

The training strengthens the ability of heritage professionals to safeguard immovable heritage and living traditions amid growing disaster risks, climate extremes and conflict. The participants developed practical skills and tools to assess and reduce disaster risk, improve emergency preparedness, coordinate cultural heritage first aid, and support early recovery.

While we have 1.5 years left of the current EU programme period, the preparatory work for the post-2027 period is in full swing. Authorities are currently mapping the needs to enable the definition of the most relevant thematic focus areas for the funding programmes. The EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region Action Plan provides a solid starting point for the needs assessments.

Over the autumn of 2026, the Strategy Secretariat organises a series of thematic dialogues which bring together funding programmes and the thematic Coordinators of the Strategy. These meetings are the platform for the programme authorities in the region to come together and establish a shared understanding of common needs and challenges across the Baltic Sea Region. The aim is to facilitate cross-fertilisation with national programming processes and the preparation of National and Regional Partnership Plans (NRPPs), including the Interreg Plan and Chapters.

The dialogues also contribute to building synergies among programmes and with Policy Area Coordinators, and lay the groundwork for joint implementation, including coordinated or synchronised calls.

title: When telcos shut down the internet, they shut down protests for the government
content:
When the streets become too dangerous, dissent often migrates online

Originally published on Global Voices

A telecom company in Niger. Image via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0).

This post is part of Global Voices’ September 2026 Spotlight series, “Protest in Democracy.” With this Spotlight, we seek to explore the many forms of protest, the tactics states use to delegitimize and suppress them, and the complex relationship between protest and democracy. You can support this coverage by donating here.

Room to protest is narrowing across much of the African continent, as governments lean on arrests, curfews, and internet blackouts to blunt dissent. When the streets become too dangerous, dissent often migrates online — which is exactly where telecommunications companies enter the picture, deciding, often under government pressure, whether a phone call gets through or a message reaches its recipient. This piece looks at how that power has been used, and at the accountability telcos have too often avoided.

title: What The New York Times learned putting an AI agent on the Epstein files
content:
When a team at The New York Times built an AI agent to dig through the Epstein files, reporters kept using it to find out what hadn't been reported yet. They did that so often that the team added a standing section on existing coverage to the agent's reports.

Between its launch in February and mid-June, more than 100 journalists asked the Epstein Files Engine 4,500 questions. Its reports contributed to at least 20 published stories. The team describes what it learned in a paper to be presented Oct. 3 at the Computation + Journalism Symposium. Members of the team also talked about the project at our AI x Investigative Journalism Forum at The Times on Sept. 25.

The Justice Department's Jan. 30 release ran to roughly 3 million pages of PDFs, 1.1 million emails, 200,000 images and more than 1,000 audio and video clips, by The Times' count. A prototype of the Engine took its first question two days later. For a week, The Times' AI Initiatives team ran reporters' questions through it by hand and pasted the answers into a Google Doc, which has since hit its 1 million-character limit. Reporters got direct access Feb. 9.

title: What We Lose When We Use AI
content:
By Reihshan Deen*

COLOMBO, Sri Lanka | 28 September 2026 (IDN) — In Plato’s Phaedrus, Socrates recounts a discussion between two Egyptian gods: Theuth, said to have invented writing, and Thamus. Thamus disapproves of Theuth’s invention, stating that it “…will create forgetfulness in the learners’ souls, because they will not use their memories; they will trust to the external written characters and not remember of themselves.

“[Writing] is an aid not to memory, but to reminiscence, and you give your disciples not truth, but only the semblance of truth; they will be hearers of many things and will have learned nothing; they will appear to be omniscient and will generally know nothing; they will be tiresome company, having the show of wisdom without the reality”.

title: Kirjastoista tuli digitaalisen hoivan keskuksia – “Ihmiset pyytävät enemmän…”
content:
Digitaalinen hoiva on uusi termi, jolla kuvataan kirjastojen tekemää työtä. Sillä tarkoitetaan tilanteita, joissa työntekijät auttavat ihmisiä digitaalisten palveluiden käytössä. Kyse ei ole pelkästä teknisestä neuvonnasta, vaan kirjastojen ammattilaiset myös kuuntelevat, tukevat ja auttavat ihmisiä, joilla on vaikeuksia käyttää verkkopalveluja. Työ muistuttaa joiltakin osin hoivatyötä.

”Kyse on emotionaalisesta puolesta ja ihmisistä huolehtimisesta. Ihmiset pyytävät enemmän kuin mitä kirjastossa voisi oikeastaan ajatella pyydettävän”, erikoistutkija Seppo Poutanen Turun yliopistosta kuvailee.

Poutanen on tutkinut digihoivaa kollegoidensa kanssa Turun yliopiston Työtieteiden keskuksessa. Aineisto kerättiin kirjastojen työntekijöille suunnatulla verkkokyselyllä.

Ilmiö vaikuttaa hänen mukaansa yleiseltä. Kirjastoissa apua tarjotaan esimerkiksi verkkopankkiasiointiin, Kelan sähköisiin palveluihin sekä Verohallinnon ja OmaKannan palveluihin liittyvissä ongelmissa.

Asiakas saattaa hävetä osaamattomuuttaan digiasioissa tai viivytellä hänelle tärkeiden asioiden hoitamista, jolloin kirjastotyöntekijän on myös osattava rauhoittaa tilannetta. Tämä tekee työstä emotionaalisesti vaativaa.

title: French Prosecutors Seek Prison Time for Ex-Minister Dati in Renault-Nissan Case
content:
France's former Minister of Justice and Minister of Culture, Rachida Dati, faces a requested four-year sentence for allegations of corruption and influence peddling stemming from her alleged lobbying work for the Renault-Nissan carmaking group between 2009 and 2013, OCCRP media partner Le Monde reports.

Almost a week after the opening of her trial in Paris, French prosecutors on Monday requested a four-year prison sentence for Dati, who currently serves as the mayor of a Paris arrondissement, with two years suspended and two years of house arrest. Prosecutors accuse Dati of receiving 900,000 euros (over $1 million) for providing consulting services to a Dutch subsidiary of Renault-Nissan without actually performing any work, all while serving as a Member of the European Parliament and working as an attorney.

Prosecutors also sought a four-year jail term for co-defendant Carlos Ghosn, the former CEO of Renault-Nissan who is being tried in absentia over charges including abuse of corporate assets, breach of trust, corruption, and active trading in influence.

title: Read the CIA’s Manual of Trickery and Deception, Written by a Professional Stage Magician
content: The idea of a youngster vacillating between whether to become a magician or join the Central Intelligence Agency may sound implausible, but those two working environments have deeper commonalities than it would seem. So, in any case, believes John McLaughlin, whose more than 30 years at the CIA included periods as its deputy director and acting director. He also describes himself as a lifelong amateur magician, an avocation that owes much to his boyhood discovery of Quicker Than the Eye, a magic manual from 1932 by one John Mulholland. Around the same time the young McLaughlin came across that book in the library, Mulholland was writing the more specialized guidebooks Some Operational Applications of the Art of Deception and Recognition Signals — though nobody without a serious security clearance would have known it.

title: Päätoimittajalta: Tutkittu tieto politiikasta kuuluu kaikille
content:
Politiikasta, jopa politiikan teoriasta, on mahdollista kirjoittaa selkeästi. Selkeät tekstit ovat välttämättömiä, kun väestön lukutaito heikentyy.

Länsimaisessa kulttuurissa on pohdittu yli 2000 vuoden ajan vallankäytön ja ihmisten yhteiselämän kysymyksiä, ja työ jatkuu edelleen. Teoreettista työtä tarvitaan käsitteiden luomiseksi ja maailman hahmottamiseksi paremmin, kuten italialaisfilosofi Roberto Esposito on korostanut useissa teoksissaan.

Esposito tuo esiin, miten filosofia on jatkuvasti ajankohtaista – Eurooppa on dramaattisimmissa historian vaiheissaan kääntynyt filosofian puoleen. Nykyistäkin tilannetta voi luonnehtia dramaattiseksi.

Hyviä viimeaikaisia esimerkkejä selkeistä politiikan teoriaa käsittelevistä teksteistä Politiikasta-lehdessä ovat vaikkapa Suvi Kuokkasen artikkeli ”Hybris, kansa ja yhteiskuntarauhan järkkyminen antiikin Kreikassa” tai Aada Petterssonin ”Valtion sisäiset konfliktit: Terve vai sairas valtiomuoto?”.

title: The Untold Origins of Trump’s Plan to Sharply Restrict Mail-In Voting
content:
Earlier this month, the Supreme Court blocked an executive order from President Donald Trump restricting voting by mail in ways that could have thrown the upcoming midterms into chaos. But the White House originally had far more disruptive plans, ProPublica has learned. 

According to several people knowledgeable about the discussions, the administration initially floated an idea that would have virtually shut down mail voting: requiring all ballots to be delivered exclusively through certified mail. The proposal — which would have required voters to be home and sign for delivery of their ballots — was ultimately abandoned, after vehement Postal Service objections that it would have been impossible to execute. 

Even after the idea fizzled, Postal Service officials were cut out of crucial conversations as the Trump administration moved forward with what became the final executive order, two people familiar with the matter said. Issued in March, its contents came as a shock even to the Postal Service’s lawyers.

    Samalla se voi kuitenkin johtaa keskustelua harhaan. Tärkein kysymys ei ole hävittääkö tekoäly ihmiskunnan, vaan säilyykö ihmisen kyky ymmärtää ja hallita yhä kehittyneempiä järjestelmiä.

title: Hanna Bergholmi õudusfilm ÖÖLAPS kinolevis
content:
Oktoobri alguses jõuab Eesti kinodesse Hanna Bergholmi lavastatud õudusfilm ÖÖLAPS (Yön lapsi), Soome 2026. Bergholmi uus film esilinastus tänavuse Berliini filmifestivali võistlusprogrammis ja pärjati eelmisel nädalal Põhjamaade filmiauhinnaga Freya kui parim film.

Linaloo peaosades mängivad suurepärased näitlejad Seidi Haarla („Kupee nr 6“) ja Rupert Grint („Harry Potter“).

Saga (Seidi Haarla) ja John (Rupert Grint) kolivad keset Soome metsi asuvasse maamajja, et pakkuda oma tulevasele lapsele loodusküllast ja rahulikku kasvukeskkonda. Peagi sünnibki kauaoodatud poeg, kuid uus elu ei kujune sugugi selliseks nagu paar oli ette kujutanud. Vastsündinuga toimetulekust saab mõlemale suur katsumus ning üha enam tundub, et ainult ema tajub, mis lapsega tegelikult toimub.

Filmis on olulisel kohal loodus, mis loob omalaadse pingelise atmosfääri ning viited viivad Soome folkloori. HÕFF, kus kevadel toimus Eesti festivali esilinastus, kirjeldab seda kui Soome folk-horror’i uut tulemist. Haapsalus viibis kohal ka filmi “Öölaps” kaas-stsenarist Ilja Rautsi.

title: Plan Calcul, Alice Recoque et le Mitra 15
content:
Du Mitra 15 au Mimitra 15

Pour une histoire la fabrique du numérique

Aujourd’hui, la diffusion du numérique dans tous les domaines de la société donne de nouvelles responsabilités à la recherche publique, en faisant mieux appréhender par tous les citoyens les grands thèmes du numérique et son impact, ainsi que pour susciter des vocations parmi les jeunes.

La culture numérique est au cœur de la dynamique d’Inria, institut national de recherche en sciences et technologies du numérique.

Ressusciter les ordinosaures — Le projet JuraSTIC (IRISA) fédère des scientifiques autour des enjeux de préservation du passé, pour mieux penser l’avenir, en mobilisant la recherche, l’ingénierie et l’enseignement supérieur. Il s’attache à restaurer des machines emblématiques, à documenter leurs usages et leurs contenus et à explorer de nouvelles pistes de recherche : rétroingénierie, reproductibilité, lutte contre l’obsolescence…

Ouvrir la boite noire de l’informatique, de son histoire et de ses outils, permet de mieux comprendre les futurs possibles du numérique.

title: Sovereign Tech Resilience relaunches with four new services
content:
Sovereign Tech Resilience adds four new services, memory safety transition, post-quantum readiness, supply chain security, and Cyber Resilience Act compliance, and expands two existing services. Applications are open.

The Sovereign Tech Resilience program has been running since 2023, after the German Bundestag allocated funds in the federal budget for a bug bounty program. The program's approach combines hands-on engineering, audits, and bug-and-fix bounties, delivered together with industry partners at no cost to participating free and open source software (FOSS) projects. It helps critical open source projects build better capacity to avoid, absorb, and handle security issues over time.

title: Florida seeks injunction to hamper OpenAI development
content:
TALLAHASSEE, Florida — Republican state Attorney General James Uthmeier intensified his fight with OpenAI and its founder Sam Altman on Monday by asking a Florida court to stop the tech giant from further developing its artificial intelligence technology while their legal battle plays out.

In his latest push to put guardrails around AI, Uthmeier is attempting to leverage the recent panic about the technology’s unchecked growth in Washington and beyond as proof that ChatGPT and other AI models are dangerous products. Uthmeier is seeking an injunction against OpenAI that would prevent the company from advancing new AI models without third-party approved protections, and cut off minors from using its popular chatbot.

“If Sam Altman meant what he said about slowing down, he can join our ask to the court,” Uthmeier said Monday in a video posted to social media. “If he will not, we ask the court to do what OpenAI will not do for itself — protect Florida families.”

Officials with OpenAI did not immediately respond with a request for comment about the development in Florida’s lawsuit.

title: Water is precious – this Swedish city separates different waste sources to reuse more of it
content:
Extreme temperatures, droughts and wildfires lead to water scarcity and the search for alternative sources of water to secure supplies. With increasing pressures from climate change, Europe’s water stress – not having enough clean freshwater to meet demands – is becoming more intense and more frequent.

But one valuable water source is often overlooked: wastewater.

While some Middle Eastern countries like Qatar reuse approximately 90% of their wastewater, Europe’s reuse of wastewater is often very low. Just 0.6% of wastewater gets recycled in Sweden, yet 15 of 21 counties already face a high risk of water scarcity.

In one of those 15 counties, a new district in the city of Helsingborg in southern Sweden is successfully recycling wastewater. In Oceanhamnen, wastewater is collected through three separate pipelines: one for toilet wastewater (blackwater), one for greywater (wastewater from bathtubs and showers, sinks, laundry and dishwashers), and a third pipeline which takes food waste from the kitchen sink directly into biogas production.

title: A bestselling novel was pulled from a French literary prize after AI accusations – what next?
content:
The French literary world has been rocked by an AI scandal, unfolding in waves. Haitian–Canadian author Thélyson Orélien had his novel removed from the shortlist of the Prix Goncourt, France’s most prestigious literary prize, last Friday – soon after an anonymous account on X claimed it was written “almost entirely by artificial intelligence”.

It Was Either That or Die (C'était ça ou mourir), about a Haitian’s perilous journey towards Canada through Brazil, Mexico and the United States, has topped the French bestseller list and sold about 35,000 copies. It won another French prize, the Fnac novel prize, last Monday and has had rave reviews.

Orélien, aged 38, emigrated to Canada in 2010, following the devastating earthquake in Haiti that flattened his home. He denies using AI to write his work.

Pangram, which was used to raise the allegations, has been called the “gold standard” of AI detectors. The Goncourt Academy, which oversees the Prix Goncourt, withdrew the book from its shortlist due to the “consistent findings of analyses by credible researchers and journalists” suggesting the book was, “in all likelihood, largely the product of artificial intelligence”.

title: Founding Documents in Context: AI-Powered and Grounded Cultural Heritage
content:
This post describes a recent collaboration between the Digital Strategy Directorate in the Library’s Office of the Chief Information Officer and the Arizona State University Cloud Innovation Center. The partnership explored necessary steps to create an effective AI-powered tool using context engineering that allows for the exploration of United States Revolutionary Era history with the Library’s collections as grounding data.

As opportunities to discover uncharted patterns in our nation’s history expand with artificial intelligence-powered research tools, technical approaches that promote authenticity and context are needed more than ever.

Recently, the Library’s Digital Strategy Directorate teamed up with Arizona State University Cloud Innovation Center students to investigate how technical innovation can be grounded in truth using founding era documents.

title: Suomalaisen sivistyksen juurille: Kansallisarkisto ja Jyväskylän yliopisto digitoivat Suomen ensimmäisen opettajaseminaarin ainutlaatuiset arkistot
content:
Hankkeessa on digitoitu merkittävä osa Jyväskylän seminaarin arkistoaineistoista. Jyväskylän tyttölyseon ja Jyväskylän lyseon arkistot täydentävät kokonaisuutta. Hanketta ovat rahoittaneet Jyväskylän yliopistosäätiö, Jyväskylän yliopisto sekä Jyväskylän yliopiston historian ja etnologian laitos.

Nyt digitaalisesti saatavilla olevat aineistot sisältävät muun muassa opetusohjelmia, vuosikertomuksia, oppilasmatrikkeleita, opetusaineistoja sekä oppilaiden tuotoksia, käsitöitä ja piirustuksia. Ne kertovat, miten ensimmäisiä suomenkielisiä opettajia koulutettiin, millaista koulun arki oli ja millaisille ihanteille koulutusjärjestelmä rakentui. Aineistot tarjoavat poikkeuksellisen kokonaisuuden suomalaisen koulutuksen, sivistyksen ja yhteiskunnan tutkimukselle.

Vuonna 1863 perustettu Jyväskylän seminaari oli Suomen ensimmäinen kansakoulunopettajaseminaari. Se vaikutti ratkaisevasti suomalaisen opettajankoulutuksen, kansakoulun ja suomenkielisen sivistyksen rakentumiseen. Seminaarista valmistui noin 4 500 opettajaa, jotka veivät osaamisensa eri puolille Suomea ja olivat rakentamassa yhdenvertaista kansansivistystä.

Jyväskylän seminaarilla oli merkittävä rooli myös naisten koulutuksen ja yhteiskunnallisen toimijuuden vahvistamisessa. Seminaarin kasvatteihin kuuluivat muun muassa kirjailijat Minna Canth ja Anni Swan sekä koulutus- ja tasa-arvovaikuttajat Lucina Hagman ja Emma Irene Åström.

Digitointi parantaa aineistojen saavutettavuutta ja mahdollistaa entistä laajemman hyödyntämisen tutkimuksessa ja opetuksessa sekä kaikkien historiasta kiinnostuneiden keskuudessa. Digitoituihin aineistoihin voi tutustua verkossa Kansallisarkiston Astia-palvelussa. Voit katsoa esimerkiksi Minna Canthin (tuolloin Johnson) hakemuksen Jyväskylän seminaariin. Tietyt alle 100-vuotiaat aineistot ovat näyttörajoitettuja.

Huom. Kansallisarkisto luopuu Jyväskylän toimipaikastaan 1.1.2027 lukien. Tutkijasalipalvelu päättyy jo 29.9.2026. Lue lisää tiedotteesta.

title: Superman, Captain America, Kermit the Frog and The Declaration of Independence
content:
This is a guest post by Nyla Adams, a recent intern in the Office of Communications.

The Declaration of Independence didn’t just make American pop culture possible — often, it’s been the star of the show.

In “National Treasure,” the 2004 popcorn thriller, Nicolas Cage must somehow steal the Declaration from the National Archives (it has a secret map on the back) to keep it from getting … really stolen. It’s complicated.

Or in “Hamilton,” Lin-Manuel Miranda’s Pulitzer Prize-winning 2015 musical (still on Broadway!), Angelica Schuyler and Thomas Jefferson each rap famous lines from Jefferson’s work on the Declaration.

In the Bicentennial mania of 1976, comic-book readers watched both Superman and Captain American travel back in time to save the Declaration’s origin story.

And on television and cable, the Declaration has popped up (mostly being quoted) in everything from “Star Trek” to “The Andy Griffith Show” to the HBO miniseries “John Adams” to … you get the idea.

title: Trump’s deportations to third countries violate human rights, UN experts warn
content:
Sending migrants to countries they do not come from can have deadly consequences and must be halted, says report

The deportation of thousands of migrants from the US to third countries has set off a “cascade of human rights violations” that could have “deadly” consequences, two dozen UN human rights experts have warned.

Since Donald Trump returned to power in 2025, the US government has been offering millions of dollars to foreign governments to take in migrants, including refugees and asylum seekers, with no ties to their countries. Deals have been struck with 35 nations, nearly a third of them in Africa.

title: Näytelmä kertoo holokaustin pysyvyydestä
content:
Eero Karisto

Suomen Kansallisteatterin Lopetus perustuu Nobel-palkitun unkarinjuutalaisen kirjailijan Imre Kertészin (1929–2016) samannimiseen romaaniin vuodelta 2003. Näytelmäsovituksessa on paljon muutakin, kuten elementtejä, jotka sivuavat nykypäivää. Teos on rakenteeltaan vaikea: on tarina, näytelmä näytelmästä, ja tavallaan irralliset keskustelut, jotka sijoittuvat eri aikoihin.

Juutalaisten vainot eivät alkaneet holokaustista eivätkä päättyneet siihen. Holokausti vaikuttaa edelleen ihmisissä ja valtioiden politiikassa. Kuulemme myös, tosin ohimennen, rinnastuksen Gazan tapahtumien ja holokaustin välillä ja kysymyksen, onko uhrista tullut pyöveli.

Epäilemättä ulkopuolisen on vaikea ymmärtää, mitä kaikkea holokausti merkitsee niille, joita se on koskenut ja koskee, joko suoraan tai välillisesti. Tätä kynnystä kuvaa näytelmässä kohtaus, jossa ei-juutalainen mies ja hänen juutalainen vaimonsa keskustelevat vaimon entisen, juutalaisen miehen suhteesta. Se entinen mies on itsemurhan tehnyt kirjailija B, jonka kadonnut romaanikäsikirjoitus on keskeisessä osassa näytelmässä.

title: Conference on Open Science for Innovation | UNESCO
content:
"UNESCO will convene the Open Science for Innovation Conference at its Headquarters in Paris on 12 November 2026, to examine how open science partnerships can support the implementation of the UNESCO Recommendation on Open Science...

The Conference explores four cross-cutting questions:


	Designing openness into partnerships  How can open science, open science partnerships and intellectual property be combined with intention and sequenced across the research to application pathway, so that they reinforce rather than undermine one another?
	Evidence from UNESCO priority areas What do selected partnerships in fields such as water and biodiversity research show about governance, funding and accountability, and about measurable progress in their respective fields?
	Openness and research security How can concerns for the security and integrity of research and data can be addressed without narrowing who is able to take part in science
	Policy levers in government hands How can governments use funding, procurement and data policy to encourage open science and open science partnerships?"

title: Mindtrek jatkaa keskustelua digitaalisesta suvereniteetista
content:
eOppimiskeskuksen jäsen COSS ry järjestää Mindtrek-konferenssin Tampereella lokakuussa. Myös eOppimiskeskuksen toimistolta suunnataan tapahtumaan seuraamaan, mitä näkökulmia tapahtuma tuo syksyn mittaan virinneisiin keskusteluihin digitaalisesta suvereniteetista. Mindtrekin tämänvuotinen teema OpenTech: Building Europe’s Digital Sovereignty on erityisen ajankohtainen myös yhdistyksen toimintakentällä.

Digitaalinen suvereniteetti oli yksi syyskuussa järjestetyn Digikillan 10-vuotisjuhlaseminaarin työpajateemoista. Kuntien ja koulutuksen näkökulmasta aiheeseen liittyy käytännönläheisiä kysymyksiä: kuinka riippuvaisia olemme yksittäisistä teknologiatoimittajista, millaisia vaihtoehtoja avoin lähdekoodi tarjoaa ja missä määrin organisaatioilla on mahdollisuus vaikuttaa omiin digitaalisiin ympäristöihinsä?

Aihepiiriä sivuttiin myös yhdistyksen ja Digikilta-verkoston lausunnossa opetuksen järjestämisestä häiriötilanteissa. Lausunnossa nostimme esiin sähkökatkojen, kyberhyökkäysten ja tietoliikennekatkosten kaltaiset häiriöt sekä tarpeen varautua kriittisten digitaalisten palvelujen toimimattomuuteen.

title: From volunteer to town councillor, with the Council Climate Action Scorecards
content:
Kiran Crawford volunteered for the Council Climate Action Scorecards — and now he’s a town councillor, using everything the Scorecards taught him about local authorities’ powers to take climate action.

Kiran was elected as a Green councillor for Royal Leamington Spa Town council in July 2026. Prior to that, as a longtime volunteer with Climate Emergency UK, he helped make the Scorecards a reality.

“I originally volunteered for the first iteration of the Scorecards back in 2021, after hearing about them from a friend who had also signed up as a volunteer.

“Having been involved in some climate campaigning before, I was looking for more ways to support good policy. The Scorecards sounded like a great way to find out how good councils’ plans were, and I thought they could be really helpful tool in campaigning for action, so I signed up to help with the assessments.

“I found the process really interesting, and learnt a lot about what powers councils have around climate. Given how useful I could see the Scorecards would be, I then volunteered as a media amplifier to help get the launch out to the press, so that they could reach as many people as possible.

title: "Britain's Gaza Secrets Exposed": How U.K. Downplayed Israeli Crimes to Keep Selling Weapons
content:
A new documentary titled Britain’s Gaza Secrets Exposed reveals new details about the U.K. government’s internal response to alleged Israeli war crimes in Gaza. Presented by journalist Ramita Navai and produced by Ben De Pear for Channel 4’s investigative program Dispatches, the documentary examines government records, some newly publicized, to show how the United Kingdom ignored or concealed mounting evidence of Israel’s genocidal actions in Gaza after the October 7 attacks.

“We were looking at how our country, which prides itself on having an ethical foreign policy and as being one of the supporting members of the United Nations on human rights, was able to keep selling arms,” says De Pear. “And basically, what we found was a doctored process … It’s quite extraordinary the level of duplicity that was going on in order for us to keep selling Israel arms.” Ben De Pear also produced the 2025 BAFTA-winning documentary Gaza: Doctors Under Attack, which the British Broadcasting Corporation, or BBC, initially commissioned but later refused to air. Gaza: Doctors Under Attack was broadcast instead by Channel 4.

title: Young Planners Work Towards Spatial Planning Challenges in the Baltic Sea Region: Insights from VASAB Young Planners’ Summer School 2026
content:
From 23 to 29 August 30 young professionals and students from across the Baltic Sea Region and Ukraine came together in Gdańsk, Poland, for a week of learning, exchange and collaboration, to explore emerging spatial planning challenges, share ideas and shape solutions for the future of our region.

Participants were allocated in 6 groups and developed ideas addressing four spatial planning challenges:

  • Preparedness and resilience
  • Climate change adaptation and mitigation, including green energy investment
  • Connections between people and places
  • Effective use of space, incl. no net land take and multiuse concepts

    • Here you can find all groups’ final presentations, explaining each group’s work and results.

    Among the six outstanding final presentations, the Summer School jury selected the group that made the strongest overall impression with their presentation, “Containing Resilience: A Modern Counterpart to a Historic Icon.” 

    The winning team – from left Hubert Wulbach, Efia Faschina, Ugnė Bačinskaitė, Wiktoria Jędrusik, Polina Dovzhenko, and their mentor Tīna Šipkēvica, Spatial Planning Expert at the VASAB Secretariat

title: Bye-bye, Birdie: The Calypso King of the World dies at 91
content:
Dedicating his life to calypso shaped him into a master of the genre and consummate Caribbean man

Originally published on Global Voices

Slinger Francisco, the Mighty Sparrow, Calypso King of the World. Photo by Maria Nunes, used with permission.

Around 4:00 p.m. Trinidad and Tobago time on Sunday, September 27, the announcement that calypso legend The Mighty Sparrow had prognosticated in song for decades, finally came. In a social media post, his daughter Karen shared that the undisputed Calypso King of the World (real name Slinger Francisco) died peacefully in New York after a brief illness, at the age of 91.

“He was an institution in the entertainment industry,” she continued, “well admired for his skill and finesse as a singer, songwriter and mentor; beloved by many. He was also a husband, father, grandfather, great-grandfather, life partner and friend.”

title: Wife, Daughter of Suspected Ecuador Gang Boss Arrested in Colombia
content:
Colombian authorities arrested two Ecuadorian women suspected of helping manage the finances of a major transnational criminal organization, Ecuadorian police said Sunday. The women were detained in Sabana de Torres during a joint operation involving police from both nations, Colombia’s GAULA anti-kidnapping unit and the FBI. Ecuadorian authorities described both women as high-value targets and said they are believed to be the wife and daughter of the alleged crime boss José Adolfo Macías Villamar, known as “Fito.”

Macías formerly led Los Choneros, an Ecuador-based criminal organization involved in cocaine trafficking, firearms trafficking and violent crime. He was recaptured in Ecuador in June 2025 and extradited to the United States the following month, where he faces federal drug and firearms charges. Ecuadorian prosecutors have separately investigated alleged money laundering involving his family circle, saying suspicious transactions worth more than $2 million entered the country’s financial system between 2016 and 2023.

title: The Little Albert Experiment: The Perverse 1920 Study That Made a Baby Afraid of Santa Claus & Bunnies
content:
The field of psychology is very different than it used to be. Nowadays, the American Psychological Association has a code of conduct for experiments that ensures a subject’s confidentiality, consent,and general mental well-being. In the old days, it wasn’t the case.

Back then, you could, for instance, con subjects into thinking that they were electrocuting a man to death, as they did in the infamous 1961 Milgram experiment, which left people traumatized and humbled in the knowledge that deep down they are little more than weak-willed puppets in the face of authority. You could also try to turn a group of unsuspecting orphans into stutterers by methodically undermining their self-esteem as the folks who ran the aptly named Monster Study of 1939 tried to do. But, if you really want to get into the swamp of moral dubiousness, look no further than the Little Albert experiments, which traumatized a baby into hating dogs, Santa Claus, and all things fuzzy.

title: Arizona Lawmaker Proposes More Federal Support for English Fluency Services
content:
An Arizona congresswoman has proposed three bills that would fund literacy classes, dual language programs and training for teachers of students learning English in the state, hoping to remedy gaps highlighted by Arizona Luminaria and ProPublica.

Rep. Adelita Grijalva, a Democrat, filed the bills Sept. 16, the same day Arizona Luminaria and ProPublica reported that the state had lowered the score students need to pass its English proficiency test. Experts warned the change will push thousands of students out of language services before they know English well enough to succeed in school. Superintendent of Public Instruction Tom Horne, a Republican longtime defender of Arizona’s English-only policies, approved the change.

title: Andy Burnham to go ‘further and faster’ than Keir Starmer on Brexit reset
content:
LIVERPOOL, England — Andy Burnham’s government will go “further and faster” in rebuilding links with the European Union, his EU relations minister has said.

Hamish Falconer told delegates at the party’s conference in Liverpool on Monday that they would “hear a bit from the prime minister tomorrow” on the issue of the EU.

Falconer said he wanted to conclude the round of talks begun by Keir Starmer on an agri-food deal, emissions trading and youth visas at a summit this year — before agreeing a new “package” with the EU.

“The prime minister is obviously ambitious. We are focused on the summit now. We are keen to go further and faster on our relationship with Europe, and I think we are clearly talking about pretty big numbers in terms of the overall addition to GDP,” he said.

“But we’ll have to get into the precise details of what we think a package can deliver once we’ve concluded negotiations on the summit and once we’ve set out a way ahead.”

title: Greater job security can make inventors less creative
content:
When Apple recently presented its (rather pricey) new folding phone, one of the questions hovering over the launch – and in particular its new CEO, John Ternus – was whether the technology giant can recover its famously innovative magic touch.

Apple remains extraordinarily profitable, but the company that revolutionised consumer electronics in the 2000s has been dogged by concerns over its dependency on a single, decades-old product – the iPhone – and its associated services. There is intense speculation around whether Ternus will reinvigorate the culture of radical innovation that drove Apple’s growth, as well as the development of the smartphone itself.

But concerns around innovation are not confined to one tech company. Over the last few months, figures like Gordon Brown and Ursula von der Leyen have underscored its vital economic importance, as well as its glaring absence from European industry in particular.

title: Till den finländska bildningens rötter: Riksarkivet och Jyväskylä universitet digitaliserar de unika arkiven för Finlands första lärarseminarium
content:
En betydande del av arkivmaterialet från Jyväskylä seminarium har digitaliserats i projektet. Arkiv från Jyväskylä flicklyceum och Jyväskylä lyceum kompletterar helheten. Projektet har finansierats av Jyväskylä universitetsstiftelse, Jyväskylä universitet samt institutionen för historia och etnologi vid Jyväskylä universitet.

De material som nu är digitalt tillgängliga innefattar bland annat undervisningsprogram, årsberättelser, elevmatriklar, undervisningsmaterial samt elevernas arbeten, handarbeten och teckningar. De vittnar om hur de första finskspråkiga lärarna utbildades, hurudan skolans vardag var och vilka ideal utbildningssystemet byggde på. Materialen erbjuder en exceptionell helhet för forskning om den finländska utbildningen, bildningen och samhället.

Jyväskylä seminarium, som grundades år 1863, var Finlands första folkskollärarseminarium. Det hade en avgörande roll för utvecklingen av den finländska lärarutbildningen, folkskolan och den finskspråkiga bildningen. Seminariet utexaminerade cirka 4 500 lärare, som sedan tog med sig sin kompetens till olika delar av Finland och bidrog till att bygga upp en jämlik folkbildning.

Seminariet i Jyväskylä hade också en betydande roll då det gäller stärkandet av utbildningen och det samhälleliga aktörskapet för kvinnor. Seminariets alumner inkluderade bland andra författarna Minna Canth och Anni Swan samt utbildnings- och jämställdhetspionjärerna Lucina Hagman och Emma Irene Åström.

Digitaliseringen förbättrar tillgången till materialen och möjliggör en allt bredare användning av dem inom forskning och undervisning samt bland alla som är intresserade av historia. Det går att ta del av de digitaliserade materialen på webben i Riksarkivets Astia-tjänst. Du kan till exempel ta del av Minna Canths (då Johnson) ansökan till Jyväskylä seminarium. Vissa under 100 år gamla material är visningsbegränsade.

title: Ostovoiman kasvu ei ulotu pienituloisimpiin – kuilu rikkaisiin kasvaa historiallisella tavalla
content:
Kotitalouksien ostovoiman ennakoitu elpyminen jakautuu Suomessa hyvin epätasaisesti Laboren analyysin mukaan. Tänä vuonna kaikkein alimman tulokymmenyksen ostovoima heikkenee 3,5 prosenttia, kun samaan aikaan se ylimmässä kymmenyksessä kasvaa 10,8 prosenttia.

Työn ja talouden tutkimus Laboren lukujen mukaan vuodesta 2025 vuoteen 2026 ostovoima heikkenee kolmessa pienituloisimmassa tulokymmenyksessä. Muissa tulokymmenyksissä ostovoima sen sijaan vahvistuu, ylimmässä peräti 10,8 prosenttia.

Pidemmällä aikavälillä ero on vielä selvempi. Vuosina 2023–2026 alimman tulokymmenyksen ostovoima heikkenee 5,4 prosenttia ja toiseksi alimman 2,2 prosenttia.

Laboren pitkän aikavälin vertailussa vuosien 1966–2026 tulokehitykseen nykyinen kehitysero on merkittävä. Erityistä on, että alimman tulokymmenyksen ostovoima laskee samaan aikaan, kun ylimmän kasvaa. Myös 1990-luvun laman jälkeisinä kasvuvuosina tuloryhmien kasvuerot olivat suuria, mutta silloin alimman tulokymmenyksen ostovoima ei laskenut.

title: Forcible Eviction of 87-Year-Old Madrid Woman Sparks Protest Encampment over Spain's Housing Crisis
content:
The eviction of 87-year-old María del Carmen Abascal Martín in Madrid, after an investment fund bought her apartment building and more than tripled her rent, has become a symbol of Spain’s rising cost of living and sparked nationwide protests against corporate greed and wealth inequality. Over 600 protesters are now camped outside Madrid’s regional government headquarters demanding new tenant protections.

“What we have is a lot of furious people, enraged people, that are demanding from the government and from the public institutions that they give us give us some sort of solution,” says Sabina Carrau, a spokesperson for the Madrid Tenants’ Union, which is supporting the “Maricarmen decree” named after Abascal, set to be debated by Spain’s government this week.

title: After five years of war, how do Ukrainian small businesses survive?
content:
Small businesses may look marginal, but for individual households they represent independence. We talk with Victoria Belim-Frolova.

Originally published on Global Voices

Kramatorsk’s Pink Coffee Shop. Photo by Victoria Belim-Frolova. Used with permission.

The war in Ukraine, with its multiple effects, has been taking its toll on various sectors, and small businesses are not immune. Yet, some businesses manage to oppose the widespread infrastructure and supply-chain problems, labor shortages, and limited access to finance — and among these, a special place belongs to women.

A UNDP-supported study found that 83 percent of small businesses were negatively affected by the war; the prevalence of women-led business has also increased since the beginning of the full-scale invasion. Many women have become entrepreneurs because of displacement, loss of household income, absence of a partner serving in the military and, last but not least, the need to combine flexible work with family care.

According to The New Voice of Ukraine, women accounted for nearly 60 percent of newly registered sole proprietors in the first quarter of 2026, compared with about 49 percent at the beginning of the conflict.

title: South Pacific: As Small Islands Battle Climate Change, Debts Should Not Be Weaponized
content:
By ANTONIA BHAGWAN*

SUVA, Fiji | 28 September 2026 (IDN|Wansolwara) — The South Pacific region with its many vulnerable island nations may have moved beyond the worst of the COVID-19 pandemic, but its economic consequences continue to weigh on governments across the region.

Once again, countries are facing rising debt levels. In its 2026 Pacific Economic Update, the World Bank linked the current financial landscape to slower economic growth, narrowing fiscal space, climate disasters, and an uncertain global economy.

Economic growth across 11 Pacific Island countries is projected to slow to 2.8% in 2026, according to the report, as rising fuel and shipping prices pressure budgets. The report shows that repeated shocks are becoming the Pacific’s new normal. It highlights the need to move beyond short-term crisis response and invest in the foundations of long-term growth.

According to Joey Tau, Coordinator of the Pacific Network on Globalisation (PANG), the region’s current debt problem must be understood historically and structurally.

“Over the past two decades, both internal and external developments have challenged the economic structures of Pacific Island states,” Tau states.

title: Two Years After Hurricane Helene, People Are Still Allowed to Live in Harm’s Way
content:
This past weekend marked the two-year anniversary of Hurricane Helene, which claimed more than 250 lives — 108 in North Carolina — and left hundreds of thousands of people without power for days to weeks. In Asheville, the largest city in the western part of the state, the storm left residents without drinking water for 53 days.

Part of what made the storm so devastating to the region when it hit, 400 miles inland from where it made landfall, is that the Appalachian Mountains’ typically porous soils were already saturated by recent rainfall. The rainwater hit bedrock and raced down steep mountain slopes like water on a slide. It overran the banks of normally shallow creeks and rivers, carrying the earth above it. One in 4 of those who died from the storm in North Carolina did so because of mud and landslides.

title: Without water, forests lose their ability to absorb CO₂
content:
To survive during periods of drought, trees halt photosynthesis, a highly water-intensive process during which, for every molecule of CO₂ absorbed by a tree leaf, an average of around 400 water molecules are released. Entire forests then may end up emitting more CO₂ than they capture.

This is alarming given that droughts are becoming increasingly frequent and that forests play a key role in climate change mitigation policies. Although quantifying the CO₂ captured by the world’s forests remains a difficult task. It is estimated that they capture around a quarter of the CO₂ emitted by human activities.

However, when faced with extreme water shortages, forests can cease to act as carbon sinks. To understand why, we need to look at the leaves of the trees.

Tree leaves are the main point of entry for CO₂ into the forest ecosystem. They act as genuine chemical factories, capturing solar energy to convert CO₂ that is present in the air into sugar (i.e. photosynthesis). These sugars meet the plant’s energy needs. They also enable trees to grow and, in doing so, to store more CO₂ emitted by human activities.

title: Towards the Shape of Responsible Research Metrics: A Hybrid Citation-Mapping Approach to Scientific and Policy Uptake
content: Research metrics have become deeply embedded in science, despite sustained criticism of their limitations and unintended effects, especially in research assessment. Key reform documents such as the San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment, the Leiden Manifesto, and The Metric Tide established core principles for the responsible use of metrics and shaped broader debates on responsible research assessment. This research-inprogress paper maps the scientific and policy uptake of these foundational documents through a hybrid citationmapping approach, combining bibliographic data from Web of Science, Scopus, and OpenAlex with policy citation data from Overton. At this stage, the analysis focuses on the scientific corpus, examining its temporal development, geographical distribution, and citation-overlap patterns. Preliminary findings highlight the prominent position of the Leiden Manifesto, limited overlap among the three foundational documents, and broad international diffusion centred in Europe and North America, with Asia playing an increasingly important role.

title: Suomenlahden siikasaalis perustuu vahvasti yksikesäisten poikasten istutuksiin – istutusten tulevaisuuteen liittyy haasteita
content:
Suomenlahden siikasaaliit ovat nykyisin lähes kokonaan yksikesäisinä istutettujen vaellussiian poikasten varassa. Uuden tutkimuksen tulokset korostavat istutustoiminnan keskeistä merkitystä rannikon ammatti- ja vapaa-ajankalastukselle sekä tarvetta turvata laadukkaiden istukkaiden tuotanto myös tulevaisuudessa.

Suomen rannikolta pyydetty siikasaalis on ollut viime vuosina Suomenlahdella yleensä noin 90–100 tonnia vuodessa. Vaellussiian luonnollinen poikastuotanto on vähäistä, minkä vuoksi kantaa tuetaan istutuksilla. Suomenlahteen istutetaan sekä vastakuoriutuneita että yksikesäisiä, lähinnä Pohjois-Suomessa sijaitsevissa luonnonravintolammikoissa kasvatettuja poikasia.

Luonnonvarakeskuksen tutkimuksen mukaan noin 90 prosenttia koko Suomenlahden siikasaaliista perustuu yksikesäisten istukkaiden varaan. Vaellussiikaistutusten tuotto on säilynyt 2020-luvun alkupuolella suunnilleen samalla tasolla kuin 25–30 vuotta sitten. Siikaistutuksissa ei ole havaittu vastaavaa tuoton heikkenemistä kuin lohella ja meritaimenella.

Tutkijoiden mukaan nykyisen kaltaisen siiankalastuksen jatkuminen edellyttää, että yksikesäisten poikasten laajamittaisia istutuksia jatketaan myös tulevaisuudessa.

title: AI, open science, and the extraction imperative: A situated approach to the normativities of open research data | Cambridge Forum on AI: Culture and Society | Cambridge Core
content: Abstract: Open Science has long been framed as a normative project grounded in values of transparency, accessibility and collaboration. Yet in the age of generative AI, many research data practitioners, who once championed openness, are increasingly questioning how these commitments can be upheld when openness also enables undesired large-scale data extraction, decontextualization and enclosure. This paper examines how the normativities of openness are being re-negotiated, and how researchers navigate the ethical and political tensions that arise when their work is repurposed for proprietary AI systems. Drawing on in-depth qualitative interviews, I explore how situated ethical reasoning informs decisions about data sharing. Participants described new risks and dilemmas, from uncontrolled scraping and heightened re-identification threats to the reframing of FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) principles as pipelines for AI-readiness. Their accounts reveal openness as a relational and contested practice, embedded in specific institutional, infrastructural and community contexts, and continuously re-balanced between care, accountability and collaboration. title: Beyond protest: Mob violence and the struggle for institutional response in Bangladesh
content:
‘People do not have the assurance that they will get justice.’

Originally published on Global Voices

August 4, 2024, Dhaka. People celebrated in jubilation after Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina resigned and left the country. Photo by: Rafi Al Ahnaf (used with permissin.

This post is part of Global Voices’ September 2026 Spotlight series, “Protest in Democracy.” With this Spotlight, we seek to explore the many forms of protest, the tactics states use to delegitimize and suppress them, and the complex relationship between protest and democracy. You can support this coverage by donating here.

Mob violence is on the rise in Bangladesh. According to the United Nations (UN) Special Rapporteur on freedom of expression Irene Khan, unchecked impunity is contributing to the trend. Ain o Salish Kendra (ASK), a Dhaka-based legal aid and human rights organization, reported in its monthly Statistics of Human Rights Violations that at least 154 people were beaten to death in mob violence across Bangladesh between January and August 2026. ASK compiled the figure from national newspapers, online news outlets and its own documentation.

title: Syria: Reconstruction Deals Lack Critical Rights Framework
content:
(Amman) – The Syrian transitional government is signing billions of dollars in reconstruction deals without a human rights framework that would ensure that rebuilding respects, protects, and fulfills the rights of affected people, Human Rights Watch said today.

In March 2026, the transitional government unveiled a national recovery blueprint, and billions of dollars in international pledges for aid, and financing and investment commitments have followed. But the legal frameworks governing reconstruction do not require the government or developers to consult affected communities, including those still displaced, before projects are approved. The process should also require negotiating—instead of imposing—compensation terms and providing an independent mechanism for residents to challenge decisions about their homes and land.

“Syria's reconstruction is progressing slowly, but without a rights framework, it could leave many Syrians with a raw deal,” said Hiba Zayadin, senior Middle East advisor at Human Rights Watch. “The legal framework being finalized now will determine whose homes are rebuilt, whose claims are recognized, and whose voices are heard.”

title: Bill Gates says an AI ‘kill switch’ isn’t enough
content:
Bill Gates said that requiring a “kill switch” alone for artificial intelligence would not be enough to prevent people from using the technology to carry out attacks as lawmakers debate how to regulate AI’s risks.

“The kill switch is, that’s kind of a weird thing. It’s not enough to have a kill switch,” the Microsoft co-founder said in an interview that aired Sunday on NBC’s “Meet the Press.”

“We’re not yet at the point where they autonomously grab computers and, you know, can’t be shut down,” he said, adding that the public discussion “just sort of shows how nontechnical various people are.”

Gates said he was not opposed to a kill switch but argued that companies should monitor sophisticated AI models and keep records of “exactly what’s being done” to help guard against people using the systems for cyberattacks or bioterrorism.

“The United States ought to make sure this is done. China will want to do this,” he continued.

Gates’ comments come after Sen. Rand Paul (R-Ky.) blocked fellow GOP Sen. John Neely Kennedy’s attempt to quickly pass legislation that would require AI companies to build a “kill switch” into their models.

title: Democracy blindsides Silicon Valley’s power players looking to transform the world with AI
content:
‘The push against datacenters speaks to the frustration of people who don’t feel they are making the choices in their lives’

The Stanford ethicist Rob Reich was once invited to a dinner organized by a Silicon Valley mogul to discuss what a state designed to maximize science and tech powered by commercial models might look like. The gathered technologists were drawn to the idea of building a small nation-state dedicated to the endeavor, Reich recalls in “System Error: Where Big Tech Went Wrong and How We Can Reboot it”.

When Reich asked whether this state would be a democracy, he got a cool no. “Democracy is too slow, and it holds science back,” he was told. “To optimize for science, we need a beneficent technocrat in charge.”
snippet: ‘The push against datacenters speaks to the frustration of people who don’t feel they are making the choices in their lives’

title: Xenia Fedorova, or how Russian propaganda turns free thinking on itself
content:
KEY TAKEAWAYS

• On September 24, the European Union sanctioned Xenia Fedorova, the Russian former head of the French arm of Russia Today (RT) and media commentator for the Bolloré group for her role in engaging in foreign information manipulation and interference (FIMI). It follows a French expulsion order against the Russian propagandist in July 2026.

• Accused of spreading Kremlin propaganda, she counterattacks by presenting herself as the victim of “single-minded thinking” spread by mainstream media in Western countries.

• In doing so, she exploits a clever rhetorical and cognitive mechanism: rather than trying to convince us, the aim is to turn our own aspiration to critical thinking against “official” sources, to push Russian propaganda.

The European Council has decided to adopt restrictive measures against Xenia Fedorova for her role in Russia’s continued hybrid activities, and in particular for engaging in foreign information manipulation and interference (FIMI), “thereby undermining democracy and stability in the EU and its member states”.

title: The Takeaway: UN General Assembly debate Day 5
content: From artificial intelligence to migration, some of the forces reshaping the twenty-first century took centre stage at the UN General Assembly on Saturday. Leaders wrestled with a common dilemma: how to harness profound technological and social change without allowing it to deepen the divisions already separating countries and communities. This edition of The Takeaway distils key points from Day 5 of the annual high-level debate.
